label: Wrap task-specific CLAUDE.md sections in <important if="condition"> blocks so each is weighted only when its condition matches, instead of leaving flat always-on prose.
strongest_evidence: anecdotal: HumanLayer's own CLAUDE.md has ~14 such blocks in 278 lines (C0176); Dex reports 'noticeably better adherence' but 'we don't have a rigorous explanation' and gives no numbers (C1208).
sources: Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md (2026-03-17, https://www.humanlayer.dev/blog/stop-claude-from-ignoring-your-claude-md)
sample_quote: "<important if=\"you are writing or modifying tests\">" (C1208)
landing_guesses: CLAUDE.md: wrap outbox, dispatcher, bill-freeze and migration invariants in conditional blocks instead of trimming | keep Commands/Build traps conditional rather than deleted

reviews.lens: cost, risk and novelty
reviews.reopens_skipped: KS-7 trim gate (KS design: trim only after the pilot): its reason is that moving narratives out takes knowledge from sessions that never look up. That reason does not apply to wrapping, because nothing leaves the file.
reviews.measurement: On a branch, wrap the outbox, dispatcher, bill-freeze, migration and build-trap sections in <important if> blocks. Run 10 fixed probe tasks (add a migration, add an outbox kind, enable the dispatcher, edit a completion screen, and so on) with fresh Sonnet agents, 3 runs each, against the current file and the wrapped one. Count invariants respected or cited. Pass = wrapped >= current on every probe, higher on >= 3 probes, and no invariant lost.
reviews.reason: grep finds 0 such blocks in the 390-line CLAUDE.md. The edit is cheap and removes nothing, but the adherence gain is unmeasured (Dex: 'no rigorous explanation'), so test it before adopting.

reviews.lens: BENEFIT: the best honest case for what each family would buy on W1 (CLAUDE.md length) and L2 (context budget, compaction), with strict evidence scoring. Shared experiment E1 (the CLAUDE.md ablation, referenced below): 10 frozen probe tasks, each needing one CLAUDE.md invariant (next migration slot, a new outbox kind, comparing a shared secret, deploying from backend/, the eas.json DSN, the dispatcher cursor, a bill-freeze resubmit, money units, a new slice edge, droppable pings). Each task runs in one fresh Sonnet session per arm. An Opus judge, blind to the arm, scores whether the agent's plan cites and obeys the invariant. The result is also checked against the knowledge-store gating (KS-7/D11), which these families mostly cannot pre-empt.
reviews.measurement: E1 with two arms: the current CLAUDE.md, and the same text with task-specific sections wrapped in <important if> blocks, nothing deleted. Adopt the wrapped file only if it scores at least as well as the current one on all 10 probe tasks and better on at least 2.
reviews.reason: This is the only W1 lever that removes no content, so the knowledge-store gating ('a trim takes knowledge from sessions that never look up') does not apply. It needs an ablation because the only evidence is HumanLayer's unmeasured 'noticeably better'.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The harness already has the real version of this mechanism. Dex himself calls the wrapper "a poor man's skills system" (C0975). The 13 skill packages being added (.claude/skills/README.md index, wizardly-hertz-02c46a worktree) load only when their descriptions match the task, and they restate exactly the sections the reviewers want to wrap, citing CLAUDE.md by line. fastapi-alembic-safety covers migrations, 0047 and NOT VALID (22 invariant hits), plus the dispatch_cursor, staff_ledger, compare_secret and try_transition rules. offline-sync-review cites CLAUDE.md:151 (sendOrQueue/client_id) and :154 (the outbox never deletes a write), and covers the bill freeze, completionPrefill and maxDutyHours. eas-expo-release cites CLAUDE.md:81 and :84 (the Sentry traps). fixflow-repo-conventions covers deploying from backend/, migration numbering, slice boundaries, the dispatcher, the bill freeze and compare_secret. A grep shows every target section (outbox, dispatcher, bill freeze, migrations, build traps, lifecycle, location, security, staff money) is in at least one skill. Phase briefs also name the invariant per phase (SHIP-PLAN :415 outbox, :830 location, :1074 bill freeze). (2) The idea transfers badly to these particular invariants. CLAUDE.md records that they broke through paths that did not look like their topic. The bill freeze was "reopened through the automated door", when the dispatcher send skipped log_customer_message (Invariants, dispatcher section). The wrapper works by "giving the model permission to ignore" (C0975), and Dex's own rule (C1209) wants narrow conditions. A narrow condition gets these cross-cutting rules wrong, and a broad one does nothing. (3) The stated mechanism may be missing. C1164 and C1197 say the wrapper counters the system message's "may not be relevant" framing. In this session CLAUDE.md is injected as "Be sure to adhere to these instructions ... MUST follow them exactly as written", with no such framing visible. I only saw this in a subagent session; the main session is unchecked. (4) It saves zero tokens: all 390 lines stay, plus about 2 per block. That is no L2 gain and no shorter W1 file, and nothing for W2 (no observability) or W4 (no workflow). (5) Timing clash. KS design line 509 says KS-7 rewrites these same sections and counts from the pre-KS-1 file. KS-5 must beat both incumbents (D8, line 707). Editing CLAUDE.md before or during the pilot muddies that comparison. The reviewers' point that "the KS gate doesn't apply" deals with content loss, not this. (6) The evidence is anecdotal only (C1208: "no rigorous explanation"; no numbers). G1-A's E1 runs once per arm per probe, and all 10 probes match their conditions, so it cannot tell "better on at least 2" from noise or see the de-weighting failure.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Cheapest check: capture the injected CLAUDE.md context in one main desktop phase session (not a subagent) and see whether it contains "may or may not be relevant to your tasks". If it does not, the stated mechanism has nothing to counter and the skip stands. If it does and someone wants to reopen this, the ablation must run with the skills loaded as in real phases, 3 runs per arm, 10 probes that match their condition plus at least 5 that do not: the invariant applies through a path the condition does not name, e.g. wiring the WhatsApp sender, which must respect the bill freeze. Pass = wrapped >= current on every probe, the 5 off-condition probes included, and higher on at least 3 of the 10 matching probes. Run it only after KS-5 so the pilot's comparison file is not changed.
refutation.reason: The skills and phase briefs in this harness already deliver these invariants by task. The wrapper would tell the model it may ignore cross-cutting invariants that CLAUDE.md itself says broke through unrelated paths. Its evidence is anecdotal, its mechanism may be absent in this build, and it saves no tokens.

reviews.reason: A cheap rule that keeps the always-true part bare. It only matters if F001 is trialled.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The harness already holds the "always-true stays bare" half. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md KS-7 (line 648) and D11 (line 710) trim CLAUDE.md by moving out only the narratives of verified entries. They keep every rule, and "Do NOT assume" stays unchanged. The design (line 765) also names the risk this family brings back: a session that does not judge a block relevant loses it. The only new part is "one narrow trigger per conditional block", and that rule means nothing unless F001's wrapping is adopted. (2) The evidence is weak. C1198 and C1199 are asserted with no data. C1209 is anecdotal ("rules of thumb from his own use"). C0816 is asserted. (3) HumanLayer's conditional blocks stay inside the file, so wrapping removes no lines. W1 stays at 390 lines (confirmed with wc), and L2 gains nothing. The only possible gain is salience, and only E1 can show that. (4) The rule transfers to FixFlow with a risk on the opposite side. Its examples (imports, components) are style rules, where a missed trigger costs little. FixFlow's invariants are safety rules that are coupled across slices. CLAUDE.md:197 says the bill freeze is "two halves of one rule", one on the server and one on the client. The dispatcher rule is safe only because of log_customer_message and the bill freeze. The outbox's known defect is covered only by the completionPrefill refusal. One narrow trigger per invariant can cut these links. (5) The planned measurement is one-sided. E1's 10 probes name their invariant directly, so a narrow trigger matches them by construction. G1-B's fail test ("matches more than 5 of the 10 probes") catches only triggers that are too broad, never ones that miss. In the rule's favour, the current file does break it: "### Data and money" (CLAUDE.md:114) groups money units, Alembic/FK migration rules and slice boundaries under one heading. Splitting that gives a concrete, low-cost change to edit.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run this inside F001's E1 wrapped arm, not as a separate trial. Keep E1's 10 direct probes and add 3 oblique probes whose task text does not name the trigger: (a) "send an automated WhatsApp 'job ready' notice", which needs log_customer_message plus the 2-day age guard and the bill freeze; (b) "accept a signed callback from a new provider", which needs compare_secret; (c) "let a tech add a tip line to the completion form", which needs minor units, the bill-freeze resubmit rule and completionPrefill. Run each probe 3 times per arm in fresh Sonnet sessions. A blind Opus judge scores whether each plan cites and obeys the invariant. Count two things per wrapped block. Over-breadth: the trigger matches more than 5 of the 13 probes. Under-reach: an oblique probe where the plan breaks the invariant that block owns. The rule passes only if all three hold: the wrapped arm meets the E1 pass threshold on the direct probes; no block is over-broad; and the wrapped arm has no more under-reach misses than the current bare file, out of 9 oblique runs. Any extra miss fails the narrow-trigger rule, even if F001 passes.
refutation.reason: Narrowed: this survives only as the authoring rule for F001's wrapped arm, and only if E1 adds oblique probes that test for missed triggers. The "keep always-true content bare" half is already the harness's position under KS-7/D11 ("Do NOT assume" unchanged, every rule kept). Wrapping does not shorten the 390-line file. The evidence is asserted, with no data. FixFlow's invariants are coupled across slices, so a too-narrow trigger, not a too-broad one, is the real risk.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The harness already contains this study. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md line 185 (M-02, ref [32], "Gloaguen et al.: repository context files raise cost > 20% without general success gains"), line 209 (X-05 F12: the AGENTS.md study "matches the owner's no-gain record", so the store must be pull-only), line 440 (§7.1: context files were "useful only for non-standard practices") and line 538 all cite it. It already produced the "never always-loaded, pull-only" rule. (2) The study's own finding contradicts the landing guess. The arXiv abstract (2602.11988) says repository overviews do not help but context files ARE useful for specifying non-standard practices. CLAUDE.md's stack table, with its "Not" column, exists because "agents (and humans) kept assuming a generic template — WatermelonDB, Supabase-native, GoTrue". That is exactly the non-standard content the study found useful. (3) The CLAUDE.md trim is already planned in a form that matches the study better. KS design line 710 (D11/KS-7) trims only the narratives of verified entries and keeps every rule, with "Do NOT assume" untouched. Line 765 records the risk of taking knowledge away from sessions that never do a lookup. (4) 'Where things live' is not purely an overview. Its Staff money and Scheduler subsections carry invariants: the ledger is append-only with an UNSIGNED amount and a CHECK, voided rows are filtered only in ledger_balances, advance policy ships OFF, and enable_dispatcher defaults OFF. G1-A's arm drops them wholesale. (5) G1-A's measurement cannot detect that loss. None of E1's 10 probes exercises staff money, and with one session per arm per task (10 binary cells) a few-percent effect like the study's cannot be resolved. (6) Transfer is weak both ways. The study measures SWE-bench-style issue-resolution success. It does not measure adherence to incident-paid traps such as deploying from backend/ or the empty-DSN eas.json, which are invisible to tests. Its "LLM-generated" arm is an init-style auto-generated file, not an incident-curated one. The card's "138 agent files" is Kyle's secondhand framing; the abstract does not mention it.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: No trial is needed. One cheap check covers the only plausible remainder (moving rule-free overview lines to docs/CODE-MAP.md): count the lines in 'Where things live' that state no rule. If there are fewer than about 30 of 390, the W1 gain is negligible and nothing should be done outside D11/KS-7.
refutation.reason: The study is already in the KS evidence base and shaped its pull-only rule. Read correctly, it supports keeping the stack table and invariants (non-standard practices help). The only trim it licenses, rule-free overview lines, is a handful of lines that D11/KS-7 already covers better, and G1-A's E1 arm is too small to measure that cut and drops staff-money invariants that no E1 probe tests.

refutation.counter_evidence:
(1) Evidence: all five cards are asserted or anecdotal. C0282 credits the "hobbling" idea to Tariq with no data. C0636 is a HumanLayer anecdote with no numbers. C0637 is an illustration. C0638 comes from a mock-up. C0286 is Aaron's judging criteria. Under the owner's rules none of this counts as evidence.

(2) The family's target is not in this file. Its examples are generic procedural instructions ("run the tests after every change", a GitHub CLI skill, an agent-browser skill). A grep of CLAUDE.md (390 lines) finds no such line. Every section is repo-specific: incident lessons, invariants, the stack and its Not column. By C0638's own taxonomy that is the informational class that "carries across model generations", which the family says to keep. So the cut it would make among the invariants is roughly zero.

(3) The "obvious from the code" test fails in this repository. CLAUDE.md lines 1-12 say the file exists because agents kept assuming WatermelonDB, Supabase-native and GoTrue. The stack table can be rebuilt from package.json and the code in well under ten reads, yet the model's built-in defaults still overrode it. Here, "reconstructable from the code" does not mean "safe to remove".

(4) The harness already has the mechanism. For skills (W4): .claude/skills/README.md content rule 1, "FixFlow facts over generic advice", which compresses anything that could apply to any project to its rule. For W1: KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN §8 (line 509) and D11 already define the KS-7 trim criterion, as do the §12 table (line 765) and line 89. Narratives of verified entries move out. Every rule sentence stays. Each of the four Build & deploy traps shrinks to one line, and "Do NOT assume" is untouched. The store is scoped to "the part a cheap agent cannot reconstruct". Line 765 also explicitly rejects pulling knowledge out of always-loaded context, because sessions that never look things up would lose it. So G1-A's stated benefit, that this "would give the KS-7 trim a criterion", is false: KS-7 already has one.

(5) G1-A's proposed E1 arm cannot discriminate. All 10 probes test invariants the criterion would keep. The lines it would actually cut are the pointer, slice-list, scheduler and command blocks (about lines 253-347), and no probe touches them. Each task also gets one session per arm, so "no probe loses" bounds the loss rate only below about 30% (the rule of three the KS design itself uses). It is also a new measurement effort, close in kind to the M00-M06 pipeline the owner skipped (HARNESS-REVIEW line 275: "no gain; owner priority low").
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Settled for the invariants. The only open part is the reconstructable pointer blocks (CLAUDE.md lines 253-347). reviews.lens: BENEFIT: the best honest case for what each family would buy on W1 (CLAUDE.md length) and L2 (context budget, compaction), with strict evidence scoring. reviews.reason: The harness hard-wires model tiers (Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) and has no re-validation step. The trials already exist, so a rerun is cheap.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) None of the cards gives a number. C0640 is a one-line agreement with "you need evals". C0508 is an argument. C0467 is Dex passing on what Steinberger said, and Dex himself still works research-first. (2) G1-B's instrument does not fit the claim. By SHIP-PLAN P1 Entry (around line 322), the cold-resume trial sends a Sonnet agent to recover P1 facts from "SHIP-PLAN §0 and P1", and the main session repairs any miss in the plan. HARNESS-REVIEW line 268 rules it "trial once". So it measures how readable the plan is, not whether a piece of scaffolding has expired. Its subject is pinned to Sonnet: a change to the default (Fable) model only changes the judge. Its facts describe P1, which will have shipped by the time it is rerun. And "keep if >= previous" can never catch a step that has become unnecessary, because a redundant step still scores well; only an ablation can show that. (3) G1-A's "the trials already exist" is false. E1 is proposed by this review and exists nowhere in the harness or the evidence, and the cold-resume trial has never run (W3). One session per arm on 10 yes/no probes gives a run-to-run spread of about 1.3–1.8 in the count, so a threshold of 2 or more fires on noise. Comparing against a score from months earlier also mixes the model change with repo drift: the next-migration-slot answer moves with every migration, and CLAUDE.md itself keeps changing. (4) The trim decision on W1 is already closed off. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN line 509 says KS-7's trim keeps every invariant's rule sentence, and it runs only after a KS-5 go and the D11 ruling. A rerun at a model release cannot license deleting an invariant. Those invariants are project facts paid for in incidents, not the kind of weaker-model scaffolding C0467 describes. (5) On W4/W5: per-release evals for 13 skills and for prompts would be a standing measurement regime. That reopens the deliberate M00–M06 skip ("a month of research established no gain; owner priority low"), and no skill has an eval today. (6) The tier guide (ORCHESTRATION §3) names tiers without version pins, so a silent model update under the same name would not even register as a trigger.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run this only if E1 runs once first, with its 10 probes, the judge rubric and the repo SHA frozen and committed under evidence/. A trigger is defined as a recorded change to the model behind the Sonnet or Opus tier. At the first trigger, run the 10 probes with the full CLAUDE.md on that frozen SHA, old model against new model side by side, 3 fresh sessions per probe per model (60 sessions). A blind Opus judge counts the probes whose plan cites and obeys the invariant. Act only if the two models' mean scores differ by 3 or more out of 10, in the same direction in at least 2 of the 3 repeats. If the new model drops, rewrite the affected rule sentences. If it rises, file nothing beyond a note to the owner, since KS-7 keeps every invariant sentence. If no tier changes before P40 closes, record "not triggered" and drop the step.
refutation.reason: Survives only as a regression check on CLAUDE.md invariant adherence when a model changes, attached to E1 (same frozen SHA, old and new model side by side, repeated runs). Refuted parts: the cold-resume rerun (wrong instrument, pinned to Sonnet), per-release skill and prompt evals (reopens M00–M06), and "remove expired pieces" (no evidence, and closed off by KS-7's keep-every-rule-sentence trim).

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The source is not evidence for the practice. C0281 (G1-cards.md:509-515) is "evidence asserted", from a reasoned podcast remark with no data. Its own claim is that nobody accepts the cost and that long-horizon replay is unreliable, so it argues against running the ablation. 2) The premise does not hold for this harness. Here staleness is judged mechanically, without ablation. CLAUDE.md:372-390 holds two honesty checks: the true Alembic head from the down_revision chain, and that every named path still resolves. SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md:365 adds a P1 CI step that fails when CLAUDE.md's head drifts. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN §5.1-5.2 invalidates store entries on events, never on time: footprint digests are recomputed, controls are re-demonstrated, and early cutoff applies. The "hobbling" class (rules the weights now know, C0282) does not apply to CLAUDE.md's project-specific invariants. 3) The planned trim never raises the question. KS-7 (KS design:644-648, risk row :765) replaces only the narratives of VERIFIED entries with their one-line rule, "keeping every rule". No rule is deleted on a staleness judgement, so no with/without test is needed to protect one. 4) The affordable with/without arm is already scheduled. KS-9 (KS design:666-670) runs "a small with/without arm if the encounter count allows", with a cheap agent with and without `ks` and the outcome measured mechanically. That matches G1-B. 5) E1 as specified cannot settle anything. Its pass criterion is cost only ("runs once at ≤20 sessions per arm pair"), not benefit. refutation.counter_evidence: (1) I ran a probe in this worktree and cleaned it up afterwards; the tree was unchanged. I made three temporary subdirectories, each with its own CLAUDE.md. The nested file was attached to my context only when I used the Read tool. A Grep over the second directory and a Bash `cat` of the third did not attach it. It also arrives only after that first Read. So the cards' "loads when files in that path are touched" (C0977) is wrong as stated. It loads on the first Read, and nothing else triggers it. Any session that never Reads in the region never sees it: Fable writing briefs (SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 55-56, "briefs, gates and judges; it never implements"), and reviewers or extractors that work from `git diff`, `gh pr diff` or Grep. (2) ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §5.1 line 367 tells every subagent "CLAUDE.md is already injected; trust it". After a split that is false for the moved rules. (3) Several invariants are explicitly cross-runtime, so they cannot move into one runtime's file. The bill freeze is "server and client are two halves of one rule" (CLAUDE.md). The lifecycle 409 detail string is parsed by three clients. The outbox client_id dedupe works on both the server and the phone. The ping trust window is enforced server-side, as are money units and slice boundaries. What can move cleanly is mostly reference material that applies to one runtime only. (4) KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN line 765 and D11 (line 710) gate the trim for exactly this reason: moving content "can take knowledge away from sessions that never look up". D11 moves only narratives, never rules, and leaves "Do NOT assume" untouched. A nested split moves rules, so that reason still holds for Fable and for reviewers that only read diffs. (5) The plan cites the root file directly: SHIP-PLAN line 86 ("update the CLAUDE.md head in the same PR"), the P1 CI check on the head, and standing rule 4. (6) For an implementer, root plus one nested file is still most of today's 390 lines, so the adherence gain is much smaller than "the root loses 40%" suggests. (7) C0283's idea of tying memories to code regions to check staleness has no numbers behind it. It is the knowledge store's job (PR #183), not this family's.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run a "split" arm of E1 on a branch. Move only the material that applies to one runtime: the backend slice catalogue, the staff-money detail, the scheduler table, the dispatcher's operational detail and compare_secret go to backend/CLAUDE.md; the offline-engine file table, the EAS build traps and the wizard-state detail go to technician-app/CLAUDE.md. Keep every cross-runtime rule in the root file, and add a one-line pointer index there naming each nested file. Measure three things. (a) The 10 E1 probe tasks, run twice per arm in fresh Sonnet sessions and scored by a blind Opus judge. The split arm must score at least as well as the baseline on every task. (b) Five root sessions that brief but do not implement, for the dispatcher, eas.json, compare_secret, migration-slot and outbox-kind tasks. Each brief must name the invariant as often as the baseline briefs do. (c) Three Opus reviewers, each given a diff with one planted violation (dispatcher cursor unseeded, empty DSN in eas.json, compare_digest on a str) through `gh pr diff` only. They must catch 3/3, as the baseline does. Adopt only if there are zero regressions in (a), (b) and (c) and the root file loses at least 30% of its lines. Also record the per-subagent token overhead against the about 7.5k tokens today. Any regression in (b) or (c) means skip, unless the root keeps those rules. Either way, §5.1's "already injected" line must change before merge.
refutation.reason: Narrowed. The trial should split off only material that applies to one runtime, keep every cross-runtime rule and a pointer index in the root, and test briefs and diff-only reviewers alongside implementers. The mechanism works here: I observed a nested CLAUDE.md attach in a workflow subagent. But it loads only on the Read tool, so Fable's briefs and diff-only reviewers lose whatever moves.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The rule would apply to nothing. The 13-skill commit 1ac6b15 (worktree wizardly-hertz-02c46a) says "No code, CLAUDE.md or ship-plan document changes", and grep finds no mention of "skill" in either worktree's CLAUDE.md. (2) The trigger-enumeration half is already in place, in the place Claude Code reads natively. .claude/skills/README.md line 43 requires each SKILL.md frontmatter `description` to be "the trigger: what it is for, when to use it, when NOT to; ≤ 1024 chars". These descriptions appear in every session's skill listing. For example, fastapi-alembic-safety lists concrete cases (an Alembic migration, a models.py change, a CHECK/FK/unique index on a populated table, a backfill script, a dump restore) and also lists when not to use it. (3) The "short version in case the skill does not load" half is already covered by CLAUDE.md itself. Content rule 2 in the skills README says skills "Never contradict CLAUDE.md": the invariants live in full in CLAUDE.md, and the skills only add procedure on top. For subagents, the agent-definition template's `skills:` field preloads the full SKILL.md, and README lines 115-116 say CLAUDE.md is always loaded as well. (4) Both reviews are off. G1-B's "already-done" cites the wrong mechanism: KS-7 (KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN line 648) covers knowledge-store entries ("one-line rule plus (ks <id>)"), not skill pointers, and it is gated and unbuilt. refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The disable-model-invocation half breaks this harness. The Claude Code skills docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/skills, fetched 2026-11-04) say the flag "also prevents the skill from being preloaded into subagents". In the 13-skill drop (worktree wizardly-hertz-02c46a, commit 1ac6b15, not on main), every one of the 11 agent definitions preloads its skill through line 6 `skills: [...]`, which covers 12 of the 13 skills. The 13th, fixflow-orchestration, is the skill the main session loads itself. G1-A's rule ("owner-only or destructive skills carry disable-model-invocation") would therefore leave fixflow-recovery-operator, fixflow-eas-release-operator and others starting with an empty skill. G1-B's guard covers "invoke" but not preload. Also, `.claude/skills/README.md` rule 4 marks owner-only steps `[owner]` inside skills, so no skill is owner-only as a whole, and the flag has zero safe candidates today. (2) The MCP half is already handled. In FixFlow sessions, MCP tools are deferred behind ToolSearch, so only their names are listed. The desktop/anthropic-skills plugin listing is not repo-controlled. (3) The trim half partly exists already. README caps descriptions at ≤1024 chars, and KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN KS-C9 already caps its own skill description at 300–400 chars. The 13 skills, though, sit at the cap: 12,898 chars measured, 955–1026 each. The 11 agent descriptions add 11,156 chars. That is about 6–10k tokens arriving in the main session, roughly the size of CLAUDE.md (29,605 bytes). So the cost is real, but the "instruction budget" adherence claim is anecdotal (C1270 thresholds were recalled from memory). (4) It has no bearing on W1 (CLAUDE.md itself is unchanged) or on W2 (compliance stays just as unobservable). Trimming also risks dropping the "Do NOT use it to…" negative-trigger clauses the README mandates.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Before 1ac6b15 merges, run /context in a fresh session in that worktree and record the skills and custom-agents token lines. Then trim each of the 13 skill descriptions and 11 agent descriptions to ≤400 chars: key use case first, keep one "do not" clause. Run /context again. Pass requires all three of these: (a) the combined lines fall by ≥50%, to about ≤4k tokens; (b) a routing check of 13 positive probes (one task per skill, phrased without naming it) plus 5 negative probes (tasks that must not load a skill, e.g. installing on a roster phone), one fresh session per probe per arm, where the trimmed arm gets ≥ (long arm − 1) correct loads and zero new false loads; (c) for each of the 11 agents, a one-turn spawn quotes one cited fact from its preloaded SKILL.md. For the flag, add a grep/CI lint that fails if any skill named in an agent's `skills:` list, or fixflow-orchestration, carries disable-model-invocation.
refutation.reason: Narrowed to a trial. The flag half is refuted: per the vendor docs it blocks subagent preload, which 12 of the 13 skills rely on, so it only fits a future owner-typed slash command that no agent preloads. The MCP half is already deferred. What survives is a trial trim of the ~24k chars of skill and agent descriptions, which is an L2 gain only and needs a routing check before adoption.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The "load tools on demand" half is already how this harness works. The tool listing in every session here lists about 130 MCP tools by name only (claude-in-chrome x20, scheduled-tasks x6, mcp-registry x3, about 60 ccd_* tools, terminal x4, docs connector x5); their schemas load only through ToolSearch. The family's own cards say the same: C1069 says "Claude offloads tools to search when there are too many", and C1247 cites Anthropic's MCP tool search. So the "50,000 tokens at start" premise (C1069, asserted, no measurement) does not apply. 2) The tools that stay fully loaded in this very refuter subagent are Claude_Browser (17 tools), visualize (2), docs (3), plus ccd_session and ccd_turn, which the app needs for update_plan and wrap_up. By reading the schemas, the switchable part is roughly 6-7k tokens. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md lines 66-78 measured phase sessions re-sending up to 944k tokens on a 1M window and compacting at 971k and 580k. That makes the switchable overhead under 1% of the window and under 2% of the 400k autoCompactWindow. The same compaction audit found that "Nothing lost caused a mistake or re-work" and that the real cost is money and latency, so start-up overhead is not the L2 failure mode. 3) It does nothing for W1: CLAUDE.md stays 390 lines. 4) It has no landing site in the repo: there is no .mcp.json, and .claude/ holds only launch.json. The servers are desktop-app connectors, so "MCP hygiene in .claude settings" (the reader's guess) is really a per-session connector toggle, and it risks turning off a tool a phase turns out to need. 5) By the estimate above, G1-B's own adopt threshold (>=10k tokens saved) would very likely fail. One small honest residual: a server's instructions are injected even when its tools are deferred (claude-in-chrome injected a conditional "prefer Bash over Read/Edit/Write in bypass mode" block here). That is about 300 tokens, conditional, and not what the family proposes.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run /context once at the start of one Fable phase session and read the MCP-tools line. If the non-deferred MCP tokens from servers that phase does not use total under 10k (about 1% of the 1M window), the skip stands. If they total 40k or more, reopen it as a trial: switch those connectors off per session for 3 phases and count tools missed (pass = 0 missed).
refutation.reason: Loading tools on demand is already built in through deferred loading and ToolSearch. The servers left to switch off cost roughly 6-7k tokens, under 1% of a 1M window whose measured problem is cost, not lost information. The idea also does not touch CLAUDE.md length (W1), so the benefit on W1 and L2 is illusory.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The harness already has the visibility this family asks for. The desktop app's `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__get_usage` returns the context window "as the composer shows it", so an always-visible meter already exists. It also gives tokensUsed, percent, the auto-compact point and a per-category breakdown, the same data as /context. I called it during this review and got tokensUsed 509,816 of 1,000,000 (51%), autoCompactsAtPercent 97, and categories Messages 417,949, System tools 41,653, MCP tools 19,871, System prompt 13,861, Memory files 10,149, Skills 6,226. Model-aware warnings and auto-compaction are native Claude Code features: HR §6 lines 318-323 cover autoCompactWindow per model id and idleCompaction at 200k. Building a meter or warnings would be redundant. 2) G1-B's reason, "the model cannot see its own fill level", is false: get_usage("self") is read-only and the model can call it. G1-A's step "each phase session records /context" names the wrong tool. /context is a built-in CLI command, and the Skill tool's description says built-in CLI commands are not skills, so the agent cannot run it. G1-B's version makes the owner transcribe numbers by hand, which costs owner attention and isn't needed. 3) The benefit on W1 has already been collected and is not a budget problem. CLAUDE.md plus MEMORY.md ("Memory files") cost 10,149 tokens, about 1% of the window. One reading settles the CLAUDE.md token cost, so recording it every phase adds nothing. W1 is about how many instructions get followed, which a token count cannot measure; the E1 ablation measures it. The W1 trim is also gated on the knowledge-store pilot, not on a number. 4) HR §6 (lines 311-330) shows exact token history can already be recovered afterwards from the transcript: 971k → 22k, about 8k per call. A gap does survive: HR-C4 ("if a phase session is observed past 500k", line 328) has no sensor named anywhere in ship plan §0 (lines 24-116). This review's own parent session is at about 510k (not a phase session) and nothing in the routine flagged it.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: For the first 4 phase sessions, Fable calls get_usage("self") at phase close. refutation.counter_evidence: (1) Weak evidence. C0067 and C0225 are both 'asserted': each is a rule in a HumanLayer file, with no incident and no numbers. (2) No benefit on the named weaknesses. The family adds a rule, so it cannot shorten CLAUDE.md (W1), and keeping one .env out of context saves tens of lines at most (L2). (3) Much of it is already in place. SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md P0a item 3 (lines 239-248) already passes the R2 keys by name ('export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=…' then 'docker run -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY'). ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md line 790 (v3) already rules that the secret scan returns 'a hash fingerprint — never the value, never a quoted line — because every agent output is journaled'. In P3b step 2 (line 592) the owner places the secrets, and an encrypted copy goes to the owner's password manager. (4) The test-credential, screenshot and chat half has nothing to protect here. The platform safety rules already say not to repeat test credentials in replies and to record them in seed/example config, and CLAUDE.md's doc map shows the demo credentials are already written down in docs/HANDOFF.md. (5) G1-A's measurement cannot tell the two arms apart: the evidence/ folder should scan clean with or without the rule, because the read-only analysts never handle secrets. Against G1-B, two real gaps remain. First, no deny rule exists: the worktree's .claude/ holds only launch.json, the user's settings.json has no deny entry, and CI runs no secret scan. Yet backend/.env and technician-app/.env are real gitignored files (.gitignore lines 28 and 47), and the §5.1 CONTEXT block makes every agent cite 'path:line — quote', so an agent that opens .env would quote its secrets into a journaled output. Second, the P0a item 4 pg_dump recipe puts the DB password inline ('postgresql://postgres.<ref>:<pw>@…'), and the P4a curl sends 'CF-Access-Client-Id/Secret' (line 622) without saying the values go by name.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: How to tell it worked: at the close of each of P0a, P3b, P3c and P4a, run a local exact-value scan of that phase's committed diff, PR body and evidence files against the live secret values (report the count only, never the value). It must find 0. The committed P0a record must show the pg_dump step using PGPASSWORD by name, not a password in the URL. Any hit means the rule failed: rotate that secret and send the owner the deny/scan-hook decision.
refutation.reason: The W1/L2 framing, the CLAUDE.md placement, the generic CONTEXT-block line and the test-credential half are refuted. A smaller rule survives, aimed at the phases that handle secrets. In the P0a, P3b, P3c and P4a briefs, secret values are passed by variable name (PGPASSWORD for pg_dump; $CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET for curl), committed records name the variable and never the value, and agents never Read or cat a .env. Separately, the owner decides whether to add a project-level deny rule on Read of .env files: it is enforced by the tool and costs no always-loaded context.

reviews.measurement: On P1's gates (ruff, mypy, pytest -rs, vitest, jest), compare a quiet wrapper with the raw commands. The wrapper prints failures plus one pass/fail/skip count line per gate. Adopt if gate output tokens fall by 80% or more, and pass/fail/skip counts are identical on a green run and on a run with one planted failure.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The backend gates already run quiet. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md Appendix A (lines 630-666) has a g() wrapper. It sends each gate's full output to /work/logs/gate-N.log and prints only "GATE[i cmd] EXIT=rc" plus "SUMMARY FAIL=". It already uses pytest -q. The agent reports the EXIT lines and the tail of any failing log, and command agents "redirect output to scratchpad logs" (line 619). The ship plan §0 "Gates" bullet (SHIP-PLAN lines 57-60) makes Appendix A mandatory for backend gates. So both reviewers missed an existing mechanism: G1-A said "existing: -", and G1-B pointed only at the CLAUDE.md commands. That covers ruff, mypy, lint-imports, alembic, pytest and pip-audit, the half of the family's claim that matters most. Logging to disk also avoids the rerun failure that C1586 describes. 2) G1-A's main evidence is misapplied. The "68% tool results" figure (HARNESS-REVIEW line 316) comes from a Fable planning session that ran workflow scripts and reads, not from gate runs. Fable never implements (ship plan §0 Routing), so gate output reaches only subagent or Docker contexts. 3) The ~75k "smart zone" and "2-3% of the window" figures (C1579) are asserted without an experiment. They are sized for a ~168k window and conflict with HR-C4's measured 500k threshold. C0069 is anecdotal and gives no token counts. 4) The Bash tool already truncates any single output at 30,000 characters, about 7.5k tokens. 5) Skip visibility no longer depends on reading output. P1's skip-aware gate (SHIP-PLAN lines 361-364: -rs --junitxml, fails when any @integration test is skipped) turns skips into an exit code. 6) What is left is small and unmeasured. The web and mobile gates run natively at default verbosity. On a green run, eslint and tsc print nothing, prettier and ruff print one line, vitest prints about 18 file lines (18 test files) and jest about 39 PASS lines (39 files). The unknowns are console noise inside the tests and the vite build and expo export listings.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: A one-off measurement at P1, then two code phases. Step 1: on a green tree, run the native web gates (npm run lint, format:check, test, build) and mobile gates (typecheck, test, expo export --platform android) once each. Record stdout+stderr characters/4 per gate. Step 2: if a full web+mobile run is at or below 3k tokens, or no single gate passes 1.5k, skip the trial and record it as already covered by Appendix A. Step 3: otherwise, wrap those commands in the same g() pattern. Add one count line per gate: tests passed, failed and skipped, parsed from the pytest/vitest/jest summary. Adopt if three things hold over the next 2 code phases: (a) wrapped output tokens fall by 70% or more against Step 1; (b) on a planted failing test and a planted it.skip, the GATE lines plus the failing-log tail show the same pass/fail/skip counts as the raw run; (c) zero gate reruns, and zero log re-reads by the implementer, are caused by missing information. Count (c) from the subagent transcripts.
refutation.reason: Narrowed. The backend half is already done: Appendix A's g() wrapper keeps full logs on disk and prints only exit lines, using pytest -q. What survives as a trial is extending that same wrapper, with a pass/fail/skip count line, to the native web and mobile gates, and only if a single green-run measurement shows their output is worth cutting. The ~75k smart-zone figure is refuted for this harness.

refutation.counter_evidence: The harness already prevents this failure on the one suite slow enough for it to matter. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md Appendix A (lines 630-666) is the backend gate recipe. Its g() wrapper sends each gate's full output to its own file (/work/logs/gate-$i.log) and prints only `GATE[i cmd] EXIT=rc`. Line 653 writes the full container log to disk ("the GATE/SETUP/SUMMARY lines are the result"), and line 654 copies the per-gate logs out. Line 652 says "NEVER a second `docker run`". Lines 659-660 have the agent report the GATE lines and the tail of each failing gate's log, so reading the tail of a saved file costs no rerun. Lines 618-623 add "redirect output to scratchpad logs" and "never re-issue a mutating command". Line 780 records this as a design ruling ("full logs to disk"). SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §0 lines 57-60 make Appendix A the required path for every backend gate run, including the Postgres integration tests the readers expected the rule to cover. Web and mobile gates (Vitest, Jest) run natively and are fast, so a truncated run there costs very little to repeat. On the claim itself: C1578 is speculation that the source flags as opinion. C1586 is one anecdote (pytest | head -n 50) plus a token count from an unofficial tokenizer. Both reviewers gave evidence 1 and benefit 1.
refutation.reason: Already done: the backend gate wrapper in Appendix A saves every gate's full output to disk and forbids a second run, so a head/tail view can never force a slow-suite rerun. A no-truncation line would duplicate it. The only gap is an ad-hoc fast test run outside the recipe, which is too cheap to need a rule or a trial.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The W1 benefit both reviewers give does not exist. Neither measurement removes a line from CLAUDE.md, and the trim is owner-gated behind the knowledge-store pilot (W1). CLAUDE.md does not hold exemplar patterns. It holds invariants (rule plus reason), and its "Where things live" section already points to docs/CODE-MAP.md. The repo already documents the patterns: ARCHITECTURE.md:191 "Adding a new feature", ARCHITECTURE.md:247 "Signed-URL upload pattern", and CODE-MAP.md:245 "the pattern every slice follows". (2) Part of the mechanism already exists. ORCHESTRATION §5.3 says "A brief names the goal, the files...". Where it matters, ship plan scopes already name the pattern with its source, e.g. SHIP-PLAN ~l.1002 "the `try_transition` pattern, preferred" and l.861 mobile import rules "mirroring the backend import-linter contracts". CI import-linter and ESLint enforce slice boundaries mechanically. (3) The failure mode in C0981, models defaulting to patterns the codebase avoids, maps in FixFlow onto CLAUDE.md invariants: direct fetch vs sendOrQueue, and load-mutate-flush vs try_transition. Code that touches those is routed to Opus (SHIP-PLAN §0 Routing; ORCH §3 Sonnet "never for invariant-sensitive code"), so Sonnet's exposure is limited to well-specified screens, read models and tests. (4) The evidence is weak. C0043 and C1220 are asserted. C0981 is anecdotal, with no counts, and its React provider/useEffect example comes from his own product. (5) The proposed measurements cannot tell the arms apart. They compare 2 PRs against 2 PRs that differ in scope. G1-A's "or zero" clause passes trivially when the baseline is zero. The reviewer output has no "pattern drift" class to count. (6) C1220's step where humans choose old vs new adds owner load to every phase. Pattern choices already go through design notes, the G1/G2 gates and the decisions journal.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Reuse E1's frozen-probe harness. Take 4 Sonnet-tier tasks from the plan: one read-model endpoint, one web screen, one mobile screen, and one test from a design's test list. Run each task in 2 fresh Sonnet sessions, one brief with a 'Mirror: <1-3 source paths>' line and one without, for 8 sessions in total. An Opus judge, blind to the arm, scores each diff against a fixed 5-item conformance checklist: (a) router→service→repository layering and barrel-only cross-slice imports; (b) the existing api client or sendOrQueue is used, never a direct fetch; (c) tests use the existing fixtures and seams (e.g. the real-Postgres integration pattern of test_identity_integration.py); (d) naming and file layout match the sibling slice; (e) no new dependency. Keep the line if the with-line arm has at least 1 fewer deviation on at least 3 of 4 tasks and more on none. Otherwise skip.
refutation.reason: Narrowed: only one thing survives. Sonnet implementation briefs get one field naming 1-3 existing files to mirror, which extends ORCH §5.3 and can be filled by the fixflow-explorer locator. It does nothing for W1 (CLAUDE.md is untouched and the trim stays gated), and the human old-vs-new choice step is dropped. The evidence is asserted or anecdotal, so it is a trial with a blind paired probe, not the 2-vs-2 PR count.

refutation.counter_evidence:
1) The source takes the figure back itself. C0365 (same podcast as C0364) says "Obviously, that number is higher now". C0589 (same interview as C0588) says he regularly runs 200-300k tokens and calls strictly obeying the 100k rule the "peak of the midwit curve". C0588 dates the 100k origin to an Opus 4.1/4.5 training session and calls it "training wheels". C1098 quotes the figure from memory. None of this applies to the models this harness runs (claude-fable-5-1, Opus 5.5).
2) The strongest card, C1189, is graded "measured", but it records a vendor's product-setting change, not a measured outcome. As carded, its arithmetic does not reconcile: 40% of 168k is 67k, not ~100k (the numbers work only if 40% means context remaining). The flat 100k for 1M models ("only 10%") was chosen, not measured.
3) The harness already does continuously what a 100k trigger would do. SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 31-43: the Decisions/ruled-out journal is appended "the moment one occurs" (HR-C2). A resume is the first unticked box plus `Plan @ <sha>`, so a fresh session costs nothing. Reviewer A's adoption rule ("append journal, write handoff, consider fresh session") repeats two existing mechanisms and adds only a threshold.
4) On this harness the threshold carries no signal. HARNESS-REVIEW §6 measured growth of about 8k-10.7k tokens per call, so 100k arrives within roughly 10-12 calls, and every phase session will cross it early. The trigger either fires every time (noise) or splits every phase across sessions, which works against HR-C1.
5) For the same reason, A's adoption test is confounded. Almost every Fable gate decision will come after 100k, and refute-by-default reviewers overturn decisions at some base rate. "At least 1 overturned after 100k" over 4 sessions is therefore near-certain whether or not a dumb zone exists, because there is no comparison against decisions made before 100k.
6) A live in-phase trigger needs a context signal that the model can see: a hook or a context system. HR-C3 skipped both, and the reasons still hold. Post-hoc observation of session size is already HR-C4's job (500k, act on observation).
7) HR §Q6 found that nothing lost in the 971k/580k compactions caused a mistake or re-work. That session was the multi-purpose review session, not a phase session, and HR-C1 already addresses it.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: This is only needed if the underlying question comes back. Run a post-hoc read of the phase-session transcripts, which needs no meter: §6 of the harness review already did this. Over at least 8 phase sessions, bin each Fable gate or judge decision by the context size when it was made (under 100k, 100-300k, over 300k). Count how often a reviewer or the owner overturned decisions in each bin. A dumb zone on this harness shows up only if the overturn rate in a later bin is at least twice the rate under 100k, with at least 10 decisions per bin. Otherwise, keep HR-C4 as it stands.
refutation.reason: The claim's own author withdraws the flat 100k (C0365: higher now; C0589: 200-300k routinely, strict 100k is the "midwit" peak). Its best evidence is a vendor setting misgraded as measured, from Opus 4.x/Sonnet 4.5. The wrap-up actions already run continuously in §0/HR-C2. At the measured ~8-10k tokens per call a 100k trigger fires in every phase, and A's adoption test would pass whether or not a dumb zone exists. HR-C4's observation rule stands.

refutation.counter_evidence:
1) The evidence is anecdotal. C0494 and C0904 are "personal heuristic, no data". C0853 is an observation at about 200-300k tokens. C0877 is one sentence of Q&A. All four come from one author and give no numbers, so the dumb-zone token threshold and the "restart at 30-50K" remedy are unsupported claims.
2) The harness already has the restart half. Fable "never implements" (SHIP-PLAN §0 Routing, l.55), so any flailing happens inside subagents, and Fable briefs a fresh one for each task. One phase per session is HR-C1. The PR-body journal and the first-unticked-box resume (§0 Resume, l.31-43; HR-C2) are the "write state to a file" step.
3) The "extreme edits to a failing test" half is already caught. The reviewer must list "every changed expected value, removed assertion and new skip or xfail with its reason" (§0 l.54-55; HARNESS-REVIEW §4, adopt row). A phase is "not done until gates are green locally and CI is green on the PR" (§0 Gates, l.59-60). Skip-aware gates report skipped counts in the closing message. So a "preexisting" claim cannot ship a red gate.
4) The detection does not transfer. In C0904 the tell is in the agent's thinking traces mid-run. Fable sees only a subagent's final report or a workflow's result, so it can apply the trigger only after the run, never as "kill it now".
5) The benefit on W2 is illusory. This is one more self-reported rule with no hook, so it does not make compliance visible.
What survives is one real gap: §0 requires a reason for each new skip or xfail but never requires that the reason be proven. A "preexisting/unrelated" reason is therefore accepted unchecked.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: The narrowed clause is an adopt, so this is how to tell it worked. Over the first 5 code phases, every new skip or xfail, and every red test reported as "preexisting/unrelated", must cite the same failure on the base SHA, either from main's CI run at that SHA or from a local run of that one test on the base commit. Pass: zero such reasons merge without that citation, and the Opus reviewer's verdict mentions each one. Fail: an uncited "preexisting" reason reaches a merged PR, or a claim later proves false on the base commit. Separately, the full dumb-zone restart trigger is not worth trialling. Fable cannot observe subagent context mid-run, and with the routine not yet run the base rate of such events is unknown. Revisit it only if, after P1-P5, at least 2 implementer runs needed more than one re-brief for the same failing test.
refutation.reason: Narrowed: skip the dumb-zone restart trigger. It rests on anecdote, Fable cannot see subagent flailing mid-run, and fresh-per-brief subagents, HR-C1 and HR-C2 already cover it. Adopt only a one-clause tightening of §0 Routing: a "preexisting/unrelated" reason for a new skip, xfail or red test must show the same failure on the base SHA. If it cannot, the work is rejected and Fable re-briefs a fresh agent from the PR journal.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The harness already counts fixed overhead. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §3 (line 90) says "Every subagent also pays a fixed overhead (CLAUDE.md ≈ 7.5k tokens plus the CONTEXT block)", and §(caps) line 583 repeats it. Both turn it into rules: tiny tasks run inline, and claims are batched per verifier. The 7.5k figure checks out, since the repo's CLAUDE.md is 390 lines and 29,605 bytes. 2) The "of a 200k window" framing does not fit the main session. In the HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md compaction audit (lines 66-74 and 312-320), the main session auto-compacted at 971k tokens. Context grew about 8k tokens per call, 68% of it tool results, so tool output drives the growth and the starting load does not. The harness already acts on that through one phase per session (HR-C1) and the 500k trigger (HR-C4). 3) The numbers are second-hand and stale. C1081 is "stated from memory, no measurement shown", and C1529's 16k is "said without a source". The two cards also contradict each other (50k vs 16k). The 32k-of-tools figure predates deferred tool loading: in this very session about 100 tools sit behind ToolSearch with no schemas loaded. 4) It has no mechanism of its own. Both reviewers send the only actionable form, a /context reading at phase start, to F042. Reviewer B's "trial" is literally "Folded into F042". On W1, most of the baseline (system prompt, tools) is not CLAUDE.md at all, so trimming CLAUDE.md would not touch it. The benefit on W1 is illusory, and on L2 the mechanism is already in place.
refutation.reason: This is a recalled fact, not a mechanism, and its numbers are unsourced and out of date. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §3 and the HR compaction audit already budget for per-agent overhead (CLAUDE.md about 7.5k tokens) and for the context growth they actually measured. Any baseline number belongs to F042, so A's skip stands and B's trial lives on only inside F042.

reviews.lens: BENEFIT: the best honest case for what each family would buy on W1 (CLAUDE.md length) and L2 (context budget, compaction), with strict evidence scoring. reviews.measurement: Count imperative instructions, not lines, in CLAUDE.md, §0 and the 13 skills, recorded once in OWNER-VIEW. It worked if KS-7 and E1 use that count as their size metric, and the total always loaded in a phase session is known against the 150–200 band.
reviews.reason: Counting is nearly free. It replaces W1's line-count proxy with the unit the only measured study uses.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) Counting rules cannot measure KS-7, the only trim the harness plans. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md line 509 and the KS-7 Scope (lines 644-651) and D11 (line 710) keep every rule sentence and every "Do NOT assume" line, and move only narratives out. A rule count before and after KS-7 is therefore unchanged by design. Using it as KS-7's size metric, which both reviews propose, would show "no change" and hide the narrative cut, the one thing KS-7 actually changes. KS-7 already reports line counts. (2) On the family's own unit, CLAUDE.md is not over the budget. A grep of the 390-line file finds 39 bold rule bullets, 38 lines containing never, must, do not or always, and about 57 sentences with imperative markers. All are far below 150-200. W1's length concern rests on the vendor's roughly-200-line guidance (KS design line 185, M-02), which a rule count does not replace. (3) The "total loaded in a phase session against the 150-200 band" figure is dominated by the platform. The Claude Code system prompt, tool descriptions and MCP schemas in the desktop app hold far more imperatives than C1200's unsourced "~50". The Artifact tool description alone has dozens, and this subagent's context already carries dozens of MCP tool schemas. The owner cannot trim any of these, so the total sits over the band no matter what the owner does. (4) The evidence is weak, by the sources' own account. C0859 says Dex "had not read the data himself". C1095 says the number is "inflated a year on". C1334 says it is "probably higher now". C1200 and C1186 give no visible data. From memory, not from a read: the underlying 2025 study (IFScale) measured satisfying many keyword-inclusion constraints at once in one output. That is a different task from obeying one conditional invariant among many, which is what each E1 probe needs. (5) E1 measures per-invariant adherence directly, so a proxy count adds nothing to any decision E1 informs.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Only if the owner wants the grep confirmed: one Haiku pass that lists CLAUDE.md's rule sentences in a typed list. If the total is under 150 (the grep gives 39-57), the instruction-budget argument does not apply to CLAUDE.md and the family needs no further work.
refutation.reason: Counting is cheap but useless here: KS-7 keeps every rule so the count never moves, CLAUDE.md is already well under 150 rules, and the platform prompt the owner can't trim dominates the total, so the count would change no decision.

reviews.measurement: First count the instructions in §0 plus the standing rules. If there are more than 40, split them into phase-start, mid-phase and close checklists of fewer than 40 each, then run the F034 alternating-phase audit. Adopt if checklist phases miss fewer of the 6 routine items over 6 phases.
reviews.reason: §0 is a dense 90-line routine that has never run (W3), and W2 says skipped steps are invisible. This is the closest analogue in the group, a 50% skip rate at 85 instructions, and the fix is cheap to try.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The claim's own cards do not measure the outcome. C1118 says "before/after instruction counts only; no adherence rate given". C1435 says the fix was "stated as working but not measured". C1274 has "no outcome data", and C1335 is "inference from the instruction-budget number". C1311 is tagged "measured", but it only counts instructions (85+ before, under 40 after). C1332's 50% is "of people, maybe more", not a skip rate per run. (2) The cause is confounded. Per C1435 and C1118, the RPI split also turned one prompt into three human-invoked commands (design, structure, plan). The step that got skipped was the interactive Q&A pause, and a separate command makes that pause impossible to skip regardless of how many instructions each prompt has. The figure 40 is simply where their prompts ended up, not a measured threshold. C1334's 150-200 figure, the only number on the instruction budget, does not imply 40. (3) G1-A proposes counting the instructions in §0 plus the standing rules. That counts the wrong thing. In SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md lines 24-116, the per-phase routine is about 18-20 obligations, and they fall at different points in a long session: start, first commit, during, close. Most of the remaining text is domain rules (drain image and cherry-pick, migrations, retired phones, standing rules 1-7). Those are constraints, not a step sequence, and they cannot be "skipped" the way the Q&A step was. (4) The harness already has a regrouped routine. The fixflow-orchestration skill being added (.claude/worktrees/wizardly-hertz-02c46a/.claude/skills/fixflow-orchestration/SKILL.md, 371 lines) restates §0 as numbered procedure steps 1-32 and beyond, grouped as Session start, Briefing, Workflow scripts, Gating and PR/merge/deploy. That skill is the real monolith Fable will load on top of CLAUDE.md. Splitting §0 itself would create a third copy of the routine, and the skill already has to keep a §1.8 list of stale or superseded text to manage drift between the two copies that exist. (5) The family adds nothing on W2. Splitting a prompt does not make compliance any more visible from outside; only an audit does, and that is the F034 mechanism, not this family. P1's cold-resume trial (plan lines 322-327) tests whether ten plan facts can be recovered, not whether the routine was followed. (6) Credit on W1 is illusory. CLAUDE.md is a set of reference invariants, not a multi-step workflow prompt, and its trim stays gated behind the knowledge-store pilot. (7) W3: the routine has never run, so no skip has been observed.
refutation.reason: Narrowed. The evidence is one confounded anecdote: no adherence rate after the split, the 40 cutoff is unfounded, and the fix also added human-invoked stops between prompts. So G1-A's "count §0, split if over 40" is refuted. What survives is G1-B's version: audit the §0 obligations in P1 and P2a, and only if a step is missed, move that moment into a short checklist in the fixflow-orchestration skill (not §0). No W1 or W2 credit.

reviews.measurement: In the P1 cold-resume trial and the next two phase sessions, record the tokens read before the first action. The ship plan is 1553 lines / 122 KB. Pass if a one-line read list ('§0 + your phase + its cited design note; do not read other phases') cuts pre-action reads by >=50% and the agent still recovers 10/10 frozen facts.
reviews.reason: A fresh session that loads a 122 KB plan to run one phase is the clearest context-budget waste here, and a read-list line costs nothing.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) Evidence: C0159 is "evidence asserted". It is a template string repeated across HumanLayer skills, with no measurement. Under the owner rules that is anecdotal. (2) The harness already has the mechanism where reads multiply, which is in subagents. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §5.3: analysts "start from the files named in the brief", follow one hop, and list every extra read. "Skeptics get the claim, its evidence and its failing condition only, in a fresh context." The §5.1 CONTEXT block says "Settled facts ... do not re-investigate" and "Prior registers to cite, not re-summarise". That is consume-once, already written down. (3) The plan's consumed intermediates are never pointed at by any phase. Across the phase sections of SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md (lines 219-1280), the critique-N files and §6.1-6.4/§6.7 get 0 references, and superseded plan versions exist only in git history (header, line 11). Phases do cite §6.5 and §6.6 rulings about 34 times (ruling R1-R9, HR-A1..A4). So "do not read §6", the natural list, would cut facts the phases depend on, which puts the P1 cold-resume trial (W3) at risk. (4) The L2 benefit is negligible. The whole plan is 122,410 bytes, about 30k tokens, about 3% of the 1M window this Fable session reached (HARNESS-REVIEW Q6: compaction at 971k). The same audit measured context growth at about 8k tokens per call, 68% of it tool results during the work. A one-time upfront read is not what pushes a session toward the ~40% zone. The ruled defence is HR-C1 (one phase per session) plus HR-C2, and HR-C4 sets the trigger at 500k. (5) G1-A's premise that "a fresh session loads a 122 KB plan" is a guess. The routine has never run, and §0 Resume already scopes re-reads to sections changed since Plan @ sha.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: No trial is needed. Watch for it in data already being collected. In P1's cold-resume transcript and the next two phase sessions, count the tokens read before the first action. Also note any Read that lands in a critique-N file or §6.1-6.4/§6.7. Reopen only if pre-action reads exceed 100k tokens in any session, or a read of consumed history changes an answer or brings back a rejected finding. Then add a single line to §0 that keeps §6.5/§6.6 in scope.
refutation.reason: The evidence is only asserted. §5.3 and the CONTEXT block already scope subagent reads. No phase points at consumed artifacts. The 3%-of-window budget gain is too small to matter, and an explicit do-not-read list risks cutting the §6.5/§6.6 rulings that phases cite. Skip, and reopen only if the P1 transcript shows wasted or misleading reads of history.

Split the plan into §0 + per-phase files if the plan read exceeds ~30k tokens or a late-file fact is missed.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) Neither card shows any harm. C1546 only lists file sizes (343,275 and 143,883 bytes), and the card says Dex does not comment on them. The idea that they show "sprawl when no one prunes" is the reader's guess. C0210 is a rule stated inside a research-writing skill, with no numbers behind it. 2) The 1000-line rule measures the wrong thing here. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md has 972 lines but 303,791 bytes, with 22 lines over 2000 characters. It would pass the rule. SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md has 1553 lines but only 122,410 bytes, and it would fail. The knowledge-store design is not on any phase session's read path (PR #183, not built). 3) Reading by section is already in the routine. The P1 cold-resume trial gives the fresh agent only "the repository and 'read SHIP-PLAN §0 and P1'" (plan lines 322-327). Resume re-reads only the sections changed since `Plan @ <sha>` (§0, lines 31-40). The pin is a git sha diffed over docs/program/, so it works with one file or many. 4) G1-A's measurement cannot work in P1. §0 is lines 24-116 and P1 is lines 317-383, so no frozen fact about P1 sits past line 1000. The trial's own rule ("fixes any miss in the plan (same PR)") already covers a miss. 5) The cost is small. Reading the whole plan once is about 30k tokens, roughly 3% of the ~1M window the harness review measured (compaction at 971k). The per-call growth in that review came from tool results (68%), not from one plan read. 6) It does not touch W1: CLAUDE.md is 390 lines, well under 1000. 7) The transfer is weak. Ralph's plan file grew because an unattended loop kept appending to it. FixFlow's plan is a hand-adjudicated v8 with a §6 adjudication record. G1-B's churn cost is also smaller than it claimed: only 11 section-style references in 4 files.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Settled for now. To reopen at no extra cost, use the P1 trial transcript that is already scheduled. Count the tokens the fresh Sonnet agent reads from SHIP-PLAN, and note whether it reads outside §0 and P1. Reopen only if those reads go over 40k tokens. Also reopen if a later phase's fact miss is traced to the plan's length rather than its wording.
refutation.reason: Skip. There is no evidence of harm, and a line cap misses the repo's real outlier (304 KB in 972 lines). The plan is already read by section (P1 trial brief, resume rule). The one test G1-A proposes cannot detect a fact missed past line 1000.

reviews.lens: Cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is reopened and still holds, what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build, run and keep honest.
reviews.existing_mechanism: Claude Code defers MCP tool schemas behind ToolSearch (visible in these sessions: dozens of MCP tools listed by name only)
reviews.reason: The measured 5.7k overhead was for eagerly loaded schemas; the current client defers them.

reviews.lens: benefit
reviews.measurement: Run /context at the start of one fresh phase session and record the token lines for MCP tools, system tools, memory files and CLAUDE.md. If MCP tools exceed 10k tokens (or 5% of the window), disable the servers a phase does not use (chrome, visualize, scheduled-tasks, mcp-registry, docs) and re-run /context to confirm the saving.
reviews.reason: There is no tool-loadout policy, and this session carries many MCP servers. One /context reading decides it, though deferred tool loading may already make the cost small.

refutation.counter_evidence:
1) The evidence is thin. C1601 and C1776 are assertions. C1772 is the only number: 5.7k tokens for the Linear MCP, from one eager-loading `claude -p` run in Sept 2025. Today's client lists most MCP servers by name only: claude-in-chrome, scheduled-tasks, mcp-registry and the ccd_* tools, about 130 tools in this session. G1-A wants to disable chrome, scheduled-tasks, mcp-registry, visualize and docs, but the first three are already deferred, so turning them off saves only their names.
2) The tool list is not what fills the window. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md §6 (line 316) measures window growth as 68% tool results and 26% Write/Edit payloads. The window is about 1M tokens: compaction ran at 971k (§Q6). HR-C1 (one phase per session) already limits L2.
3) I measured the first-turn prompt in the transcripts. A Fable main session on this repo starts at about 85-88k tokens, roughly 8.5% of a 1M window, so the L2 benefit is small. Nothing links tool definitions to CLAUDE.md adherence, so the W1 claim has no support.
4) The harness already chooses tools per agent: .claude/agents/fixflow-explorer.md sets `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash`.
5) G1-B's already-done is also too strong. Deferral is partial: MCP schemas still load eagerly. This refuter carries mcp__Claude_Browser__* (17 tools), mcp__visualize__*, the docs connector and mcp__terminal__read_terminal, and uses none of them. Across 399 Opus and Sonnet workflow subagents, the median fixed first-turn prompt is about 64k tokens. One restricted-tool built-in agent (claude-code-guide, Haiku) started at about 35k.
refutation.what_would_settle_it:
Step 1, one reading: run /context at the start of one fresh phase session and record the tokens for MCP tools, system tools, skills, memory files and CLAUDE.md. Adopt a per-phase MCP disable list only if eagerly loaded MCP schemas are at least 20k tokens (2% of the window). Otherwise close the main-session part as skip.
Step 2, subagents: in one workflow of at least 20 refuter or extractor agents, run half under a whitelisted-tools agent type (the fixflow-explorer pattern), if the Workflow API accepts one. Count first-turn prompt tokens, total tokens per agent and how often the verdicts match.
Pass threshold for step 2: the prompt falls by at least 20k tokens per agent (at least 30%), verdicts match in at least 90% of pairs, and no agent fails because a tool it needed was missing.
refutation.reason: Refuted as stated (MCP servers crowd the phase window; adopt a loadout policy): most MCP schemas are already deferred, the window is about 1M, and §6 shows tool results fill it, not definitions. A smaller version survives: on high-volume workflow subagents, a whitelisted tool set (as fixflow-explorer already uses) may cut a measured ~64k first-turn prompt that is re-read on every call. Trial it with one /context reading plus one A/B workflow; install nothing.

Adopt a wrap-up threshold only if a phase that passed 40% of its window (about 400k on Fable) shows more reviewer-found defects or reopened boxes than the phases below it; otherwise keep HR-C4 as it stands.

reviews.lens: benefit

reviews.measurement: For the first five phase sessions, log peak context tokens at phase close from transcript usage. Any phase closing above 400k (40% of 1M) is split for its next run and engages HR-C4. Also record whether reviewer reds cluster in the high-context phases. The harness review's own session ran to 971k with nothing lost, so this data decides whether 40% matters here.
reviews.reason: Turns an anecdotal 40% rule into a logged number at no cost, on the very thing HR-C4 already watches.

refutation.counter_evidence:
1) The harness already has this mechanism. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01 §6: HR-C1 is one phase per new session, and HR-C4 is an observation trigger: if a phase session is seen past 500k, set a Fable autoCompactWindow of 500000. SHIP-PLAN §6.6 shows phases are already split so each fits a session (P13e, P5-spike, P5b-1/2, P9-0a/b). The resume machinery in SHIP-PLAN §0 (Plan @ sha, first unticked box, decisions journal per HR-C2) already makes restarting cheap. A 400k split rule (G1-A) would add a second, unevidenced threshold under HR-C4's 500k.
2) The number does not transfer. All five cards date from Aug to Oct 2025, when windows were about 200k, so Dex's 40% was roughly 80k tokens. At Fable's 1M window, 40% is 400k, five times that absolute budget, so "40%" is not the same rule. The cards weaken it further. C1690 concedes newer models are less affected. C1751 is "one 3-hour session, not a benchmark". C1777 says "no measurement of the band is given". C1834 records Dex adding "this doesn't always become true", and his own figure drifted from 50% to 40% while the restart point was ~60%.
3) The mechanism mostly misses this harness. SHIP-PLAN §0 Routing: Fable "briefs, gates and judges; it never implements". Code and reviews come from fresh-context Sonnet and Opus subagents, each with its own CONTEXT block (ORCHESTRATION §5.1). The dumb zone therefore reaches only the main session's gating and judging, not the code that reviewers grade.
4) Both reviewers' measurements are flawed. Comparing reviewer-found defects above and below 400k over 5 phases is confounded: the phases that run long are the hard ones, such as migrations and outbox work, and the defects come from subagents, not from the filled context. G1-B's "/context at close" misses the peak whenever a compaction occurred; per §6, a 971k session compacted to 22k. The peak has to come from the transcript usage fields.
5) Not decisive either way: Q6 (971k, "nothing lost caused a mistake") measures what compaction lost, not reasoning quality at high fill. It does not refute the dumb zone, and it does not support a 40% rule.
refutation.what_would_settle_it:
For the first 5 phase sessions, record two things from the session transcript JSONL (the method §6 already used) in each closing message's "what evidence ran" line.
(a) The main session's peak per-call context: input plus cache-read tokens, the true peak even if the session compacted.
(b) For each owner correction or reviewer reversal of a Fable gating or judging decision logged in the PR's "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections" journal, the token position at which Fable made that decision.

Outcomes:
- If no phase peaks above 400k, the family is moot. Close it as skip and keep HR-C4 unchanged.
- If any phase passes 500k, apply HR-C4 as already written.
- Adopt a "restart from the PR at about 400k" rule only if both hold: at least 2 corrected Fable decisions were made past 400k, and the correction rate per decision past 400k is at least 2x the rate below it.

Do not use reviewer-found code defects as the outcome. Subagents produce the code, so that comparison measures phase difficulty, not context fill.
refutation.reason: Narrowed. The 40% budget is anecdotal, was set on 200k windows, and HR-C1, HR-C4 and the phase sizing already cover its intent. Only a near-free instrument survives: log Fable's peak context and the token position of each corrected Fable decision for 5 phases, to fire HR-C4 and to test whether high fill degrades the judge.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The budget's premise doesn't fit this harness. The 170k "usable" figure and the 7/7/3/10-15% split are Huntley numbers that Dex repeated for Ralph loops on 200k windows in Aug–Oct 2025. All four cards rate them asserted or anecdotal, with no experiment. In HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md §6 the Fable main session first compacted at 971,158 tokens and an idle compaction happened at 580k, so the main window is about 1M, not 170k. (2) The harness already accounts for context by line item, and it measured this rather than asserting it. §6 gives growth per call (about 8k/call over 108 calls in window 1, 10.7k in window 2) and the mix: 68% tool results, 26% Write/Edit payloads and workflow scripts. HR-C1, HR-C2 and HR-C4 already turn that into policy: one phase per session, state kept in the PR body, and a Fable-keyed autoCompactWindow if a phase passes 500k. The dynamic part dominates. The static items are small: CLAUDE.md is 29,605 bytes, about 7.4k tokens (under 1% of 1M), and the whole ship plan is 122,410 bytes, about 30k tokens (about 3%). §0 also only has the plan read in sections ("re-read any changed section"). (3) G1-A's pass criterion is a tautology. "Gives W1's trim a token figure" is already met by `wc -c CLAUDE.md` (29,605 bytes, about 7.4k tokens), with no trial needed. A token figure also can't move W1. W1's harm is adherence falling as instruction count rises, not budget, and the trim is gated on the knowledge-store pilot (KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN), not on cost. If anything, the token figure argues against trimming on budget grounds. (4) What's left of G1-A (record static items in a /context reading) is the sibling F157's measurement. It adds no independent mechanism.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Only to reopen: run /context once at the start of P0a's session and once inside one Sonnet subagent spawned by it. Reopen only if the static items (system prompt, tools/MCP, CLAUDE.md, memory, plan sections read) exceed 10% of the subagent's window, or 5% of Fable's. Otherwise it stays skipped.
refutation.reason: The 170k/percentage budget is an unmeasured Huntley claim for 200k windows. The harness's §6 compaction audit already measured context composition, and HR-C1/C4 act on it. G1-A's "token figure for W1" is a free wc -c fact that cannot affect an adherence-driven trim gated on the pilot.
