refutation.counter_evidence:
The evidence is weak. Both cards are "evidence asserted". C1613 explains its mechanism informally and runs no experiment. C1854 is a rule of thumb about whether to adopt the agent at all, stated by Vaibhav rather than Dex: try it for 10 minutes, and fall back after 30. "Fall back" means a human does the task, which does not transfer here, because Fable "never implements" (SHIP-PLAN §0 Routing, l.55-56). Nothing supports the number "two".

Most of the mechanism already exists. Restarting from the journal is the existing resume path: the draft PR's "Plan @ sha", the first unticked box and the "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections" journal (§0 Resume, l.31-43), plus HR-C1 (HARNESS-REVIEW §6, l.325). Workflow retries already go to fresh agents, with a per-attempt "#retry" label and a two-null circuit breaker (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §4.3, l.205-247). Skeptics and refuters are fresh-context by design (l.543). A path for when the plan itself is wrong also exists: record it in W0-results and amend the plan (SHIP-PLAN l.1552-1553). Only the trigger is missing.

Adopting now is premature. W3 says the routine has never run, so nobody knows how often derailment happens. A restart also cannot fix a defect in the plan or the brief, since a fresh session reads the same text. And a hand_off_to_session fork carries the bad trajectory with it.
refutation.what_would_settle_it:
Put one §0 sentence in force and run it over the first 10 phase sessions, starting at P0a. Each time a box takes two failed corrections in one session, log a firing in the PR-body journal. Corrections can come from the owner to Fable or from Fable to the same implementer. For each firing, record whether the fresh session closed that box with zero further corrections on it.
- Adopt if there are at least 2 firings and at least 2 of every 3 restarts close the box clean.
- If there are fewer than 2 firings, extend the trial to 20 phases. Drop the sentence if there are still 0.
- Also drop it if fewer than half the restarts close the box. That would mean the trouble lies in the brief or the plan, not in the trajectory.
The owner can audit the firings, because the owner is the one making the owner-to-Fable corrections.
refutation.reason: This survives only as a narrow trial. The rule is one §0 sentence (not in CLAUDE.md, so W1 does not grow): after two failed corrections on the same box, commit and push the WIP, write what failed into the journal's "ruled out" section, and resume in a new session rather than a fork. A failed subagent gets a new brief in a fresh agent rather than more messages to the same one. If the box fails a third time after the restart, it goes to the plan-wrong path, not to another restart. Drop C1854's 10/30-minute timebox. The two reviewers split between trial and adopt; I side with trial.

refutation.counter_evidence:
Against the family. The vector in C1727 is a stale global CLAUDE.md, and that vector is missing here: C:/Users/User/.claude/CLAUDE.md does not exist. The evidence is two anecdotes with no numbers (C1682, C1727), so it scores as anecdote. The harness already handles fact drift in three places: (1) P1's CI check fails when CLAUDE.md's Alembic head is wrong and warns on paths that do not resolve, and P13c makes it fatal (SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md lines 365-370); (2) KS-4 plans to correct the inventory's contradictions at their source (KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md line 602), but it is gated behind D1b and not built; (3) HARNESS-REVIEW §6 line 266 adopted "memory file as a pointer" after the memory file carried a stale next step. Skill bodies are loaded on demand, not always loaded, so a pairwise sweep across all 13 SKILL.md files goes beyond the family's own claim. G1-A's rule (a standing pre-phase check after one confirmed hit) costs one Opus run per phase over about 40 phases, which is too much for that bar.

Against the refutation. None of the mechanisms above checks one instruction source against another, and I found a live instance with one grep. CLAUDE.md:366 is always loaded and says "**Start here if you are picking up open work.**", pointing to docs/HANDOFF-2026-07-28-open-work.md and its "unfinished Wave-2 plan". CLAUDE.md never names SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md. Ship plan §0 (lines 24-116) says to resume from its first unticked box and has no rule saying it takes precedence over CLAUDE.md. That is the shape of C1727: an always-loaded pointer steering a session away from the plan. A second risk: MEMORY.md is also always loaded and still states next steps ("next = owner P0a", "owner next: D1"), even though HR adopted "pointers, not state".
refutation.what_would_settle_it:
Run one fresh Opus sweep after the 13 skills land. Scope: CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md and the files it points to, ship plan §0 and ORCHESTRATION §3/§5, plus each SKILL.md (description and body). Check each source against CLAUDE.md and §0 only, not every pair. Each hit must quote both texts and name the different action a fresh agent would take. A fresh refuter then confirms or rejects each hit.

Count the confirmed conflicts that change behaviour, leaving out the one already known (CLAUDE.md:366 vs §0).
- 2 or more: make the sweep a standing check on every PR that edits an instruction source (skills, CLAUDE.md, memory).
- 0 or 1: fix them at source and drop the check.

Separately, in P1's cold-resume trial, record whether the fresh agent's first planning read is HANDOFF-2026-07-28 rather than the ship plan. If it is, that shows the known conflict actually steers.
refutation.reason: Narrowed: run one sweep after the skills land, covering always-loaded and phase-start sources checked against CLAUDE.md and §0, fixing what it finds at source, with no per-phase standing check. The case for it is live: CLAUDE.md:366 points fresh sessions to the July handoff, not the ship plan, and the P1/P13c/KS-4 checks cover fact drift but not one instruction contradicting another.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The idea rests on one mechanism: a "probably ignore this" framing that trigger wording would get past. That framing is missing from the CLAUDE.md wrapper the current harness delivers. In this session the wrapper reads "These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior and you MUST follow them exactly as written". Neither that system-reminder nor the gitStatus/context one ends with the old "this context may or may not be relevant to your tasks" line, so the framing this idea targets is not in what the current harness sends. (2) Evidence: C1622 is a single HN reply from 2025-12-01 with no numbers. That is the "we did this at HumanLayer" kind of anecdote the owner rules downgrade. (3) The harness already uses trigger wording where a trigger matters. Three of the 14 doc-map rows already read as triggers: CLAUDE.md:365 ("Read before touching travel/messaging/consent or adding an outbox kind"), :366 ("Start here if you are picking up open work") and the CODE-MAP row ("start here if unfamiliar"). The pointer that will carry the W1 trim is the KS plan hook in KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md §7.6, and it is already conditional ("Before a session escalates a defect … retries a failed build … or applies a fix that a prose register prescribes, it runs `ks lookup`"). §7.8 then measures compliance with that hook, which covers the "was it consulted" question better than any wording change. The skill format's own convention is "Use when…" descriptions, and every skill listed in this session follows it. The 13 incoming skills inherit that convention, so W4 gains nothing. (4) W1 is about length (390 lines, confirmed with wc -l). Rewording the rows does not shorten the file and may lengthen it. (5) Neither proposed trial can measure the effect. G1-A compares 5 sessions against 5 older transcripts from different phases, and "the trigger condition held" is a judgment call. G1-B reruns the P1 cold-resume trial once (n=1), which cannot separate a wording effect from run-to-run variance. That trial also measures recovery of frozen phase facts, not whether agents open on-demand docs at the right moment.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Open the first turn of one main-session (Fable) phase transcript and check whether the CLAUDE.md system-reminder ends with the "may or may not be relevant to your tasks" trailer. If it does not, the premise is gone. If it does, reopen the narrow version: count, across P1's cold-resume trial, the facts that were missed because the agent did not open a doc-map doc.
refutation.reason: The "probably ignore" framing it targets is missing from the current CLAUDE.md wrapper, the only evidence is one HN anecdote with no numbers, and the harness already uses trigger wording where it matters: doc-map rows 365-366, the KS §7.6 hook, and the "Use when" convention for skills. Rewording the rest does not shorten CLAUDE.md (W1), and neither trial can measure an effect. A row someone edits anyway can take "when X, read Y" wording as a style choice, but that does not justify a trial slot.

reviews.measurement: Within the knowledge-store pilot, move runtime-specific invariants into directory-scoped files: the mobile outbox and client bill-freeze guards to technician-app/CLAUDE.md, the dispatcher, money and lifecycle rules to backend/CLAUDE.md. refutation.counter_evidence:
(1) The harness already has the two cheaper parts of the family. C1639's "index with one-line descriptions" is the CLAUDE.md Doc map (CLAUDE.md:349, "read on demand; this file is the index"). The skills route is W4's 13 skill packages, which another session is adding now. Only directory-scoped CLAUDE.md files would be new.
(2) Directory scoping splits rules that are deliberately cross-runtime. CLAUDE.md:197 is titled "server and client are two halves of one rule" (the bill freeze). CLAUDE.md:179-191 says the backend 409 detail is "regexed by three clients". Split by directory, a backend-only reader loses the client half, which is the cross-half miss behind #162. The alternative is duplicating the rule, which then drifts.
(3) The harness assumes one always-injected file. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §5.1 tells every subagent "CLAUDE.md is already injected; trust it". SHIP-PLAN:415 and :830 brief Opus reviewers "with CLAUDE.md's outbox/location invariants". Fable never implements, so it may never read a file under backend/ and would lose the rules it judges against.
(4) Nested files only auto-load when the Read tool opens a file in that subtree. Here reviewers inspect `git diff`, and in bypass mode agents are told to read with Bash cat/sed. So reviewer A's main reason ("does not rely on the agent following pointers") has not been checked for this harness.
(5) KS design D11 (line 710) and its "wrong baseline" rebuttal (line 765) deliberately trim "only narratives, never rules", because moving rules out "can take knowledge away from sessions that never look up". Reviewer A's trial moves rules, which reopens that ruling, and its reason still holds per (3)-(4).
(6) The only drift gate covers root CLAUDE.md alone: SHIP-PLAN:365-370, the P1 check on the Alembic head and path resolution. Nested files would sit outside it, and C1616 (Dex himself) says sub-context goes stale.
(7) Arithmetic: if only non-invariant single-runtime reference is moved, the root stays at about 330 lines, nowhere near 200. That is the slice list (261-281), the scheduler table (309-328) and the offline table (62-78), about 60 lines. The rest of the roughly 160 runtime-specific lines are invariants caught by (2)-(5).
(8) L2 benefit is negligible: about 390 lines is a few thousand tokens in a one-phase-per-session routine. The evidence is weak too: all four cards are asserted or anecdotal, and KS M-02 [32] (Gloaguen et al.) finds context files raise cost by more than 20% without general success gains.
(9) Restructuring CLAUDE.md before P1's cold-resume trial would confound the routine's first test (W3).
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run this only if the idea is reopened at KS-7. In a scratch worktree, put a one-line sentinel rule in backend/CLAUDE.md. Spawn 4 workflow subagents on one backend diff task: 2 that inspect only through `git diff`/Bash cat, and 2 that use the Read tool. Count how many quote the sentinel. If the Bash-only agents do not reach 2/2, nested auto-load cannot carry invariants in this harness and the skip is final.
refutation.reason: The harness already has the index (Doc map) and skills (W4). Directory-scoped files would split cross-runtime rules (bill freeze, 409 string) and break the "CLAUDE.md is already injected" briefs. Auto-loading them is unverified for Bash/git-diff reviewers. KS D11 deliberately keeps rules in the root. The safe remainder trims only ~60 lines, so B's skip stands.

C1621 (G1-cards.md:2761-2767) is a set of HN commenters (sothatsit, Sammi, ffsm8, vunderba, dimitri-vs) with no counts, so under the owner rules it scores as a claim. (2) G1-B's measurement can only return zero. SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md:322-327 says the P1 cold-resume agent is given "only the repository and 'read SHIP-PLAN §0 and P1'", and the ten frozen facts are "about this phase from the plan". The prompt names the documents directly, and CLAUDE.md has no SHIP-PLAN or docs/program row (grep finds nothing). So no frozen fact sits "behind a CLAUDE.md doc-map pointer", the count is 0 by construction, and the "0 ⇒ pointers stand" branch would wrongly clear the pointers. (3) The harness already has what the family recommends. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:440 and E-10 (:177) route store access through a project skill (`.claude/skills/knowledge-store/SKILL.md`) instead of a prose pointer. :13 and :648 keep every rule in CLAUDE.md and move out only the case narratives of verified entries, as "one-line rule + (ks <id>)", so a pointer that is never followed loses a story, not a rule. sample_quote: "It seems to be 50/50 or LESS that Claude.md even reads/uses this file." (C1630)
landing_guesses: External check for routine steps

reviews.lens: Cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is reopened and still holds, what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build, run and keep honest.
reviews.existing_mechanism: CI gates, SHA-bound Opus reviewer, P1 cold-resume trial
reviews.reopens_skipped: Pre-commit verification hook skip ('RT-04/05 defects; CI gates the PRs'); two HN anecdotes in opposite directions are no reason to reopen it
reviews.reason: External checks exist where it matters; contested anecdotes do not justify hooks.

reviews.lens: benefit
reviews.measurement: Add a CI step (not a pre-commit hook) that fails a phase PR whose body lacks the 'Plan @ <sha>' first line, the Scope checklist or the journal heading. Over the first 5 phase PRs, count real catches and false fails; keep it if there is at least one catch and no false fail.
reviews.reason: Gives W2 an external compliance signal; it fits the skip reason 'CI gates the PRs' rather than reopening the pre-commit hook.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The only card, C1630 (G1-cards.md line 2817), is one HN thread with two anecdotes that point opposite ways and carry no numbers: saberience says "50/50 or LESS", AndyNemmity says a large targeted file works. The owner's rules treat that as anecdote. The thread is also about CLAUDE.md adherence, but the phase routine lives in SHIP-PLAN §0 (lines 24-56), not in CLAUDE.md, so it does not test routine compliance directly. 2) The family's principle is already in the harness. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN §7.8 is titled "Compliance is measured, not assumed": critic K24, the KS-O11 lookup is a named step of the Opus review, and line 833 records that compliance is self-reported. SHIP-PLAN §0 Routing (lines 51-55) ties the reviewer's verdict to the PR head SHA, with fail-before/pass-after per register id. HARNESS-REVIEW line 268 makes the P1 cold-resume trial an external test of the routine. 3) The W1 half has nothing to adopt. Contradictory anecdotes give the trim no direction, and the trim is already gated behind the store pilot (KS §8 / KS-7). 4) G1-B says this reopens a deliberate skip, which is wrong for G1-A's mechanism. HARNESS-REVIEW line 272 skips the pre-commit hook because "CI gates the PRs", and a CI check of the PR body fits that reason. 5) Nothing in the harness does this today. .github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on pull_request with the default types (no `edited`) and never reads the PR body; deploy.yml is the only other workflow. 6) Limits on the benefit. The check sees only whether the three elements are present: a bare heading passes it, and it cannot show that the journal was appended live or that the `git diff <sha>..origin/main` was run on resume. Operations phases keep their Plan @ line in W0-results.md, not in a PR body, so they fall outside it. The routine has never run (W3), so how often these elements go missing is unknown. 7) Constraint on how to build it: the check must not go into ci.yml. That file has `concurrency: ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true`, so adding `edited` there would cancel and restart all three gate jobs on every `gh pr edit` journal append. It needs its own workflow file (the same pattern as KS D6), with the body passed through env rather than inline `${{ }}` interpolation.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run it over the first 5 code-phase PRs, from P1 on. A separate workflow (pull_request types opened/edited/synchronize/ready_for_review, limited to phase PRs by a label, body passed through env) checks three things: line 1 matches ^Plan @ [0-9a-f]{7,40}$, the body has at least one task-list item, and the "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections" heading is present. Count real catches: any run before merge where an element is missing, confirmed by reading the body. Count false fails: a red run on a compliant body or on a non-phase PR. Keep it as a required check if there is at least 1 catch and 0 false fails. Drop it if there are 0 catches in 5. A zero-build version gives the same count: run `gh pr view <n> --json body` on each of the 5 PRs when the reviewer is dispatched and again at merge.
refutation.reason: The card's evidence is two contradictory anecdotes about CLAUDE.md, not about the plan routine, and "compliance is measured, not assumed" already exists (KS §7.8, the SHA-bound reviewer, the P1 trial). Only G1-A's narrow CI check of the PR body's structure survives, run as a separate workflow and trialled over 5 PRs; the W1 claim does not.

Pass condition: if CLAUDE.md + skills exceed 15k tokens or 5% of the first-turn context, the W1 trim gets a cost figure as well as an adherence argument; otherwise record that W1 is about adherence, not budget, and close the idea.

reviews.lens: Cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is being reopened, what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build and keep honest, and what can go wrong.
reviews.existing_mechanism: HARNESS-REVIEW §6 compaction audit measured per-call growth from the transcript (about 8k tokens per call, 68% tool results), but nothing measures the fixed prefix (system prompt, tool schemas, CLAUDE.md, skill listings)
reviews.reopens_skipped: Brushes the skipped M00-M06 measurement pipeline ('no gain; owner priority low'). That skip still holds for a pipeline, but a one-off native reading is not a pipeline.
reviews.measurement: Run Claude Code's built-in /context once in a fresh phase session before and after the 13 skills land, and once after any W1 trim. Record the tokens for CLAUDE.md, tool schemas and skills in the W0-results evidence folder. Act only if CLAUDE.md plus skills are 10% or more of the pre-message prefix. No proxy: on Windows it means a TLS-intercepting proxy that sees auth headers.
reviews.reason: The question (what does the fixed prefix cost?) is worth one native reading that costs nothing; the proxy method is not worth its risk.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) Both reviews rest on "nothing has measured the fixed prefix", and that is wrong for the part W1 is about. CLAUDE.md's cost is already on record: ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md lines 90 and 583 give "fixed overhead per agent (CLAUDE.md ≈ 7.5k tokens + CONTEXT)". KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md line 59 says it is "injected into every agent at about 7.5k tokens" and that every new entry adds to every agent's fixed overhead. Line 185 of the same file already gives W1 a cost argument backed by evidence: Gloaguen et al. find repository context files raise cost by more than 20% without general success gains. `wc` today: 390 lines, 29,605 bytes, about 7.4k tokens, which matches. 2) The pass thresholds both reviewers propose are settled in advance by that number. G1-A's "5% of first-turn context" is met by CLAUDE.md alone unless the prefix is over about 150k tokens. G1-B's "10% of the prefix" is met unless the prefix is over about 75k. So the reading would always "pass" and tells nothing new. 3) For L2, HARNESS-REVIEW §6 (lines 66-73 and 316-317) already broke down where the budget goes. Growth was about 8k tokens per call over 108 calls (68% tool results, 26% Write/Edit payloads), and compaction came at 971k. A cached prefix of tens of thousands of tokens is a few percent of that, and its CLAUDE.md share is less than one call's growth. HR-C1 (one phase per session) is the defence, and a smaller prefix changes nothing about it. 4) W1 is framed as an adherence problem, and its trim is gated behind the knowledge-store pilot. A token share changes neither the adherence argument nor the gate. 5) For W2, a trace of the request body shows what was loaded, not whether the routine was followed. CLAUDE.md is always loaded, and §6 already audited tool calls from the transcript. 6) The proxy method itself means a TLS-intercepting proxy on Windows that sees auth headers. Both reviewers already rejected it. The card (C1843) is a demonstration trace with no token counts and no claim of an outcome, so the evidence behind any benefit is nil.
refutation.reason: The useful part, a token figure for CLAUDE.md, is already recorded at about 7.5k tokens in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN (lines 90 and 583) and KS-DESIGN line 59, and §6 already measured where context growth goes. The remaining split between system prompt, tools and skills feeds no decision: both proposed thresholds are settled by arithmetic, and the proxy method is unsafe, so skip that part.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The harness already does program design where it matters, so G2-A's premise ("design notes cover architecture, not code shape") is wrong. On origin/docs/orchestration-design-2026-10, O-07-design.md fixes file placement (a new slice backend/app/features/accounting/ laid out router → service → repository with models, schemas and tests). Its §4 gives a typed seam with signatures: `core/posting_transport.py: async Protocol PostingTransport { name; async find(external_id) -> RemoteRef|None; async push(snapshot) -> RemoteRef }`, plus typed DefinitiveTransportError, AmbiguousTransportError and TransportAuthError and a fake transport. O-10-design.md D4 fixes where the code goes and how it is gated (an index.ts import placed before the task bodies, plus a gate promise every sync awaits) and names the test files (manifest.test, unpark.test, drainAll.test). SHIP-PLAN P10a's Scope names the "transport seam" and the functions to build. 2) Code shape is also enforced mechanically: CLAUDE.md requires the slice layout, import-linter and ESLint no-restricted-imports enforce boundaries in CI, and dependency-cruiser is planned for mobile (P5b-2). 3) SHIP-PLAN §0 Routing already covers who designs: Opus owns all invariant-sensitive code, and Sonnet implements only "well-specified" work "from a design's test list". 4) The evidence is all anecdotal with no numbers (C0504, C0505, C0980, C0887). Two members are sales channels: C0537 promotes HumanLayer's own show-me skill, and in C0560 Ondrej sells a program-design bundle. 5) It does nothing for its named weaknesses. A new pre-code gate does not test the routine (W3), and adding it before the routine's first run muddies the P1 trial. It is not a verifier (L3), and it is not a reusable workflow (W4). 6) G2-A's trial measurement is biased toward zero. The Opus reviewer's brief tells it to refute named register ids, not to judge interface shape, so counting its "shape findings" would undercount the very defect the trial is meant to detect.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Reopen check, not a trial. Over P1-P3, count the PRs Sonnet implemented, and in each count the rework commits after first review whose stated cause is interface, signature or file placement (not logic). These come from the PR journal and the commit messages, not from the register-id reviewer. Reopen only if at least 2 of those PRs each have at least 2 such rework commits, and then only for Sonnet phases whose design note has no signature-level section.
refutation.reason: The design notes for invariant code already reach signatures, seams, file placement and named tests, and CI enforces the slice layout. The leftover gap is Sonnet's "well-specified" work, and the only support for closing it is vendor anecdote. Adding a fourth gate before the routine has run once would muddy W3. Skip, and re-check with the rework count after P3.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The harness already has the anti-steering mechanism, and it is enforced by schema, not by a prompt rule. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §5.1 RULES say "Return constants, lines and declared names; never a severity or a verdict unless your schema has that field". Line 544 says "Mappers return constants, lines and names; the hypotheses tag routes, it does not judge". In §5.2 the anomalies field is "neutral, evidenced, no severity". That is Dex's own goal ("a good research is mostly facts", C1120), with output typing doing the work that hiding the ticket does for him. The §5.1 CONTEXT block carries program-level goals and settled facts, not a per-task intended change, so G2-A's premise is weak. 2) Verifiers already get blinded input. §4.6.2 and line 543 say "Skeptics get the claim, its evidence and its failing condition only, in a fresh context — not the analyst's reasoning". Line 309 adds a rival-hypothesis lens (the O-01 skeptic must explain the symptom with app-logic causes alone). Refuters have to see the claim, and the bias toward confirming is countered by the default-refute verdict rules. 3) The landing on the cold-resume trial is backwards. SHIP-PLAN P1 (lines 322-326) gives the fresh Sonnet agent only the repository and "read SHIP-PLAN §0 and P1". The plan is the thing under test, so hiding it defeats the trial, and giving the agent questions would leak which ten facts are wanted. 4) No target remains. HARNESS-REVIEW Q3 (line 47) says "discovery is the phase this program has finished". The 40 phases carry out Scope already written from register ids, so there is no question-then-research step ahead of design. That means G2-A's measurement ("the next two discovery tasks") may never run. 5) The knowledge-store pilot already replays raw symptoms blind (KS design line 45). 6) The evidence is weak. All six cards are "asserted" or "anecdotal": one author's prompt rule repeated across his own skill packs, with no numbers. Out-of-family note for the W3 owner: P1 commits expected.json (the answer key) into the repository the blind agent reads. That is the real blinding gap in the trial. Fix it by committing only its sha256, or by checking out the agent's copy before that commit.
refutation.reason: The harness already gets the same effect: mappers are schema-bound to facts, skeptics see only the claim, and the cold-resume agent gets no hints. Discovery is finished, and the evidence is one author's anecdote. G2-A's paired trial is degenerate: the schemas already forbid opinions, and n=2 cannot separate refutation rates.

reviews.measurement: In the first three phase reviews, every register id's fail-before/pass-after line cites the command run and its observed exit/output, and a test that was only read is marked 'read, not run'.
reviews.reason: One line in the reviewer brief turns asserted verification into a cited command and its result. That directly narrows W2's self-report gap.

refutation.counter_evidence: Two of the three cards are already covered, and all three are asserted or anecdotal. C0216 (verify by running a derivation) is already planned: SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md lines 365-366 have P1 add a CI step that fails when CLAUDE.md's Alembic head differs from the down_revision chain head. C0223 (check the stored DB state) is already the practice: CLAUDE.md says authorization is tested in pytest against real Postgres, the deploy-train table has a post-deploy check column (SHIP-PLAN line 77), and the drain has an AFTER check (Standing rule 1). The broad principle is also already harness doctrine. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN lines 114-115 make Stage-1 agents return 'commands and exit codes'. Line 218 makes command agents return output tails plus exit codes. Line 782 says the result is the GATE lines, 'not the exit code of an echo'. The closing message reports 'what evidence ran (incl. skipped counts)' (SHIP-PLAN lines 44-45). The pass-after half needs no new rule: a phase is not done until CI is green on the PR (lines 59-60). One gap is real: the reviewer only has to 'name the test that fails on the base commit' (lines 54-55). Nothing asks the reviewer to show it ran that test on base, so a test the reviewer only read looks the same as one it ran. No hook exists, so a cited output is still self-reported. The W2 benefit is therefore only partial.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: How we'd know it worked: check the first three phase PRs. Every register id's fail-before line should either give the command, the base SHA and the observed failing output (or a log path in the evidence folder), or be marked 'read, not run'. Zero bare 'test X fails on base' assertions. In each of those PRs, Fable re-runs one cited fail-before command on the base SHA. Pass if it reproduces the cited failure in 3 of 3 PRs. Any reproduction that fails, or any bare assertion, means the line alone is not enough. The fix then is to require the logs in the evidence folder under its sha256 manifest.
refutation.reason: Narrowed: C0216 is already planned (P1's CI head check) and C0223 is already practice (integration tests against real Postgres, post-deploy checks). The pass-after half is already proven by CI being green on the PR. What survives is one clause in the §0 reviewer brief: each fail-before line cites the command run on the base SHA and its observed result, or is marked 'read, not run'. It costs almost nothing and makes that claim checkable, but it is not hook-enforced.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The external evidence is only asserted. In the rpi repo, the 'document-precedence' and 'latest-user-direction' tests check that HumanLayer's own prompt obeys its own order on a toy cap value (1000 vs 2000). They give no error-rate data. The need comes from this harness, not from the source. (2) The harness already has precedence rules, scattered across files: the CLAUDE.md header ("When this file and a prose doc disagree, this file + the code win"); ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §5.1 CONTEXT block, line 367 ("CLAUDE.md is already injected; trust it"); SHIP-PLAN §2, line 130 ("the Entry line wins if they ever disagree"); and §0 standing rule 5, line 110, which voids the O-08 §4 "503 stub" line inline. §0 lines 36-43 already make the PR journal the home of owner corrections, and the resume step already re-reads changed plan sections. "The user's latest instruction overrides all" is already how chat works, and it gives a cold resume nothing; the journal is what carries corrections across sessions. (3) G2-A's order (owner > journal > Plan @ sha > CLAUDE.md > design note) contradicts two always-present rules: CLAUDE.md's supremacy line (the ship plan is a prose doc under docs/) and the §5.1 instruction "trust it". It would create a conflict between precedence rules. (4) HumanLayer's "most recent wins" relies on a linear chain: ticket, research, design, outline, plan. FixFlow's documents are not linear. CLAUDE.md records the current state (Railway, manual `railway up`), while the plan records the intended state (a VPS host from P3 on). A flat order or "latest wins" therefore gives the wrong answer in one direction or the other. (5) There is a real divergence today that neither reviewer's order settles. SHIP-PLAN §0, lines 86-88, always requires VALIDATE in a later migration after an audit script has run, and cites CLAUDE.md for this. CLAUDE.md itself allows the same migration when the column is provably clean. G2-B's split ("CLAUDE.md over prose for stack facts") would pick the looser rule. A clause saying the stricter rule applies is needed. (6) The benefit on W2 does not exist: a precedence sentence does not make compliance observable. G2-B's measurement (no journal entry records a conflict settled ad hoc) depends on self-report, because a conflict settled silently leaves no entry.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Adopt; the check that it worked uses the P1 cold-resume trial. Plant two conflicts in its frozen fact set: (a) an owner correction in the PR journal that contradicts the Plan @ sha text, and (b) the VALIDATE rule, where the plan is stricter than CLAUDE.md. The fresh Sonnet agent passes if it reports the journal's value and the stricter rule and cites the §0 sentence, 2 of 2. Without planted conflicts, natural ones may never come up and the trial would show nothing. Then, for P1-P3, add one item to each Opus PR-reviewer brief: list every disagreement the diff touches between the plan, CLAUDE.md, the cited design note and the journal, and state whether its resolution follows §0. The threshold is 0 mismatches over the three phases.

refutation.counter_evidence: Against the family as stated, a pointer injected into every session or prompt: (1) HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md line 274 skips a SessionStart hook that prints the resume pointer, with the exact JSON held as HR-C5 (lines 330-336). No .claude/settings.json exists. Injecting on every session or prompt needs that same hook, and the reason for the skip (one phase per session) still holds. (2) The main session already gets this pointer. MEMORY.md is always loaded, and project-fixflow-ship-plan.md line 13 says "State lives in the repo... Read SHIP-PLAN header + §0, the current phase section". (3) The pointer does nothing for W3's named test. SHIP-PLAN P1 Entry (lines 322-326) already tells the trial agent to "read SHIP-PLAN §0 and P1". G2-A's check (SHIP-PLAN §0 among the first five reads) therefore passes by construction and cannot show any effect of the pointer. (4) The evidence is only asserted or marketing material (C0113, C0271 and C0302 describe injected text, with no data). HumanLayer's observability comes from cloud sync that follows tool calls (C0114), not from the pointer, so the W2 benefit is illusory. Adding text to CLAUDE.md does not help W1 and makes it slightly worse. Against G2-B's already-done: memory lives outside the repository. PR #182's CLAUDE.md (git show FETCH_HEAD: 390 lines, no diff from HEAD) still labels docs/HANDOFF-2026-07-28-open-work.md "Start here if you are picking up open work" at line 366, and has no SHIP-PLAN row. SHIP-PLAN line 567 schedules only a generic "doc map updated" in a later deploy phase. So an agent that has only the repository is pointed at the July hand-off, even though the plan's own goal is to be derivable from the repo alone.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: What would show the adopt worked: build the post-change commit (the row moved). Give a fresh Sonnet agent only the repository and a neutral prompt that names no file ("pick up the open program work"). It passes if, in 3 of 3 runs, the agent opens docs/program/SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §0 before docs/HANDOFF-2026-07-28-open-work.md. Run the same prompt 3 times on the pre-change commit as the baseline, where the expected result is HANDOFF first. That is 6 cheap runs, and they can be added to P1's trial as a variant. Do not use the trial's own prompt, because it already names §0.
refutation.reason: The per-session or per-prompt injection is refuted: it re-adopts the HR-C5 SessionStart skip, the main session already gets the pointer from auto-memory, the P1 trial prompt already names §0, the evidence is marketing only, and the W2 benefit is illusory. refutation.counter_evidence:
(1) The evidence is weak. All 7 cards are marketing, asserted or anecdotal, and none gives a number. C0270 (humanlayer-pi) is an alpha cloud mirror built for the pi agent, not Claude Code. It uploads tool calls and repo diffs to a third party. C0280's queryable run store is specific to BAML, and building one rebuilds the skipped "Measurement pipeline M00–M06; evaluation-run schema" (HARNESS-REVIEW §4 skip table, line 275). C0242's steering count per PR is a team factory metric, and here the one developer is the only steerer. So the "externally mirror" and "run store" halves are refuted.
(2) Most §0 acts already leave durable artifacts outside the agent, so a transcript is the wrong source for them. SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 24-60 list them: the draft PR at the first commit (PR createdAt can be compared with the first commit), the "Plan @ <sha>" first line, the journal kept with `gh pr edit` (GitHub keeps the edit history), the OWNER-VIEW.md refresh commit, the reviewer verdict naming the head SHA, and docs/program/evidence/resume-trial-P1/ with its sha256 manifest. All of these can be checked with gh and git.
(3) There is precedent: HARNESS-REVIEW §6 already audited its own session transcript by line number (lines 1944 and 2735).
(4) The data exists and greps work. ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl records each tool_use: one session had Bash 498, Edit 207 and Workflow 44 calls, plus 11 `gh pr edit` hits. There are 1681 subagent JSONL files under subagents/. But there are 5 separate EMS-workshop1* slug directories, one per worktree. cleanupPeriodDays is unset, so the default 30-day prune applies, and the oldest transcript left on the machine is from 2026-10-26. The audit must therefore run soon after each phase closes and glob every slug directory.
(5) The reviewers' tests are flawed. G2-A's "any mismatch → adopt" is one-sided. Both reviewers compare against the closing message's claims, but its six questions claim almost none of the §0 acts, so there is little to compare.
The M00–M06 skip reason ("no gain") was about measuring effect, not checking compliance. A one-off grep with nothing installed therefore does not re-adopt that skip.
refutation.reason: Narrowed. The external mirror and queryable run store are refuted: marketing evidence, a cloud upload, and a rebuild of the skipped M00–M06. What survives is a trial of one local transcript grep after each phase closes. It covers only the routine acts git and GitHub cannot show, chiefly "Fable never implements", the reviewer brief's SHA and register ids, and the cold-resume dispatch. It is the one W2 check that reads the harness's own record rather than the agent's report.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) Transcripts on this machine are already filed by worktree. C:/Users/User/.claude/projects/C--Users-User-Documents-projects-EMS-workshop1--claude-worktrees-harness-ideas-horthy-2371b9/ holds one session, 9c3f9742-d1e5-4e7b-ad89-bb5bcaada06a.jsonl. That matches the branch claude/harness-ideas-horthy-2371b9 and the session uuid in the scratchpad path. So for a phase run in one session in one worktree, the PR's head branch already finds the transcript, with nothing added. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §7 (~line 586) already relies on .claude/projects/<proj>/<session>/ for resume. (2) Retention defeats a bare link. ~/.claude/settings.json sets no cleanupPeriodDays, and no transcript on this machine is older than 2026-10-26 (50 files: 23 from October, 27 from November), even though the project's history goes back further. A 40-phase plan will leave links pointing at deleted .jsonl files unless the owner decides how transcripts are kept. Committing transcripts into the evidence folder would risk leaking secrets. (3) The repo squash-merges (SHIP-PLAN §0 line 68), so per-commit trailers get folded away. The only durable place is the PR body journal, which already exists (§0 lines 36-43). That makes a separate trailer or hidden-comment mechanism redundant. (4) C0154 depends on a HumanLayer daemon that sets HUMANLAYER_SESSION_URL, and this harness has no such daemon. C1165 is anecdotal, and in it Dex says no one reads every session. (5) The link alone says nothing about W2. Its only value is as the join key for reading the transcript (F023). KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN lines 248 and 549/768 already record actor_session provenance on store events. That design notes the ids are self-declared and already defers binding them to transcripts. So 'the store was never consulted' belongs to the store's own log, not to a PR link.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run this with the F023 trial over the first 3 phase PRs that close, with the audit done at least 7 days after each close. For each PR, record three things. (a) Was the transcript found from the head branch, through its worktree folder, alone? (b) Did the PR journal's 'Sessions:' line find every session of the phase? (c) Were all of the phase's .jsonl files still on disk at audit time? Keep the line only if two things hold: (c) is 3/3, and at least one phase was resumed, ran several sessions, or renamed its branch, so (a) failed while (b) found all its sessions. If (a) is 3/3, drop the line as redundant. If (c) is below 3/3, the link is moot until the owner decides retention (raise cleanupPeriodDays, or export outside git). If F023 fails, drop this too.
refutation.reason: Only a much smaller version survives. Skip the trailer, the hidden comment and the deep link. Branch→worktree folder already finds the transcript of a one-session phase, and squash-merge folds trailers away. What is left: one plain 'Sessions: <uuid>…' line in the existing PR journal, copied from the scratchpad path and never invented. It earns its place only for resumed or multi-session phases, and only if transcripts are kept beyond the default cleanup. Trial it alongside F023 or not at all.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) C1252's point is the hook form: hooks can apply more expressive, input-value rules than permissions do. Its landing guess, "deny railway up from the repo root", depends on the working directory, which only a PreToolUse hook can see. That reopens the skipped hook category, and HR §6 HR-C5 already flags hook-shell risk on Windows (whether `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` expands). Both reviewers quietly switched to plain `permissions.deny`, which is a default Claude Code feature, not the family's claim. (2) G2-B's "prod-targeted alembic upgrade" cannot be written as a prefix rule. `alembic upgrade head && alembic check` is a gate command (CLAUDE.md Commands; SHIP-PLAN Appendix A backend gates). The prod target comes from the environment, and after P3 `start.sh` applies migrations at deploy. A deny on `alembic upgrade` would block the gate. (3) SHIP-PLAN §0 L61-81: from P3, prod is a VPS deployed by runbook R5 ("owner at SSH"). Railway keeps only the old-hostname hang stub (L519, L636). So a `railway up` rule guards the drain-window stub, and the backend only until P3. The SSH deploy path is not covered at all. (4) The harness has two shell tools, Bash and PowerShell. A `Bash(...)` rule does not gate the PowerShell tool, and nobody has verified a PowerShell rule form. Prefix rules can also be evaded with `npx @railway/cli up`, `bash -c` or `cmd /c`. That makes this a seatbelt against mistakes, not a control. (5) Zero bearing on W2: it makes no phase-routine step observable. (6) C0717's email incident has no counterpart an agent can reach here: the WhatsApp send is server-side, behind `enable_dispatcher`. Its evidence is a single anecdote. (7) G2-A's success metric ("zero such commands executed") would read zero without the rule too, so it cannot be falsified. Supporting the narrowed form: no `.claude/settings.json` exists in the repo or the main checkout, and the user settings hold no permissions, so nothing already does this. HANDOFF L59-63 shows that sessions have run `railway up --ci` and that a repo-root deploy caused a prod outage. This is local evidence, stronger than Horthy's anecdotes.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Acceptance test, run once before calling it adopted. Put the deny block in the project `.claude/settings.json` and run in the same permission mode the workflow subagents use (bypassPermissions). Have an agent attempt four commands: `railway up --ci` via Bash, `cd backend && railway up --ci --service efficient-tenderness` via Bash, `railway up` via the PowerShell tool, and `railway run alembic current` via Bash. It passes when all four are refused by the deny rule and the full backend, web and mobile gate lists (including `alembic upgrade head && alembic check`) run with nothing blocked. If the PowerShell attempt is not refused, add the PowerShell rule form or record the gap in the PR. Then, across P1-P3, count gate commands falsely blocked by the rule. The threshold is 0. It has worked when the four attempts are refused and the false-block count stays at 0.
refutation.reason: Narrowed. What survives is not a hook and not an alembic rule: a single `permissions.deny` block with Bash and PowerShell forms of `railway up` and `railway run` (optionally `git push --force`). It cheaply makes a locally recorded outage trap mechanical, which still matters for the Railway stub during the drain window. It does nothing for W2.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) Both reviewers' landing ("named /phase-start and /phase-close skills") duplicates a skill that already exists. The fixflow-orchestration skill (.claude/worktrees/wizardly-hertz-02c46a/.claude/skills/fixflow-orchestration/SKILL.md, commit 1ac6b15, 371 lines) has the description "Use it at the start of every ship-plan phase session (P0a..P14-fleet)". It carries §0 as numbered steps: 2-3 resume (gh pr view, first unticked box, Plan @ <sha> diff), 26 draft PR at first commit, and 35 Close (six questions, OWNER-VIEW refresh, journal entries moved to their owners). fixflow-repo-conventions step 14 repeats the close. Claude Code can invoke every skill by slash command, so /fixflow-orchestration already is /phase-start. (2) The evidence is anecdotal. C1272 says "Personal experience across skills; no counts", and C1268's demo is a trivial secret-passcode skill. That slash invocation loads a skill deterministically is documented tool behaviour that needs neither card. (3) The W2 benefit is mostly illusory. Explicit invocation shows that the instructions were loaded, not that they were followed. The §0 acts the reviewers would count are already visible from outside without any skill: draft PR timing and the Plan @ line and journal (gh pr view), the OWNER-VIEW.md commit (git log), and the closing message (transcript). The part that really is self-reported (store consulted, fail-before/pass-after actually run) is not touched by invocation. (4) Neither measurement can attribute an effect. G2-A compares against "the prose-only routine on the first phase run", which does not exist because the routine has never run (W3). G2-B's 3/3 has no control.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Over the first 3 phase sessions, the owner opens with the plain phase prompt and no slash command. From the session transcripts (search for a Skill call to fixflow-orchestration), count the sessions in which Fable loads the skill before its first subagent brief or first commit. The owner may intervene after turn 1 if it has not loaded. If 3/3 sessions auto-load, the description match is enough and no convention is needed. If 2/3 or fewer do, make an explicit `/fixflow-orchestration` the first line of every phase prompt, plus an explicit close prompt naming step 35. Whatever the result, judge close compliance in each session from artifacts, not from invocation: the PR body has the Plan @ line, the journal entries were moved, the closing message has all six answers, and an OWNER-VIEW.md commit exists. Pass is all present in 3/3.
refutation.reason: Narrowed: no new /phase-start or /phase-close skills, because fixflow-orchestration (steps 2-3, 26, 35) and fixflow-repo-conventions (step 14) already encode §0 and are already slash-invocable. What survives is a zero-cost habit: invoke /fixflow-orchestration explicitly at phase start, and prompt the close step explicitly, instead of relying on the description match. It guarantees the instructions are loaded, not that they are followed, so it does little for W2; compliance is still checked from the PR and git artifacts.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) Evidence: C1273 (G2-cards.md line 2622) says the only basis is that the claim was "Relayed from a conversation with Jeff ... informal". It names no model, no window size and no count. Under the owner rules that makes it anecdotal, and both reviewers scored evidence 1. (2) The harness already does the variant G2-A proposes, a fixed token at the end of the closing message. SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §0 (Resume bullet) requires every phase's closing message to answer six fixed questions: goal, fit, choice, before/after, evidence including skipped counts, and what remains. It then refreshes OWNER-VIEW.md. Fable reads that instruction at phase start, carries it out only at the end, and the owner can see whether it was followed. It is already an end-of-session canary, and a more relevant one than a passcode because it is part of the routine itself. HR-2026-11-01 §4 line 262 adopted it. (3) A per-turn canary is self-reinforcing. After N replies that end with the token, the model can keep producing it by copying its own recent output rather than by still obeying an instruction from early in the context. A hit therefore tells you little, and only a miss is informative. (4) W2: the passcode tests whether one trivial, salient instruction is still followed. It does not test whether the routine was followed or whether the store was consulted. The routine already leaves outside-checkable artifacts under SHIP-PLAN §0: the "Plan @ <sha>" first line, the draft-PR checkbox list, the Decisions/ruled out journal, a reviewer verdict that names the head SHA, and the OWNER-VIEW.md diff. (5) W1: a canary measured at one CLAUDE.md length cannot show whether the length hurts adherence. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN M-02 already records that adherence falls past about 200 lines, and the trim stays gated on the pilot. Putting the canary in CLAUDE.md lengthens that file. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md lines 90 and 583 say CLAUDE.md (about 7.5k tokens) is injected into every subagent, so the instruction would reach every workflow agent. (6) L2: HR §6 already settles the response. HR-C1 runs one phase per session, and HR-C4 sets an objective trigger: act if a phase session is observed past 500k. For the 1M-window sessions in this repo, 60% is about 600k, which is past that trigger. Below it, a canary that never misses cannot tell "no decay" from "never reached the decay zone".
refutation.what_would_settle_it: The only open question is whether instruction decay starts below HR-C4's 500k trigger. Do not test it with a new instruction. Use the close the routine already has. At each phase close from P1 to P3, record the session's context fill (from /context or the transcript usage fields) next to a pass/fail grade of five things: the six-question close, the "Plan @ sha" line, the journal entries, the ticked boxes and the OWNER-VIEW.md refresh. Reopen a canary only if at least one session fails that grade while its fill is below 500k. Otherwise HR-C1 and HR-C4 already cover the case.
refutation.reason: G2-A proposed a fixed token at the end of the closing message. That duplicates SHIP-PLAN §0's six-question close, which is already an early-loaded, late-checked, visible test of instruction-following. A per-turn canary is weaker: the model can keep it alive by copying its own earlier replies. It also does not measure whether the routine was followed (W2) or whether length hurts adherence (W1), and placed in CLAUDE.md it would make that file longer and reach every subagent. Its only support is an informal demo relayed second-hand, so the G2-B skip stands.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The evidence is weak. In G2-cards.md, C1117 is marked "asserted": a lesson stated in a talk, with no numbers, and the claim that a smaller model then suffices is never measured. C0402 is marked "anecdotal": a blog blurb about rolling out to hundreds of engineers, with no outcome figures. Under the owner rules, neither counts as evidence. (2) The principle is already in place wherever this harness has multi-agent control flow. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md puts that control flow in script code, not prose: slices of five, a circuit breaker, a HALT path and resume replay at lines 205-207, plus a script contract and typed schemas at line 817. Workflow scripts are also committed rather than lost, at docs/program/evidence/harness-ideas/horthy/workflows/*.js.txt (three sweeps) and tools/*.mjs.txt. So "not saved" is only half true: they are kept as evidence, not as a library. (3) A driver for a whole phase would collide with a ruling already made. HARNESS-REVIEW §4 (lines 254, 270-271) read the clinic's workflow CLI and task tree and skipped the task.md state tree and Python checkpoint resume, because "FixFlow already has one owner per kind of state". A phase driver that tracks progress through the steps would become a second owner of the draft-PR checklist, which SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 31-46 makes the resume authority. (4) This does not solve W2. With no hooks (no .claude/settings.json exists; .claude/ holds only launch.json), whether Fable ran the script is still self-reported. Meanwhile, the routine in SHIP-PLAN §0 already leaves artifacts anyone can check from outside: the "Plan @ <sha>" first line, the checkbox list, the journal with a destination for each entry, a reviewer verdict bound to the head SHA with fail-before/pass-after for each id (lines 51-55), and the OWNER-VIEW.md commit. (5) W3 makes it premature. The routine has never run, and P1's cold-resume trial (HR §4 line 268) is its first test. Scripting it now would freeze guesses about where it fails. (6) Phases are mixed: code, operations and repeatable (×n) phases, with steps that need the owner in the loop (starting Docker, an SSH deploy, phone drains, §0 lines 26-60). A general driver would have to branch on human events it cannot see.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: After each of the first three phases to close (P1 and the next two), a Haiku extractor reads the merged PR body, git log and closing message. It counts which of six mechanical close steps were omitted: (a) first line "Plan @ <sha>"; (b) every journal entry names where it was moved; (c) OWNER-VIEW.md changed at close; (d) the reviewer verdict names the merged head SHA, or a re-read of the diff since that SHA is recorded; (e) every register id fixed has a test named that fails before the fix and passes after; (f) all six closing questions answered, including skipped counts. If two or more of the three phases omit at least one step, build ONE saved Workflow script for the close sequence only, not a whole-phase driver, and recount over the next three phases. It passes at zero omissions across those three phases with no new owner-facing steps. If zero or one phase omits a step, record "skip: prose routine holds".
refutation.reason: "Control flow in code" already governs orchestration here (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN script contract, committed workflow scripts), and the evidence for a phase driver is asserted or anecdotal. A whole-phase driver would also duplicate the PR-checklist state owner that HR §4 protects, and would not fix self-reported compliance without hooks. Only a gated trial survives: script the mechanical phase-close sequence, and only if P1-P3 show the prose routine dropping close steps.

refutation.counter_evidence: The evidence is weak and does not carry over to this repo. C0050 to C0053 are all "evidence asserted": one TS script drives codex exec over throwaway fixtures, and no pass rates are published. HumanLayer uses it to regression-test a skill package that many users run. FixFlow's routine is run once per phase by one developer. Building and maintaining a suite of about 58 scenarios would be close to two things HR §4/§6 deliberately skipped, the M00–M06 measurement pipeline (owner priority low) and the doctor script, and both reasons still hold. Running at "medium effort" in C0050 is a setting, not evidence that medium works, so the L1 link fails. The W2 benefit is mostly illusory: a check on one fresh subagent in one trial says nothing about whether the Fable main session follows the routine across 40 phases. G2-A's planted decoy doc is unnecessary and risky, because a decoy committed to the real repo can mislead later sessions. Novelty does hold: a grep of SHIP-PLAN and ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN for transcript, tool-call, side-effect, git HEAD and decoy found no existing mechanism. There is also a concrete defect that supports the narrowed check. SHIP-PLAN P1 (lines 322-326) has the session write expected.json and commit it under docs/program/evidence/resume-trial-P1/ before it dispatches a fresh agent "given only the repository". The answer key is therefore readable by the agent under test. The judge compares only the recovered facts, so a trial contaminated by that file would pass without anyone noticing. The answer key is already the natural decoy, so no extra one is needed.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run once, inside P1's cold-resume trial (n=1, re-run once if contaminated). Before dispatch, record HEAD. Prefer to commit only sha256(expected.json) before the run and the file itself after it. After the run, check four things. (1) HEAD is unchanged and `git status --porcelain` is empty. (2) From the subagent's JSONL transcript, the file paths of its Read/Grep/Glob/Bash calls include SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md. (3) No call touches docs/program/evidence/resume-trial-P1/, and the string expected.json appears in no tool output. (4) Either all 10 facts are recovered, or every miss is traced to a plan defect fixed in the same PR. Pass = all four. Keep the read-log check for later trials only if it flagged something the agent's own report left out. Otherwise drop it after P1.
refutation.reason: What survives is not the 58-scenario suite. It is one bounded side-effect check inside P1's existing trial: HEAD and worktree unchanged, plus a transcript read log showing the plan was read and the committed answer key was not. It is cheap because P1 already pays for the agent run. It matters because the trial as written leaves its own answer key in the repo. It tests W3, not W2.

refutation.counter_evidence:
(1) The only part that transfers is already in the plan. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md §4 rules the fresh-agent cold-resume trial "trial once, as P1's first act". SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md P1 Entry (lines 322-327) makes it concrete: ten facts in docs/program/evidence/resume-trial-P1/expected.json, one Sonnet agent, misses fixed in the plan.

(2) G2-A's extension (re-run after every §0/CLAUDE.md change and every model switch, and adopt it as standing below 9/10) goes back on two rulings. It turns that deliberate "trial once" into a standing measurement loop. That loop is the M00–M06 pipeline, which HR §4 skipped ("a month of research established no gain; owner priority low"). KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md C-01 also lists M00–M06 among the skips not to re-adopt. Nothing has changed since 2026-11-01 that weakens that reason.

(3) The ten facts cannot serve as a regression baseline:
- They are "ten facts about this phase from the plan".
- P1's own procedure fixes every miss in the plan, so the set is tuned to 10/10 after its first run.
- Once P1 closes, the facts describe a finished phase.
- The repository changes every phase, so a later score mixes up model or routine effects with plan drift.
- The trial prompt is "read SHIP-PLAN §0 and P1", so the facts do not test CLAUDE.md content. A W1 trim would not register.
- It is n=10 from one stochastic run with no variance baseline, so the 9/10 threshold fires on a single random miss.

(4) The evidence does not transfer:
- C0701 is anecdotal and concerns product prompts at HumanLayer customers.
- C0509 is advice Dex attributes to Willison.
- C0823 needs a stream of product generations to label in an admin view. A one-developer, 40-phase program has nothing like that, and 30 cases would cost most of the program's sessions.
- C1113 has Dex admitting he has no answer yet on evaluating prompt changes. That counts against the claim.

(5) On W2 the gain is illusory. A recall score shows whether the plan text can be recovered, not whether a session followed the routine.

refutation.counter_evidence: Against the family as a whole: the harness resumes from git and the PR, not from a bare checkout. SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 31-37 resume a phase with `gh pr view <branch>` (first unticked box), `git log` and `eas build:list`, and the PR body opens with "Plan @ <sha>". A SlopCodeBench-style checkout with no commit history and no prior context would take those away, so the trial would fail for reasons that are not plan defects. That half does not transfer. The replay benchmark for comparing effort levels (L1, W5) is the skipped measurement pipeline M00-M06 under another name; that skip ("no gain; owner priority low") still holds, and both cards are anecdotal or asserted with no numbers. Against G2-A's "already-done": SHIP-PLAN lines 322-326 have P1 commit the ten facts to `docs/program/evidence/resume-trial-P1/expected.json` and then send the agent to "read SHIP-PLAN §0 and P1". The P1 text the agent is told to read names that answer-key path at line 324, and the agent works in the same worktree where the file was just committed. Nothing in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN, SHIP-PLAN or HARNESS-REVIEW hides it: a search for blind, hide, leak, pre-register and answer key found no such mechanism.
refutation.what_would_settle_it:
How to show it worked, on the one P1 trial:
(a) The sha256 of expected.json is in the draft PR's journal before the agent is dispatched, and it matches the file committed after judging.
(b) The trial agent's transcript has zero Read, Grep or Glob calls touching `resume-trial-P1/` or expected.json.
(c) The agent ran on a checkout without the answer file (the parent SHA, or the file kept in the scratchpad until judging).
Pass means all three hold. If (b) fails, the trial result is void and is rerun with the file hidden.
refutation.reason: Narrowed to the part C0244 calls the hard problem: keep the answer from the agent. P1's cold-resume trial has to keep expected.json out of the trial agent's reach: record its sha256 in the PR journal, commit it only after judging, and do not name its path in anything the agent reads. Without that, the only test of W3 can pass by reading the key, since P1 itself points to it. The no-history raw checkout and the replay-for-effort benchmark do not survive.

refutation.counter_evidence: Half of C0171 is already in place. The "trust the existing log" and "record changes as epochs" parts are covered by SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 31-43: resume reads the existing PR checklist or W0-results table, the PR body starts with "Plan @ <sha>", a git diff re-reads changed plan sections, and a Decisions / owner-corrections journal records changes. HR §4 adopted all of this (rows 1-2). HR §4 also skipped "Python checkpoint hashing and resume freshness" in favour of the git version, so any scripted or hook form of this check would bring back that skip. The W2 benefit is not real: a prose "stop and ask" rule is self-reported compliance too. The source is a library README design rule (asserted, no data). A blanket form of the rule would misfire: some phases resume from "The file" or "The section" and carry no Plan line (SHIP-PLAN lines 293 and 315). G2-B's already-done is wrong for one case, though. §0 says nothing about a missing or inconsistent source: a branch with commits but no draft PR, a PR body with no Plan line or an unreachable sha, or commits that landed after the last ticked box. Ticking is a separate gh pr edit, so a crash between the commit and the edit makes "first unticked box" redo a landed item. If that item is a migration, the next free slot gets taken a second time.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: What would show it worked: during P1's cold-resume trial, run one extra fault-injected dispatch. Give a fresh Sonnet agent a local branch with one Scope commit and either no draft PR or a PR body missing the Plan line, and ask it to resume P1. Pass = it stops and reports the mismatch, and does not open a new PR, start Scope item 1 or redo the committed item. Then check the first 5 real code phases for zero duplicate PRs and zero re-done items that had already landed.
refutation.reason: What survives is one sentence in §0, limited to phases whose Resume names a draft PR or a W0-results step table: if that source is missing, lacks the Plan @ sha line or has an unreachable sha, or the branch has commits the ticked boxes do not cover, list the commits and stop and ask the owner rather than starting fresh. This helps W3 only, not W2. The config-epoch half is already done, and a hook or script version would re-adopt the HR §4 skip.

reviews.measurement: The §0 resume line reads 'git fetch origin, then git diff …', and a resumed phase's journal shows the fetch ran.
reviews.reason: Without a fetch, the resume diff compares against a stale origin/main and can falsely report that nothing changed. The fix is one word.

refutation.counter_evidence: The only source is C0654 (G2-cards.md:1563), a line in a HumanLayer template with no numbers. It scores as asserted, so it gives no support on its own. The idea's second half, "propose pull commands rather than running them", is built for a setup with several repositories and does not carry over. FixFlow works in per-session worktrees on a single repository. A read-only `git fetch` updates the remote ref without touching any working tree, so no pull is needed and there is nothing to propose. The defect is also latent, not observed: today local main, origin/main and the remote all sit at a31924a, FETCH_HEAD was written 2026-11-04 11:48, and main has not moved since 2026-08-03. Nothing defeats the narrow fix, though. SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §0 line 38 runs `git diff --stat <sha>..origin/main -- docs/program/`, and a grep of the whole pr182 docs tree finds no `git fetch` or `git pull` anywhere. `gh pr view` reads the GitHub API, which does not refresh the local origin/main ref. §0 lines 28-30 also allow a second phase to run alongside a backend phase. That is the case where a plan amendment merges mid-phase and a stale ref would make the diff report no change.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: To show it worked: across the resumes and phase starts from P0a to P5, each PR journal records the origin/main sha it read after the fetch. Each recorded sha should equal what `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` showed at that moment. Pass if every one matches and no plan amendment merged mid-phase goes unread when the next box is ticked.
refutation.reason: What survives is a smaller version: add `git fetch origin` to §0, before the resume diff and before recording `Plan @ <sha>` at phase start. Git only updates origin/main on a fetch, and §0 never asks for one. Without it the resume check can silently miss a plan amendment. The broader "verify every checkout, propose pulls" form is unnecessary here.

refutation.counter_evidence: The harness already has the mechanism, and it differs from the family's rule on purpose. (1) ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md lines 16-19, "Who decides what": "Subagents gather, analyse and verify; they never decide." This covers C0212: autonomous review passes do not resolve anything. The same passage makes Fable "orchestrator, architect and judge" who "makes the calls", so agent-settled design rulings are part of the design. Examples are "ruling R2" and "ruling R9", HR-A3 and G2-D2 in SHIP-PLAN. (2) SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §4 (lines 1281-1317), "What the owner decides, and when it blocks", is the register of owner-only decisions. Each row has a Blocks column and a "Default if undecided" column, and some rows say "no default — P9-0b must answer". C0102/C0666 say a decision "stays open until you give a clear answer". The plan chose per-decision defaults instead, so it does not stall a 40-phase plan run by one developer. (3) §0 lines 39-43 add the "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections" journal. That records rejected options ("ruled out") and owner-made entries ("owner corrections") separately, and each entry moves at close to a W0-results decision row. HR line 260 adopted this journal. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN also has an owner-decision form (line 274) and an OWNER status class (line 57). Entries already name who decided: "owner decision 2026-11-01", "owner sign-off", "ruling Rn". (4) G2-A's success test, "every decision moved to W0-results is owner-settled, none agent-settled", would count the Fable rulings the routine is meant to produce as failures. (5) The evidence is weak and the W2 gain is not real. All five cards are rated "asserted". The tests in C0040 check where entries sit in the skill's own document, not any outcome. A 'proposed/owner-settled' tag would be written by the same agent whose compliance is in question. It is the self-report W2 is about, so it gives no outside check.
refutation.reason: Already done: subagents never decide, the owner-only decisions are in SHIP-PLAN §4 with blocks and defaults, and the journal records ruled-out options and owner corrections. Owner-only resolution of every design question would reverse the deliberate choice of Fable as judge and the §4 defaults, and a self-applied provenance tag adds no outside check for W2.

refutation.counter_evidence:
(1) The evidence is weak on every card. C0390's ARR figure is anecdotal and not linked to the loop by any cause. C0548 is a talk by an unnamed attendee that Dex called "very good". C0457 is asserted, and its card says "no mechanism given here". C1237 is an endorsed quote with no data, and the same post says not to hunt for problems in advance and to "bias towards shipping". C0004 is a marketing bullet. Under the owner rules none of this counts as more than a claim.
(2) The harness already has the capture and the routing. SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 39-43 keep a "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections (this phase)" journal, appended as each one happens and moved at phase close to a W0-results decision row or a plan amendment. HR-2026-11-01 lines 260 and 278 record that journal as adopted and list "Lessons carried into the plan". CLAUDE.md already follows Hashimoto's rule: "Rule first, reason second. Each of these was paid for" and "each one has already cost real time".
(3) Engineering away every mistake with prose rules is what made CLAUDE.md 390 lines long. So the family's main outcome feeds W1 rather than easing W2.
(4) The weekly cadence does not fit this routine. The unit of work is one phase per session, not a week. Mining agent traces, as C0548 does, reopens the measurement pipeline M00-M06 and the context-system skip ("a month of research established no gain").
(5) The benefit on W2 is mostly illusory. The loop only sees corrections the owner noticed and journalled, which is the same self-report W2 complains about. A skipped routine that nobody caught never reaches it.
refutation.what_would_settle_it:
Run the trial over the first five phase sessions that actually execute (from P1 on). At each close, give every owner-correction journal entry a one-word cause tag: harness (the agent skipped or misread a rule that was already clear), plan, or product. Count the harness-tagged entries and how many times each shape repeats.
- Pass: at least one harness shape appears 2 or more times across the five phases, and it produces a harness change the owner accepts. That change must be a CI check, a skill or a §0 edit, or a CLAUDE.md line that comes with an equal removal.
- Drop the tag if no harness-tagged shape repeats in five phases, or if every resulting change is a net CLAUDE.md addition.
Also record whether any harness-tagged entry came from something other than the owner noticing. If none did, confirm that the tag does nothing for W2.
refutation.reason: The weekly loop that mines PR comments and traces fails: weak evidence, it reopens the measurement skip, it doesn't fit one-phase sessions, it adds to W1, and it does little for W2. What survives is a one-word cause tag on the §0 owner-corrections journal entries, so that a correction caused by the agent ignoring a rule has an owner and a repeat shows up across phases. The cheapest trial is to add that tag, not a new ritual or a new closing-message line.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The step Dex lets small work skip is per-task planning: research, design discussion and outline (C0098, C0741, C1132, C1135). FixFlow did that planning once, up front. In SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md every phase arrives with its Scope, Entry, Done-when, Workflow and Size already written, and §0 has no per-phase research, design or outline step. Every phase already "starts from a document that specifies the task" (C0060). §0 Routing (lines 47-56) also has Sonnet implement "from a design's test list". 2) Dex's oneshot still ends in a PR (C0098: "implement and PR"). None of the nine cards argues for dropping review, resume pointers or reporting, and those are what is left in §0. G2-A's light track drops the OWNER-VIEW refresh. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md line 267 adopted that refresh, tied to phase close, because the owner asked for it, so dropping it reopens an owner decision without evidence. 3) The plan is already tiered by risk and by type. Routing sends invariant work to Opus. Operations phases resume from a W0-results table instead of a draft PR (§0 lines 33-35). Owner phases resume from "the table" or "the file" (P0a: "Workflow. None"). Every code phase has a Size line (Small/Medium/Large) and an "If long, split" rule (P1, P2a, P3a, P5a, P8b). 4) The phases a light track could apply to are almost none. Both small code phases are Opus-routed money work: P12a "Opus (money)" and P9-0a "Opus (money-adjacent)". G2-A itself excludes Opus-routed phases. The only phases routed purely to Sonnet are P7b-2, P12 and P13c, about 3 of 40, and all come after P5. So neither reviewer's window (G2-A: first six phases; G2-B: P1-P5) contains a single qualifying phase. P1, P2a, P2b-1 and P2b-2 are Opus; P2c, P3b, P3c and P4a are ops or owner sessions; P3a's compose and restore are Opus-reviewed. Both measurements can only come back empty. 5) "Any phase may be entered directly" contradicts the per-phase Entry gates, which are safety ordering (drain-image, T_close, "P3b done"). In Dex's own sense (workflow steps, not ship-plan phases) that point is already covered by item 1. 6) The evidence is all asserted or anecdotal. The 40% oneshot figure is "I would guess" (C0741), and the workflow tables carry "no usage data" (C0059). There is no FixFlow observation of the routine being skipped, because it has never run (W3). The W2 benefit is therefore speculative. A self-declared "light" label is also exactly the unauditable escape hatch G2-B warns about, since there are no hooks.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Nothing to measure now: the shortest-path principle is already built in (risk routing, Size lines, lighter resume for ops and owner phases). Revisit only on a trigger: if the closing messages of the Sonnet-routed code phases P7b-2, P12 and P13c record a §0 step skipped, or a step that found nothing, in at least 2 of the 3, ask the owner then whether those phases alone should get a lighter close.
refutation.reason: The plan already does this. Planning happens once in the plan, and every phase is already sorted by risk, type and size. The only new part, a lighter routine for small phases, would cut review and reporting, which Dex's evidence never addresses. It would also apply to about 3 of 40 phases, all after the window both reviewers chose to measure in.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The harness already has most of the mechanism. SHIP-PLAN §0, lines 39-43, keeps a "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections (this phase)" journal that is appended the moment an entry occurs. A deliberate deviation from Scope is already a decision entry, so a separate PR section adds only the explicit prompt and the "none" line. (2) The test half of a deviation inventory already exists. §0, lines 52-55, makes the Opus reviewer list "every changed expected value, removed assertion and new skip or xfail with its reason". (3) The W2 benefit is illusory unless someone checks the list independently. The deviation list is written by the same agent or session that deviated, so it is self-reported. An unnoticed deviation never appears on it. The only observable is the reviewer comparing the diff against Scope, and the reviewer brief in §0 does not ask for that today: it names register ids to break. (4) The evidence is anecdotal or asserted, with no numbers. C0986 is one podcast guest's review habit, relayed by Dex. C0033 is a four-line report format inside an agent file. (5) The stop-and-report half has no place to land yet. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN line 111 says "S3 not designed yet (... per-phase implementation recipes)", and line 749 also leaves the implementer recipes open, so no implementer brief or output schema exists to carry the Expected / Found / Why / How-to-proceed fields. (6) .github/pull_request_template.md is a generic npm checklist with no plan-anchored field. Phase PR bodies follow §0, not the template, so this lands in §0 and in the reviewer brief, not in the template. Nothing here reopens a deliberate skip: HR §4/§6 do not mention deviations.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run it over the first three phase PRs that get an Opus review (P1 onward). Count three things: (a) deviation entries in the journal, each giving expected, found and why, or an explicit "none" at close; (b) deviations from Scope or the design that the reviewer finds by comparing the diff against the Scope checklist and that the journal did not list, each recorded as a routine miss; (c) reviewer findings or owner corrections that trace to a listed deviation. Do the same for implementer subagent returns: count the mismatch reports, and count the design mismatches the reviewer finds in the diff that no mismatch report raised. Keep the heading if, across the 3 PRs, (c) is at least 1 or (b) is at least 1. In the second case it has made a silent deviation visible, which is the W2 gain. Drop the heading if all three PRs say "none" and the reviewer finds no unlisted deviation. Keep the reviewer's diff-against-Scope line either way.
refutation.reason: Narrowed. Instead of a new PR section, the smaller version has three parts: a fourth journal heading in §0, "deviations from Scope @ Plan sha (expected / found / why)", ending in an explicit "none"; one reviewer-brief line, "compare the diff against Scope; an unlisted deviation is a routine miss"; and a mismatches field in the implementer output schemas once S3 is designed. Anecdotal evidence and a routine that has never run make it a trial, not an adopt.
