refutation.counter_evidence:
Both reviewers say workflow scripts "are not saved". The repository says otherwise. The practice they propose to adopt (commit each Workflow script next to its outputs, saved as .js.txt so the lint job skips it, and list it in manifest.sha256) has been the working convention in every evidence folder created since 2026-11-01:
(1) docs/program/evidence/harness-ideas/horthy/README.md rows 18-19 ("`workflows/*.js.txt` | The Workflow-tool scripts exactly as run"). Its manifest.sha256 lists 9 tools/*.txt files and 3 workflows/horthy-sweep-*.js.txt files.
(2) KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md appendix (~lines 970-971): the evidence/knowledge-store/critique-2026-11-03/ and refute-v1.3/ folders each hold "the workflow script, output and journal (wf_*.*, *.js.txt ...)".
Only the oldest folder, evidence/README.md (the W1/W2 runs from 2026-11-01), holds outputs alone. The "not saved" premise in the brief is out of date.
The wider family adds nothing beyond this. The "spec as durable artifact" half already exists in SHIP-PLAN §0: the draft PR body starts "Plan @ <sha>" and keeps a Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections journal. Recording raw chat is backed only by Dex relaying Sean Grove (C0340/C0341, evidence asserted), and Dex later disowned it (C0416: "spec is the new code" is not enough). All five cards are asserted or title-only.
The claimed benefits are also overstated:
- "Reproducible" is wrong. The scripts drive non-deterministic agents, and the sources stay out of the repository by design (horthy README row 10). Saving a script makes evidence auditable, not reproducible.
- W5 is barely touched. The saved scripts are tied to one run, with hardcoded folder lists and SK+/R+ path constants (horthy-sweep-wf_5b59f5db-8bc.js.txt lines 70-82), so they are an archive, not a reusable library.
- W3 (cold resume) does not depend on these scripts. It runs from the PR journal.
One possible slip: tools/split-review-input.mjs.txt is untracked and not in the manifest. It is most likely in-flight work from the review that is still running, not proof that the convention fails.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: The practice already exists, so only one quick check remains. When the horthy review is committed, check that tools/split-review-input.mjs.txt and the review Workflow's own .js.txt are committed and listed in horthy/manifest.sha256. If either is missing, the fix is housekeeping: add a one-line rule to ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §5. It is not a new adoption.
refutation.reason: The family's one concrete action (commit the producing script beside its evidence, listed in the manifest) is already the de facto convention in the horthy and knowledge-store evidence folders. The "spec/plan as durable artifact" half is SHIP-PLAN §0's Plan @ sha plus decisions journal. The remaining claims ("reproducible", "starts the W5 library", "chat as source") are overstated or come from a source its own author later disowned.

label: Choose compliance sensors that cannot be silently disabled (config kept outside the lint config).
strongest_evidence: anecdotal: React Doctor example chosen because an inline comment can't switch it off (C0916).
sample_quote: "whether it can be silently disabled" (C0916)
landing_guesses: Verifier design: a check an agent cannot quietly skip

reviews.lens: cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is reopened, what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build and keep honest
reviews.existing_mechanism: Ship plan §0 Routing: reviewer lists every new skip or xfail; skip-aware gates (pytest -rs, no --passWithNoTests)
reviews.measurement: Reviewer verdicts on the next 5 PRs carry a 'new suppressions' list; a later grep of those diffs for noqa / type: ignore / eslint-disable / ts-expect-error finds none the verdict missed.
reviews.reason: Add inline suppressions (noqa, type: ignore, eslint-disable, ts-expect-error, import-linter ignores) to the reviewer's existing 'list every new skip' item; it's one line in the brief.

reviews.lens: benefit
reviews.existing_mechanism: Reviewer already lists new skips/xfails (plan §0 Routing); eslint.config.js has no noInlineConfig, and the repo already carries ~59 noqa/eslint-disable/type-ignore directives
reviews.measurement: Each PR verdict lists every new eslint-disable, # noqa, type: ignore and import-linter ignore in the diff; after P1-P3, a git diff grep over merged PRs finds zero suppressions the verdict did not list.
reviews.reason: Slice-boundary sensors can be switched off inline today; one line in the refute brief makes that visible at no cost.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The principle is already met for the slice-boundary sensors. Import-linter has no inline disable at all; its only escape hatch is `ignore_imports` in backend/pyproject.toml (lines 118 and 181), which is config. The planned mobile check, dependency-cruiser (P5b-2), also keeps its exceptions in config. Mypy runs `strict = true` with `warn_unused_ignores = true` (pyproject.toml:86-87), and every one of the 21 `type: ignore` lines in the repo carries an error code. 2) G2-A says the slice sensors can be switched off inline today. Only the web ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rule can be, and none of the 6 eslint-disable lines in the repo targets it: they disable react-refresh/only-export-components (3) and react-hooks/exhaustive-deps (3). 3) Keeping the config "outside the lint config" does not stop an agent that can write to the repo, because it can edit pyproject.toml or eslint.config.js in the same PR. The only real protection is that the change shows up in a reviewed diff, so the idea comes down to making suppressions visible. 4) The W2 link is false. W2 asks whether the phase routine or the knowledge store was actually used. Lint suppressions say nothing about that. 5) The evidence is one anecdote from a design-taxonomy example (React Doctor), with no numbers. 6) The base rate is low: 7 of the last 40 commits on main added any suppression (9 in total), all in the backend and all with codes. What does survive: plan §0 Routing has the reviewer list "new skip or xfail", which is test vocabulary and does not cover `# noqa`, `type: ignore`, `eslint-disable` or `ts-expect-error`. The repo already has inline suppressions of security rules (`# noqa: S608`, `S603`, `S105`), so enumerating new ones has real but small value.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: For the next 5 merged code PRs, run a git diff grep over each PR's base..head. Count added lines that match noqa, `type: ignore`, eslint-disable, ts-expect-error or ts-ignore, plus any change to `ignore_imports`, `per-file-ignores`, `[tool.mypy]`, `[tool.ruff]` or eslint.config.js. Compare that count with the reviewer verdict's "new suppressions" line, where an explicit "none" counts as present. It worked if 5/5 verdicts carry the line and the grep finds 0 suppressions the verdict missed. At about 0.2 suppressions per commit, expect roughly one non-empty list. If none occur, the trial shows only that the line is present, which is acceptable because it costs nothing.
refutation.reason: Narrowed. Choosing sensors that cannot be disabled inline is already done: import-linter allows no inline disable and mypy flags unused ignores. The W2 benefit is illusory. What survives is one clause added to §0 Routing's "new skip or xfail" item, so the reviewer lists every new inline suppression and lint/type/import-config exception, each with its reason.

refutation.counter_evidence:
1. The evidence is one anecdote. C1124 (G2-cards.md, lines 2385-2391) is a single live observation in Vaibhav's repo: a plan picked Storybook 8 when 10 was current, plus an old Rust crate. It has no count and no outcome, so under the owner rules it scores as a claim.

2. The rule's direction is wrong for this stack. CLAUDE.md pins Expo SDK 52 and RN 0.76.9. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md line 33 records the pinned packages (expo-location@18.0.10, expo-notifications@0.29.14, ...). Lines 603-607 forbid even the expo/expo sdk-52 branch head because it "is not the pinned patch version". SDK moves are a dedicated phase, SHIP-PLAN P14-n (line 1262: one major per phase, entry after P5d-2). For P5b-2's expo-notifications reminder, "check the web for the current version" would point at a newer, incompatible release. G2-B is right on this.

3. The useful core already exists:
   - ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN line 608 is a web-research rule: WebSearch/WebFetch, record tool_status and urls_attempted, never invent a fact.
   - The harness review gathered dependency facts by "Sonnet, web + repo", for example graphifyy 0.9.100 with its 2026-11-01 release date (HARNESS-REVIEW line 290).
   - It requires "a version at least 14 days old" (HARNESS-REVIEW line 299).

4. There is little for the rule to act on. The only new non-Expo dependency in the plan is dependency-cruiser, a devDependency in P5b-2 (SHIP-PLAN line 860). A plan that names an older major from memory still installs, and CI plus the P5b-2 Opus reviewer would catch a broken install.

5. It does nothing for the named weaknesses. It does not test the untried phase routine (W3). It is not a verifier on agent output (L3); it checks an input fact.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Only if someone wants to reopen it: after P5b-2 merges, compare the dependency-cruiser version in technician-app/package.json with `npm view dependency-cruiser time --json`. Count the dependency-adding phases where (a) the chosen version trails the registry by at least one major and (b) that lag caused a CI or runtime failure. Reopen only if (b) is at least 1 across P5b-2 and P13c.
refutation.reason: The evidence is one anecdote. "Use the current version" fights the deliberate pins (Expo SDK 52, P14-n), and the harness already checks dependency facts on the web with the 14-day rule (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN line 608, HARNESS-REVIEW line 299). That leaves one devDependency in one phase, and CI already guards it.

reviews.reason: Plan is already written and gated; unknowns surface through the journal, so deleting sections buys little.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The harness already keeps unknowns out of build Scopes, and labels them when they do enter. SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §4 "What the owner decides, and when it blocks" (line 1281) lists each open decision with an explicit "Default if undecided" or "P3b blocks". Open technical questions get their own phases instead of a guessed Scope: P5-spike (line 764) exists to "Settle HR-A1b's open question with device evidence instead of a desk opinion", and P9-0b decides cash custody before P9a-1/P9b build it. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md (lines 564-566) has owner decisions gate the design agents, because "spending Opus before those answers is spending it on a guess". Its open-risks list (lines 568-571, 772-773) keeps an unsettled claim with its settling test instead of dropping it. The §0 PR journal (lines 39-43) records decisions as they happen. 2) G2-B's blanket rule, "an open question rather than a pre-banked decision", contradicts a deliberate §4 design. §4 pre-banks labelled defaults on purpose so a one-developer program does not stall; for example, it assumes yes when P0a item 15 is unknown (line 1295). 3) The literal tip does not transfer here. Deleting a section relies on the model rediscovering the answer from code patterns. This repo routes invariant code to Opus with design notes precisely because its code patterns mislead: CLAUDE.md calls "last write wins by id" a false assumption, and the HANDOFF §6 defect shapes say the same. 4) The evidence is one person's habit. In the same clip (C1156) his co-host says it did not apply to his novel case. 5) The benefit on W3 is illusory. W3 is that the routine has never been tested, and P1's cold-resume trial (line 322) is that test; this tip has no effect on it. G2-B's measurement also cannot be observed, because an unjournaled guess leaves no record to count.
refutation.reason: The useful core (state unknowns as open, labelled items, not as silent guesses) is already in place: ship-plan §4 defaults and blockers, the spike and decide-first phases, the orchestration open-risks list and owner-decision gating, and the PR journal. The literal tip (delete the section and let the model fill it from code patterns) conflicts with §4's deliberate labelled defaults and with Opus ownership of invariant code. It rests on a single anecdote and does nothing for W3.

reviews.lens: cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is reopened, what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build and keep honest
reviews.existing_mechanism: Workflow-tool scripts with stages for discovery/verification (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §4.3 script contract); the phase routine itself is prose in ship plan §0
reviews.reopens_skipped: Not a hook: a Workflow script for the phase-close stage does not touch the pre-commit/SessionStart skips
reviews.measurement: Script only the phase-close stage (Opus reviewer dispatch bound to head SHA, journal moved, six-question message, OWNER-VIEW refresh) for 2 phases and leave 2 phases prose-run; a post-hoc audit counts missing close items per phase; keep the script if the scripted phases miss 0 and the prose phases miss at least 1.
reviews.reason: The skip-prone tail of the routine is the cheapest part to move into control flow, and a saved script also chips at W5.

reviews.lens: benefit
reviews.existing_mechanism: Per-task Workflow scripts (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §3/§5), authored and discarded each time
reviews.measurement: Commit the per-PR reviewer workflow (refute brief, head-SHA verdict, fail-before/pass-after per id) as one script; over P1-P3 count phases that run it without structural edits; keep if reused unchanged in at least 2 of 3.
reviews.reason: Moving the skip-prone reviewer sequence into saved control flow attacks W2 and W5 together without a hook.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The evidence is weak. All three cards are anecdotal or asserted with no numbers (C1333 workshop experience; C1424 Riptide rebuild "no numbers"; C1458 asserted), so under the owner rules this is a claim, not evidence. 2) The harness already does the general principle. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §4.3 (lines 198-240) puts W1/W2 sequencing in Workflow scripts: deterministic issue order, phase() stages, a circuit breaker and a return contract. 3) The skip-prone steps are already being packaged. The skills batch in worktree wizardly-hertz-02c46a includes .claude/skills/fixflow-orchestration/SKILL.md with a session procedure: step 28 is reviewer dispatch bound to the head SHA with fail-before/pass-after per id; step 35 is the six-question close, the OWNER-VIEW refresh and moving the journal. Its §3 check table includes "reviewer verdict SHA == PR head SHA". §1.3 line 79 adds a pinned fixflow-pr-reviewer agentType (Opus), and a saved references/w1-script-skeleton.md partly answers W5. 4) The whole routine does not transfer. A phase session is owner-paced: merge, Docker start and deploy are [owner] steps (skill steps 5 and 30-34), so a script cannot span it. The six-question message and OWNER-VIEW refresh are Fable's judgement and writing, not control flow, which undercuts G2-B's "script the close stage" version. 5) The W2 benefit is mostly illusory. A saved script still has to be invoked by the same self-reporting main session; only a hook makes a step unskippable, and hooks are a deliberate skip. 6) W3: the routine has never run, so scripting it now would freeze a sequence nobody has tested.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run the PR-review stage as prose (skill step 28) in P1 and audit it after merge. Then commit one review-stage Workflow script to the repo. It takes args {registerIds, headSha}, calls fixflow-pr-reviewer with a VERDICT schema that carries head_sha and, per id, fail_on_base_test and pass_on_head_test, and compares the SHAs in code. Use it on the next 3 code-phase PRs, with each PR journal citing the runId. For each merged PR, count review-stage omissions: a verdict SHA that differs from the merged head with no re-read noted; a fixed register id with no named fail-on-base/pass-on-head test; or an unlisted changed expected value, removed assertion or new skip/xfail. Keep the script if the scripted PRs show 0 omissions and it needed only args changes (no structural edit) in at least 2 of 3. Drop it if it needed structural edits in 2 or more of the 3, or if P1's prose run also shows 0 omissions and the script saved no Fable turns.
refutation.reason: Only one small version survives: a single saved Workflow script for the deterministic part of the PR-review stage (SHA binding, per-id fail/pass table, compare in code), run as a trial after P1, chipping at W5 and making that one stage auditable. Moving the whole phase routine or its close into code does not survive: the skills batch already packages it, it is owner-paced and judgement-heavy, and it does not fix W2 without the hooks that were deliberately skipped.

reviews.lens: cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is reopened, what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build and keep honest

reviews.measurement: Each phase's first user message is the committed kickoff text; the P1-P3 audit finds the first-unticked-box resume, the reviewer and the closing message happened in every phase.

reviews.measurement: A fixed phase-launch prompt restates the five must-do steps (draft PR with Plan @ sha, store consult, reviewer brief, six-question close, OWNER-VIEW refresh); the F183 transcript audit of P1 shows zero skipped steps, else escalate to the F118 script.
reviews.reason: Putting key orders in the user message is free and targets the known step-skipping failure on a never-run routine.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The evidence is one anecdotal card (C1653). It concerns the interactive "ask open questions first" step of a planning prompt, not the procedural steps of §0, and its "thousands of runs" comes with no numbers, which the owner's rules score as anecdote. (2) It does nothing for W2's detection problem. Most §0 steps already leave outside traces that `gh pr view` and git can check without hooks: the draft PR whose first body line is "Plan @ <sha>", the checkbox list, the reviewer verdict naming the head SHA with fail-before/pass-after, and the OWNER-VIEW.md commit (SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 31-46, 51-55). Only these steps leave no trace: the resume `git diff --stat` re-read, appending to the journal at the moment something happens, and the six-question close. (3) A fixed kickoff list built for code phases would give the very next phase the wrong first step. P0a is an operations phase, and its first act is committing its step table to W0-results.md, not opening a draft PR (§0 lines 33-36). P1's first act is the cold-resume trial (plan line 322). (4) Reviewer A's "store consult" step points at a knowledge store that does not exist yet (PR #183 is a design, its D1 audit not run). (5) A second copy of the orders is another projection that can drift. §0 was amended through v6-v8, and the overhead-skeptic raised the same drift objection to OWNER-VIEW (HARNESS-REVIEW §4 line 267). Nothing defeats the core idea, though. Today the orders reach the model only through a read of a dense §0 paragraph (a tool result). The memory file's "How to apply" is a pointer to §0, not the orders. `.claude/skills/README.md` has no phase-kickoff skill. HR-C5 is a compaction hook held in reserve, and a pasted message reopens no deliberate skip.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run the first 4 phase sessions (P0a onward), each opened with the kickoff block pasted as the first user message. Afterwards, a Haiku extraction over each transcript plus `gh pr view` / `git log` checks every step the block names. For an operations phase: was the W0-results step table, with its Plan @ line, the first commit? For a code phase: was the draft PR opened at the first commit with "Plan @ <sha>" as body line 1? Were journal entries dated before the close? Did the Opus reviewer verdict name the head SHA and give fail-before/pass-after per register id? Did a six-question close message appear in the transcript? Was OWNER-VIEW.md committed within the phase? On every resumed session, did the `git diff --stat <sha>..origin/main -- docs/program/` command run? Pass means zero missed steps across all 4 sessions: keep the block. If any named step is missed even once, the block is not enough: escalate to the F118 check script, not a hook. If a step the block does not name is missed, add it to the block. Fable judges. This measures whether the block is enough, not whether it is needed (there is no control), which is acceptable because it costs nothing.
refutation.reason: A smaller version survives. Put a 5-8 line "paste to open a phase" block inside SHIP-PLAN §0 itself (one file, so no drift), with separate first steps for code and operations phases, naming only the steps that leave no trace and dropping the unbuilt store-consult step. It is a trial, not an adopt: the evidence is a single anecdote, and the block lowers skip risk without making compliance visible (W2).

refutation.counter_evidence: The broad family is refuted. (1) Evidence: none of the three cards has a measurement. C1338 and C1677 are rated "asserted" and C1523 "anecdotal". (2) Deterministic work is already done in code: CI runs three jobs with import-linter and ESLint slice rules plus skip-aware gates; the P1 CI step fails when CLAUDE.md's Alembic head is wrong (SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md line 365); the backend gates follow a scripted recipe (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md Appendix A, line 630). The Workflow scripts are themselves code orchestrators: they compute `git log` before any model sees it (line 166) and fix the issue order and labels in code (line 200). (3) The push/commit anecdote does not transfer. C1523 describes an unattended Ralph loop that lost work because nothing told it to push. Here the phase sessions are interactive and a draft PR is opened at the first commit (SHIP-PLAN line 31), so a missing push shows up at once. (4) The readers' guess of "hooks over prose rules" would reopen the pre-commit verification hook. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md line 272 skipped that hook because of the RT-04/05 defects and because CI already gates the PRs, and both reasons still hold. (5) G2-A's script "run at close" by the session does not touch W2: whether the script was run would itself be self-reported. G2-B's "already-done" goes too far, though. Nothing deterministic checks the routine's artefacts. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md line 548 admits that compliance is self-reported with no hook, and CI never reads PR bodies. The weakest proposed items (for example "journal heading present") have the RT-04/05 shape: a check that passes without testing anything.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Trial a separate, dependency-free GitHub workflow (not a hook, and not run by the model). It triggers on pull_request opened, edited, synchronize and ready_for_review, is advisory while the PR is a draft, and fails once the PR is marked ready. It checks only facts a script can decide: (a) the first body line is `Plan @ <40-hex>` and that commit exists (`git cat-file -e`); (b) the latest reviewer-verdict comment names the PR's current head SHA (headRefOid), which catches a push after review; (c) the PR body has no unticked `- [ ]` box without a note beside it; (d) `docs/program/OWNER-VIEW.md` is among the PR's changed files; (e) every committed evidence manifest's sha256 values match the files. Run it on the first 5 code-phase PRs from P1 on. Count three things: misses it flags that the closing message called done (each confirmed by the owner, and each noted as whether the owner or the main session would have caught it before merge anyway); false positives; and hours to build and maintain. Keep it if it catches at least 1 miss that would otherwise have been missed, with 0 false positives and no more than 2 hours of build time. Retire it if it catches nothing in 5 PRs.
refutation.reason: The general principle is already in place (CI, gate scripts, Workflow orchestrators), and the hook and push/commit versions either reopen a skip whose reasons still hold or don't transfer. What survives is a smaller trial: one CI-run, mechanical-only check of code-phase PR artefacts (Plan @ SHA, reviewer verdict bound to the head SHA, ticked boxes, OWNER-VIEW changed, manifest hashes), which moves the checkable part of W2 out of self-report.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) Evidence is asserted only. C1406 is a short exchange with no data, and it ended against the hard block. (2) The hook variant breaks on legitimate work. git log shows that 8 of 369 commits edited import-linter contract lines (245e299, 4a40423/#162, 7d567c7/0040, db545cb/0042, 834311f/0034, d96236e, 7fb087f, ee343da). The ship plan schedules more of these edits for agents: P5b-2 adds dependency-cruiser (line 853-861) and P9 adds the accounting slice's import-linter edges (line 1141). Opus/Sonnet are routed to own migrations and infra files (§0 line 47-50), so a PreToolUse block would force a bypass or a manual edit on planned phases. (3) The CODEOWNERS / PR-rule variant is already in place and cannot be enforced. .github/CODEOWNERS already has `* @Tempest-Zero` and `/.github/ @Tempest-Zero`, so a protected-paths line routes the review to the same sole owner and adds nothing. `gh api repos/:owner/:repo/branches/main/protection` returns 403 ("Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public"), so neither required reviews nor code-owner reviews can be enforced. A solo author could not approve their own PR in any case. (4) Part of the landing guess is already covered: the P1 CI check compares CLAUDE.md's Alembic head against the migration chain. (5) Correction: the hook the harness review skipped (HARNESS-REVIEW line 272) is a pre-commit verification hook, not an edit block, so G2-B's "reopens the hook skip" is not exact. The hard block fails on (2) without relying on it. What is left uncovered: the §0 reviewer brief (SHIP-PLAN line 54-55) lists only test-side sensor weakening ("every changed expected value, removed assertion and new skip or xfail"). It does not name changes to boundary or gate configs, which weaken a check the same way while CI stays green, because CI runs whatever config the PR carries.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Over the first five merged phase PRs (P1 through P5b-2), run `git diff <base>..<head> -- backend/pyproject.toml eslint.config.js .github/workflows/ci.yml '.dependency-cruiser*'` on each PR. Keep only hunks inside [tool.importlinter], no-restricted-imports, dependency-cruiser rules, or ci.yml gate/run steps. For each such hunk, check whether the Opus verdict bound to that head SHA names it with a reason. Decision: if 1 or more hunks go unnamed, adopt one clause in §0 line 55, "every change to a boundary or gate config (import-linter contracts, ESLint restricted imports, dependency-cruiser rules, CI gate steps)", next to removed assertions and new skips. If 0 go unnamed across 3 or more PRs that touch these configs, skip. If fewer than 3 PRs touch them, skip as too rare to matter. Leave the CLAUDE.md head line out because the P1 CI check already covers it.
refutation.reason: Refuted: the hard block and the CODEOWNERS/PR rule (configs change legitimately in planned phases; CODEOWNERS already routes everything to the sole owner; branch protection is unavailable on this plan). Surviving: at most one clause in the existing Opus reviewer brief naming boundary- and gate-config diffs, trialled over P1 through P5b-2 and adopted only if a config change goes unnamed.

refutation.counter_evidence:
The harness already does what this family asks. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md §6 HR-C5 (lines ~330-336) keeps the only planned hook as exact JSON for the in-repo `.claude/settings.json`. That hook is stateless: an echo plus `git log`, with no state file. The §4 table skips the pre-commit hook and the context system, whose hooks are the undocumented-PreCompact kind, and HR-C3 says "no PreCompact hook, no context-system install". Line 299 makes graphify conditional on "no `graphify install` and no git hook". The owner rule "nothing installed without an owner decision" covers the rest.

Observed state today:
- The worktree has no `.claude/settings.json`; `.claude/` holds only `launch.json`.
- `C:/Users/User/.claude/settings.json` has only the keys autoCompactWindow, enableWorkflows, modelSettings and skipWorkflowUsageWarning: no hooks.
- `C:/Users/User/.claude/plugins` holds only a directory cache, with no installed plugins.
- `C:/Users/User/.claude/dev-mods` is empty.

So no opaque or global hook exists for the rule to guard against. The source evidence is thin. C1512 is Dex's own unmeasured test ("no numbers") of one Anthropic plugin (ralph-wiggum) that this harness does not use. The family also does nothing for W2: W2's problem is that compliance can't be seen because there are no hooks, and a rule limiting the shape of hooks adds no visibility. It does nothing for L3 either.
refutation.reason: The harness already insists on visible, in-repo, stateless hooks (HR-C5's in-repo JSON, HR-C3, the §4 skips, the graphify no-hook condition, the owner-decision rule), and no global or plugin hook is installed, so G2-B is right that this is already done. refutation.counter_evidence:
(1) None of the evidence is a measurement. C1390 is Dex's own account with no numbers, and what it describes is a model improving enough to allow a longer workflow (three steps to five). That is an opportunity, not a regression, so it gives no support for a re-test aimed at regressions. C1631 is an HN commenter's opinion and C1904 is a principle stated without data. Under the owner rules all three count as claims or anecdotes.

(2) "Own prompts as versioned code" is already in place. CLAUDE.md, the skills and the plan are in git. The draft PR body starts with "Plan @ <sha>" (HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md §4 adopt rows; SHIP-PLAN §0). CLAUDE.md has its "Keeping this file honest" section, and P1 adds a CI check for the Alembic head and that named paths resolve.

(3) Benchmarking every change reopens the skipped "Measurement pipeline M00–M06; evaluation-run schema" (HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md, skip row: "a month of research established no gain; owner priority low"). Nothing new defeats that reason.

(4) G2-A's narrowed trial measures the wrong thing. The P1 cold-resume trial's ten facts are "about this phase from the plan", and the agent is told "read SHIP-PLAN §0 and P1" (SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md, P1 Entry, about line 322). The W1 trim (KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md line 509 and KS-7) keeps every rule sentence and leaves "Do NOT assume" unchanged. It moves out only the narratives of verified entries. So a rerun is close to insensitive to what the trim removes. With one agent run and ten facts, "≥ baseline" cannot tell a one-fact miss from noise.

(5) The real risk in the trim is losing knowledge for sessions that never look anything up. That is already gated by measurement, with the right instrument: KS-7 runs only after the KS-5 pilot shows lookups happen (§7.8), and every removed narrative must resolve with `ks show <id>`, with line counts before and after in the PR body.

(6) The harness review ruled the trial "trial once" on purpose. Also, every one of the 40 phases already starts as a fresh-context resume under whatever model is current, and misses land in the "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections" journal. A model-release re-audit adds almost nothing on top of that.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Reopen re-testing at model releases only if there is evidence of a model-caused regression. Two cheap checks would show one. First, the P1 trial (run once, as planned) records any miss. Second, after a model switch, the phase journals record at least one resume miss that the owner or reviewer attributes to the new model. Count these across the first 3 phase sessions after the switch, compared with the 3 before it. One or more attributable misses would justify rerunning the frozen P1 trial at the frozen plan sha. Zero means it stays skipped.

refutation.counter_evidence: Against the family: the only card (C1343) is an unmeasured remark made while iterating on a prompt ("no data"). On W2 the benefit is illusory, because sorting misses into bins does nothing to make routine compliance visible from outside. The harness already applies the same "attribute the failure before acting" discipline to gates: ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md line 32 and S-07a (line 187) say any Node failure is re-run under node:22 before it is called a repo defect. So the idea is not new to the harness, only missing from one step. There is also a risk. The session that wrote expected.json is the one that judges the misses, and a "the agent erred" bin would let the plan's author excuse gaps in the plan. Against G2-B's skip: SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md lines 325-326 ("judges the recovered facts against the file and fixes any miss in the plan"), and HR row 268 ("judges the miss"), send every miss to a plan edit. The step does not separate a fault in the plan from a fault in the reading. It assumes the plan is at fault, which is the reflex the idea warns about. G2-B's claim that the step "already has to separate" them is not supported by the text.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Adopt check: P1's docs/program/evidence/resume-trial-P1/ holds a judgment file with one row per missed fact, giving the fact id, a class (absent, ambiguous, or present-but-missed) and the plan line quoted. Every plan edit in the P1 PR traces to an absent or ambiguous row. A present-but-missed row counts only if the fact is stated verbatim inside §0 or P1. If no line can be quoted, or the fact sits outside §0/P1, the miss is classed absent or ambiguous and the plan is fixed as now. The change has worked if every miss row is filled in this way. It has failed if any miss row is unfilled, or if a plan edit made in the PR has no matching row.
refutation.reason: Narrowed to W3 only: a one-sentence change to P1's cold-resume judging step. Classify each miss and cite the plan line before editing the plan. Edit the plan only for absent or ambiguous facts. Count a miss as present-but-missed only with a verbatim quote from §0 or P1, so the current default of fixing the plan still holds. The W2 claim and the CLAUDE.md-trim landing are refuted, and Dex's remark adds no evidence.

1. The "document only, don't decide" half is already built and enforced on output. C:/Users/User/Documents/projects/EMS_workshop1/.claude/agents/fixflow-explorer.md says "You do not evaluate it" and "Return a plain list. No severity, no recommendation". ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md backs this up in four places: the §5.1 CONTEXT block RULES ("Return constants, lines and declared names; never a severity or a verdict unless your schema has that field"); §5.3 ("Mappers return constants, lines and names; the hypotheses tag routes, it does not judge"); the §5.2 schema at line 424 ("neutral, evidenced, no severity"); and §4.6/§5.3, where skeptics get "the claim, its evidence and its failing condition only", not the analyst's reasoning, with default-refute and citation checks downstream. Blinding is also applied where anchoring actually decides something: in KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md, the PR reviewer re-rules "blind, before reading the author's ruling", and the pilot replays symptoms blind.
2. The "withhold what is being built" half goes against a deliberate design choice, and that choice has a working substitute. §5.1 prepends the program goals to every subagent, and §5.3 requires each brief to name "the goal, the files, the hypotheses it bears on". The harness handles anchoring with schema-bound fact-only output plus fresh-context default-refute skeptics and completeness critics, not by withholding input.
3. The step this rule targets has already passed. In SHIP-PLAN §0 (lines 24-116), a grep for research, explor or diagnos finds no research step. The harness review's graphify skip states that "discovery finished". The phases implement against a written plan.
4. The landing guesses don't transfer. The P1 cold-resume agent already gets only the repository. Refuters have to receive the claim in order to refute it.
5. The evidence is thin. It is one A/B with no numbers (C1658), and the same sources record dissent: C1450 (Vaibhav found the query useful) and C1659 (the co-host calls it "a different style").
6. G2-B's trial cannot settle the question. One paired run cannot separate run-to-run variance from the treatment. Counting "opinion sentences" is circular: an agent that isn't told the plan will of course mention it less. Schema-bound agents also have no field to put opinions in, so both arms would score about 0.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Reopen only if this check fails. Over the first 5 phase sessions, count research or diagnosis subagent outputs that carry a recommendation or decision despite the fact-only schema, plus claims refuted by a skeptic or completeness critic where the cause is traced to the brief's stated goal. If the total is 2 or more, run a paired test with 5 or more question pairs, scored on wrong file:line facts and omissions, not on opinion count.
refutation.reason: The objective, decide-nothing part is already enforced by the explorer agent, the §5.1/§5.3 rules, fact-only schemas and blinded refuters. Withholding the goal reverses a deliberate §5.3 design, rests on one disputed anecdote, and targets a pre-plan research step this plan has already passed, so it does nothing for W3, W4, L2 or L3.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The rule's only evidence is one card (C1568). Its reason is Dex's own hardware: a yubikey touch on every push, so retrying is pointless. Nothing in this harness says a FixFlow push needs a physical key. The user-git-identity memory records only a repo-local name/email, with no signing key. (2) A blanket "stop, don't work around" contradicts a fix the harness itself recorded. memory/project-windows-git-longpaths.md logs 15 of 15 scratchpad clones failing with "Filename too long". The approved response was a workaround, `git -c core.longpaths=true` on each command. Under this rule every one of those sessions would have stalled. On this Windows machine, git failures are often environmental and routine: long paths, a non-fast-forward rejection after the rebase that ship plan §0 "Migrations" requires, or a cherry-pick conflict. (3) The dangerous workarounds are already forbidden by name. Ship plan §0 lines 66-71 say release/drain is built "by git cherry-pick only — never git merge"; `git log release/drain` must show no commit from another PR and is recorded in W0-results; the backend gates must pass on release/drain before tagging. The base Claude Code instructions say never use --no-verify and to look for a safer alternative before `push --force`. The memory says "branch, never main". G2-B's cherry-pick risk is therefore already covered by an outcome check that does not depend on the agent reporting honestly. The one gap left there is a cherry-pick whose conflict was resolved by hand: it ships code the SHA-bound review never read. A stop rule is the wrong fix for that. It needs an outcome check, such as `git patch-id` equality between each squash commit and its cherry-pick, and that is not this family. (4) The benefit on W2 is illusory. W2 says prose rules are self-reported and no hook can see them; this adds another prose rule of the same kind. G2-B's measure is circular: an agent that quietly worked around a failed push would not write that in the phase journal, so "no journal entry" cannot tell compliance from a hidden bypass. (5) G2-A's claim that this is "already default behaviour" is only half right. The base default for a hook failure is "investigate and fix the underlying issue", the opposite of stopping. The conclusion still holds, because the specific bypasses that matter are already named and forbidden.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Reopen only on this evidence: search the P1-P3 phase session transcripts for a git command with a non-zero exit followed in the same turn by `--force`, `--no-verify`, `git merge` onto release/drain, or `branch -D`. A single occurrence reopens the family, and it should come back as a hook or an outcome check, not a prose rule.
refutation.reason: The only evidence is one anecdote whose reason (a hardware-key push) does not apply here. A blanket stop-on-failure rule contradicts the long-paths workaround the harness has already recorded. Ship plan §0 and the base instructions already forbid the dangerous bypasses by name. A self-reported prose rule does nothing for W2.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The only evidence is one asserted prompt rule (C1497, "Step 2 rule", claudelayer create_plan.md). It has no outcome data, so under the owner rules it is a claim. (2) The harness already does most of this. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:839 ran each owner critique point through two Opus verifiers, under the rule "a critique is not taken blindly". ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §5 rule (d), around line 537, lets analysts challenge settled facts with evidence. For prior-session notes there are the HR §6 rows (memory as pointer, the CLAUDE.md head CI check) and plan §0's re-read of changed sections on resume. (3) The harness has no recorded case of a wrong owner correction. The one wrong fact it found, "no Python on this machine" (HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md, Doctor-script row), came from the design doc and memory, and the existing review caught it. The benefit claim therefore has no local base rate. (4) The full form ("spawn new research" for every correction) transfers poorly here. Many owner corrections are decisions, where the owner is the authority. Others are field facts (phones, shop, Docker), which the repo cannot verify and which standing rule 2 already routes to device evidence. Verifying those would reopen rulings the harness records specifically so they are not re-argued. (5) Against G2-B's already-done: SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §0 lines 39-43 only records owner corrections in the journal. It has no verification field, so a correction that states a code or environment fact made by voice mid-phase is still accepted on authority.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Over P1-P3 (three phase sessions), read each PR-body journal at phase close and classify every owner correction as a decision, a field fact, or a checkable repo/environment fact. Pass (format): 100% of checkable-fact entries carry "verified: <path:line or command>" or "contradicted: <evidence>, raised to owner". Keep the rule if at least one correction in the three phases was contradicted or materially refined by its check. Drop it if no checkable-fact corrections occur, or if all were confirmed and the checks added more than about 5 minutes per phase.
refutation.reason: A smaller version survives. When an owner correction mid-phase states a checkable code or environment fact (not a decision, not a field fact), Fable checks it inline with a grep or command; it does not spawn a research agent. The journal entry then carries either "verified: path:line or command" or "contradicted: evidence, raised to owner", and a contradiction goes back to the owner, never silently overridden. Critiques and prior-session notes are already covered (KS §12.7, ORCH §5(d), HR §6). The benefit is unproven because no wrong owner correction is on record, so this is a trial, not an adopt.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The event-log half does not hold up. C1686 is not Dex's (its own card says "Dex adoption not shown"). It is about event-sourced agent loops and deterministic replay for testing, not compliance auditing, and a Claude Code session cannot be replayed deterministically. The append-only journal it would supply already exists: the "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections" journal in the PR body (SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 39-43, HR-C2). C1565 is a forensics command with no outcomes (card: "no outcomes"), so it is anecdotal. (2) The store half is already designed, and it cannot be tested in the window G2-A proposes. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN line 209/476/794 has the prospective lookup log, written by the tool on every `ks lookup` call. Line 480 has `ks close` report whether the lookup ran. Lines 548/670/833 (K24, KS-9) plan the cross-check of "escalations without a lookup" against the main session's dispatch records. The store is also not built, so G2-A's pass condition ("settles 'store consulted or not' on all three phases" P1-P3) cannot be met. (3) Several routine steps already leave independent git/gh records, so they need no transcripts: the `Plan @ <sha>` first line, ticked boxes, the journal, the reviewer verdict naming the head SHA, CI on the PR, and the OWNER-VIEW.md commit (SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 31-55). G2-A's "nothing audits phase compliance" overstates the gap. (4) Both reviewers' "Haiku reads the JSONL" does not fit: HR §6 measured phase-scale sessions at 971k and 580k tokens, far beyond a Haiku window. A deterministic pre-filter of tool_use records has to come first. Nothing here reopens a deliberate skip: it is not a hook or the context system, and HR §4 line 275's M00-M06 is an evaluation-run pipeline, not a compliance check. Feasibility has precedent: HR §6 parsed this session's transcript, and ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN line 586 names the on-disk subagents/workflows/<runId>/journal.jsonl.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Over the first three phase sessions (P1, P2, P3), run a zero-dep Node script at phase close. Python is not on PATH, and transcripts are pruned after cleanupPeriodDays, so it must run at close. The script filters the main-session and subagent JSONL down to tool_use rows: tool, subagent model, Bash command and exit, edited paths. It scores a fixed list of 8 steps that leave no git/gh artifact as evidenced, absent or undecidable: (a) reviewer subagent ran on an Opus model id; (b) the reviewer brief contains the head SHA; (c) the brief contains register ids; (d) the main session made no Edit/Write outside docs/ (Fable never implements); (e) backend/web/mobile gate commands executed with exit 0; (f) `git diff --stat <sha>..origin/main -- docs/program/` was run on resume; (g) implementers' model ids match the routing table; (h) the closing message carries the six answers. Commit the scored rows to the evidence folder with a sha256 manifest. Keep if at least 7 of 8 steps are decidable in every phase and the owner's spot-check of 3 steps per phase agrees 9/9, at under 15 minutes of owner time per phase. Drop it if the subagent model id is not recorded in the JSONL, since (a) and (g) then become undecidable.
refutation.reason: A smaller version survives as a trial: a deterministic, read-only check, run at phase close, of transcript tool_use records for routine steps that leave no git/gh artifact (Opus reviewer, gates run, Fable never edits code, resume diff run). It drops the event-log replay half (refuted, and the PR-body journal already exists) and the "store consulted" criterion, which the KS lookup log and the K24/KS-9 cross-check already cover, for a store that will not exist during P1-P3.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) Both reviewers say live watching is "the cheapest compliance evidence available". That is false. Claude Code keeps a full JSONL transcript of every session: C:/Users/User/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl, confirmed for this session as 9c3f9742-d1e5-4e7b-ad89-bb5bcaada06a.jsonl. The transcript records every Read, Grep, Edit and dispatch. So "the store was never consulted" or "the routine was skipped" (W2) can be seen from outside after the fact, for the whole session, without the owner's real-time attention. A live watch covers only ~15 calls and depends on the owner noticing. 2) The harness already has the slot for live catches. Ship plan §0 lines 39-42 keep a "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections" journal, appended at once. Phase sessions are interactive desktop chats, so the owner can already see and interrupt any tool call. The only new part is the habit of watching on purpose. 3) G2-B's window points attention at the cheapest part of P1. Ship plan lines 322-327 make P1's first act the cold-resume trial: write expected.json, commit it, dispatch a Sonnet agent, judge. The costly wrong turns (Fable implementing, code before the trial is judged, routing errors) come later. 4) The evidence is weak. There are two anecdotes and no numbers. C1532 concerns an unattended Ralph bash loop, which differs from a gated interactive phase. C1685 is a Vulcan CEO's advice, not Dex's. Neither card shows a cost saving.
refutation.what_would_settle_it:
Applies to P1 only. The owner watches from session start through the first CODE commit, not just ~15 calls. He writes each departure from §0 into the existing owner-corrections journal. He does not interrupt the cold-resume subagent, so its recovery stays uncontaminated. After close, a fresh agent audits the P1 transcript JSONL against a fixed §0 checklist:
- draft PR opened at the first commit, body starting `Plan @ <sha>`
- expected.json committed before the dispatch
- trial judged and plan fixed before the first code commit
- no Edit/Write to code by Fable
- implementer routing per design §3
- reviewer verdict names the head SHA and fail-before/pass-after per register id
- six-question close
- OWNER-VIEW.md refreshed
Count three things: L = departures caught live in time to avoid rework; T = departures found only by the transcript audit; S = departures the closing message self-reported. Continue live watching into P2 only if L >= 1 and that departure would have cost at least one commit of rework if found after the fact. Otherwise stop watching and keep the transcript audit as the W2 instrument. If T > S, W2's self-report gap is confirmed and the audit, not watching, is the fix to adopt.
refutation.reason: Narrowed: as compliance evidence for W2, live watching is beaten by the persisted session transcript, which is cheaper and complete. What survives is a one-off owner watch of P1 through its first code commit, using §0's existing owner-corrections journal, kept only if it catches a costly departure in time that the transcript audit would have found too late.

reviews.reason: Before every --body-file write, re-fetch the body with gh pr view --json body. Otherwise an owner's edit in the GitHub UI is silently overwritten (single-writer hazard seen live).

reviews.lens: benefit
reviews.existing_mechanism: Journal appended via whole-body gh pr edit --body-file (plan §0 Resume)
reviews.measurement: Owner corrections go in PR comments and the session moves them into the journal citing the comment; over P1-P3 no owner edit is lost and every journal correction cites its source comment.
reviews.reason: A whole-body rewrite silently drops a concurrent owner edit to the PR body; single-writer costs nothing.

refutation.counter_evidence: Dex's case, where a human hand-edits a plan file while the model is still writing it, has no counterpart in this harness, and the only evidence for it is one live anecdote (C1731). HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md line 270 already records "one owner per kind of state (plan, PR body, W0-results, git)". OWNER-VIEW.md lines 79-83 gives the owner chat and merging as their channels; it never has them edit the PR body. The ship plan changes only through amendment PRs, and SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 36-39 (`Plan @ <sha>` plus `git diff --stat <sha>..origin/main -- docs/program/` on resume) already catches a plan that another session changed. So a "single writer at a time" rule is effectively already in place. G2-A's new PR-comment channel for owner corrections adds an owner process that the routine does not need. What is not covered: SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 39-41 append the journal with `gh pr edit --body-file`, which replaces the whole body, and no rule says where the text comes from. Two things can lose content as a result. First, GitHub renders the Scope checklist as clickable checkboxes, so one owner click in the UI edits the body. Second, a session that rewrites the body from its own memory after compaction drops entries, which is the very failure HR-C2 has the journal there to prevent. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md has no rule about who writes the PR body.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Showing it worked: when each of P1, P2 and P3 closes, pull the PR body's edit history (GraphQL pullRequest.userContentEdits). Every journal line and every ticked box that appears in any earlier revision must still appear in the final body, unless the journal says where it was moved. Pass means zero unexplained losses across all 3 PRs, plus the P1 cold-resume trial recovering every fact that the journal holds.
refutation.reason: Narrowed: the routine has only one writer already (the owner speaks through chat, and the plan changes only through PRs checked by the Plan@sha diff), so a single-writer rule and a PR-comment channel are redundant. What survives is one clause in §0: right before every --body-file write, fetch the live body with `gh pr view --json body` and edit that text, never a copy rebuilt from memory.

label: Commit the specs and prompts, not just final code, as the source of truth.
strongest_evidence: anecdotal: credits Sean Grove; his team's 8-week transition (C1797)
sources: Getting AI to Work in Complex Codebases (2025-08-29, https://github.com/humanlayer/advanced-context-engineering-for-coding-agents/blob/main/ace-fca.md)
sample_quote: "the specs became our source of truth for what was being built and why" (C1797)

reviews.lens: cost, risk and novelty
reviews.existing_mechanism: SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §0: specs/design notes/register committed under docs/program/, draft-PR body opens 'Plan @ <sha>' plus the 'Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections' journal moved to W0-results or a plan amendment at close; evidence folders under docs/program/evidence/ with sha256 manifests. The 'commit the prompts' half (Workflow scripts, briefs) is not saved, which is W5's subject, not this group's
reviews.reason: The harness already treats committed plan, design notes and decision journal as the source of truth; the only part it lacks, saving workflow scripts and briefs, belongs to the W5 review, so nothing new for W2/W3.

reviews.lens: BENEFIT
reviews.existing_mechanism: The specs are already the committed source of truth: SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md plus the cited design notes, the draft PR's first line 'Plan @ <sha>' and resume diff (§0), the 'Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections' journal moved to W0-results or a plan amendment at close, and evidence folders with sha256 manifests. The precedent for committing prompts exists too: docs/program/evidence/harness-ideas/horthy/ has workflows/ and tools/ folders. Phase briefs and workflow scripts are not saved in general (W5).
reviews.measurement: At P1 close, the phase evidence folder holds every brief Fable dispatched (CONTEXT block included), the reviewer's refute-by-default brief and any workflow script, all listed in manifest.sha256. Pass if the file count matches the session's agent dispatches and an outsider can confirm the reviewer was given the register ids.
reviews.reason: The spec half is already done. The cheap gain is the prompt half: commit each phase's briefs and scripts next to their outputs, as the horthy evidence folder already does, so 'was the reviewer told X' can be checked from outside (W2) and a script can be reused (W5). Evidence is only Dex's anecdote; adopt because it costs almost nothing.

refutation.counter_evidence:
1. The spec half is already in place. SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §0 (lines 31-46) requires a draft PR whose body opens with "Plan @ <sha>" (the commit of the plan plus the cited design note), a resume diff over docs/program/, and the "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections" journal, which is moved at close to a W0-results row or a plan amendment. Line 1520 says raw W1/W2 outputs are committed under docs/program/evidence/. P1's first act (lines 323-327) is the cold-resume trial, a direct test of whether the committed plan works as the source of truth. That covers W3. The family does nothing for W1, because committing specs does not shorten CLAUDE.md.
2. The prompt half also has a working precedent. docs/program/evidence/harness-ideas/horthy/ commits three Workflow scripts (workflows/horthy-sweep*-wf_*.js.txt) and nine tool scripts (tools/*.mjs.txt, *.sh.txt) beside a manifest.sha256. So W5's "not saved" is already untrue for review work.
3. G2-A's W2 gain ("was the reviewer told X") is already checkable without the brief. §0 lines 51-55 make the reviewer name, for each register id fixed, the test that fails on base and passes on head. The plan names each phase's reviewer ids (for example line 454: "Opus reviewer briefed with O-10 R1-R7"). An outsider can compare the plan's ids with the verdict's ids, and a missing id shows up there. Every brief is also kept in the local session transcript.
4. The evidence is a single anecdote (Dex crediting Sean Grove, an 8-week transition, no numbers). Under the owner rules it scores as a claim.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Mostly settled. Cheapest confirming check: at P1 close, see whether the Opus reviewer's verdict gives a fail-before/pass-after test for every register id in P1's Scope. If it does, a committed brief adds nothing for W2. If an id is missing, saving the brief becomes a question for the W5 review, not this family.
refutation.reason: The specs half is already done by §0 (Plan @ sha, the decisions journal, committed design notes and evidence), and P1's cold-resume trial tests it (W3). Nothing here helps W1. The prompts half is already practised in the horthy evidence folder, its W2 gain is covered by the per-id reviewer verdict, and saving workflow scripts belongs to the W5 review. So G2-B's already-done stands over G2-A's adopt.

label: An orchestrating Claude Code adds tolerance over deterministic tools, so stale written procedures still work, which also hides doc drift.
strongest_evidence: anecdotal: Kevin's commands were stale after a rename and it still worked (C1399)
sources: AI That Works #45 AI Content Pipeline Revisited (2026-02-17, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U5Gssat8IUw)
sample_quote: "robustness and flexibility and almost like squishiness over a set of deterministic tools" (C1399)
landing_guesses: Doc-drift check for step names

reviews.lens: cost, risk and novelty
reviews.existing_mechanism: Partly done: CLAUDE.md 'Keeping this file honest' has a manual path-resolution grep and a down_revision-chain check; P1 adds a CI check that the CLAUDE.md Alembic head matches the chain; orchestration citation checks; resume re-reads changed docs/program sections. No automated check covers the file paths and step names in SHIP-PLAN §0 or the paths CLAUDE.md names
reviews.measurement: Run CLAUDE.md's existing path-resolution grep once, by hand, over CLAUDE.md and SHIP-PLAN §0 plus the phase being opened, and count paths that do not resolve. If 1 or more is dead (a drift the agent would quietly route around), add that grep as a step in an existing CI job. If none is dead, and none is again at the P1 cold-resume trial, drop the idea.
reviews.reason: The point that a tolerant agent hides stale procedures is a real risk to a self-reported routine (W2/W3). A one-time grep costs minutes and decides whether a CI drift step pays for itself, and it needs no hook, so it does not reopen the pre-commit-hook skip.

reviews.lens: BENEFIT
reviews.existing_mechanism: Some drift checks exist. CLAUDE.md's 'Keeping this file honest' greps for paths and the Alembic head, P1 adds a CI check that CLAUDE.md's head matches the migration chain, and §0's resume runs a git diff of docs/program/ since 'Plan @ <sha>'. Nothing checks that the commands, paths and step names in SHIP-PLAN §0 and the phase entries still resolve.
reviews.measurement: In P1's cold-resume trial, the fresh Sonnet agent must also list every command, path or step name in §0 and P1 that it could not resolve literally and had to work around. Separately, a small resolver script (paths exist, gh/git/npm commands parse, named files and scripts exist) runs over the same text. Count the stale references the script finds that the agent did not flag. If there is at least 1, adopt the resolver as a closing-message check (or a P1 CI step). If there are 0, skip it.
reviews.reason: This is the honest benefit case for W3. An agent that tolerates drift means the cold-resume trial can pass while §0 is already stale, so a passed trial does not prove the plan is accurate. A literal resolver over the plan's commands and paths is cheap, and one bounded run at P1 decides whether the gap is real.

refutation.counter_evidence:
1) The mechanism is already adopted. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md §4 (line 264) adopts a CI check that fails when CLAUDE.md's Alembic head differs from the down_revision chain and warns when a path CLAUDE.md names does not resolve. SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md P1 Deliverables (lines 365-370) puts that check in P1, with an allow-list file, and records that "27 names do not resolve today". That is G2-B's proposed one-time count, already run, with its adopt outcome already taken. G2-B's "existing" line ("No automated check covers ... the paths CLAUDE.md names") is wrong.
2) Plan drift is already covered three ways:
- SHIP-PLAN §0 (lines 36-39): on resume, `Plan @ <sha>` plus `git diff --stat <sha>..origin/main -- docs/program/`, then re-read the changed sections.
- P1 Entry (lines 322-327): the cold-resume trial's judge "fixes any miss in the plan (same PR) before the first code commit".
- ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §4.6 (lines 315-318): the citation check marks each citation LOCATED/MOVED/DEAD_CITATION/ALREADY_FIXED. HARNESS-REVIEW line 357 shows it worked on the plan: every blocker and major citation was re-located and two line drifts were found. Drift was caught, not hidden.
3) The evidence runs the other way. C1399's claim presents tolerance as a benefit ("makes imperfect written procedures workable"). "Hides doc drift" is the reader's inference, with no instance in the source or in this repo. The evidence is one anecdote.
4) G2-A's resolver is biased toward adopt. SHIP-PLAN §0 and P1 name files the phases themselves will create (docs/program/W0-results.md, docs/program/notices/release.md, docs/program/evidence/resume-trial-P1/expected.json, backend/scripts/set_pin.py) and placeholders (`gh pr view <branch>`, `<sha>`). A literal resolver flags all of these by design, so the ">=1 unresolved -> adopt" threshold is met trivially.
5) The "gh/git/npm commands parse / tools exist" half re-adopts the doctor-script skip (HARNESS-REVIEW line 276: "P0a item 10 covers tools"), and that reason still holds.
6) G2-A's other half asks the tolerant agent to report what it tolerated. That is the self-reporting W2 already names, so it adds no independent signal.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Settled for now. Reopen only if, over P1-P5, a phase PR's "Decisions / ruled out" journal or its Opus review records work done against a SHIP-PLAN path, command or step that no longer matched the code. A reference that is merely line-shifted or not yet created does not count. Threshold: 1 or more such case, and then extend the existing P1 path-resolution step to SHIP-PLAN's present-tense code citations only.
refutation.reason: The CLAUDE.md drift check is already an adopted P1 deliverable, and its one-time count is already taken (27 unresolved, allow-listed). Citation checks, the resume diff and the trial judge already cover plan drift. The remaining SHIP-PLAN resolver rests on one anecdote that praises tolerance, flags the plan's references to files not yet created by design, and its tool-check half re-adopts the doctor-script skip.

Count main-session Grep/Glob calls per location question, and count locations the main session later had to find itself after an explorer return. Keep the wording if main-session search calls fall by half or more with no extra missed locations. Do not remove Read.

refutation.counter_evidence:
The family has three parts, and none of them survives.

(1) Dropping Read does not make the agent find-only. Dex's current rpi locator (C0029, dated 2026-11-01) keeps Bash in its tool list (Grep, Glob, Bash, Skill). FixFlow's explorer also has Bash (EMS_workshop1/.claude/agents/fixflow-explorer.md:4). Either agent can still `cat` or `sed` a file. The only version that truly blocked reading was the 2025-12 dotfiles one with Grep/Glob/LS (C1557), and Dex himself later replaced LS with Bash. "Find-only" is already set as a rule in fixflow-explorer.md:11-15: Grep and Glob first, confirm-reads capped at 40 lines, `path:line` output, no judgement.

(2) The trigger "delegate whenever you'd grep/glob more than once" contradicts a written harness rule. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §3 (around lines 90-91) says every subagent pays a fixed overhead before it does any work (CLAUDE.md is about 7.5k tokens, plus the CONTEXT block), "so tiny tasks are inline commands". The same §3 tier table lists "inline pre-flight commands" as Fable's own job, and limits the explorer to "'where is X?' file location from a gate". Two greps cost a few hundred tokens inline, against at least 7.5k to spawn the agent.

(3) Delegating saves little context (L2). The explorer's output contract (line 13: list every hit with its matching line, "do not pick one") returns about the same volume that raw grep output would put in the main session. Only dead-end searches would be saved. Subagents also cannot spawn subagents, so the description trigger only ever reaches the main session. There, Fable gates and judges and does not implement, so it rarely searches much.

The remaining pieces add nothing. Grouping output by purpose is cosmetic. On model choice, Dex uses Sonnet or inherit, while FixFlow's agent is pinned to Haiku, which is cheaper, so there is no L1 gain.

The evidence behind the family is only the frontmatter itself: "asserted" for C0029 and "anecdotal" for C1557, with no numbers. Both reviewers scored evidence at 0.
refutation.reason: Refuted. Removing Read does not enforce find-only while Bash stays, and Dex's own current version keeps Bash. The explorer's own rules already make it locate-only. The "more than once" trigger reverses the harness's §3 rule that tiny tasks run inline, a rule set because of the roughly 7.5k-token subagent overhead. The trigger would also save almost no main-session context, since the explorer returns every hit.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The evidence is weak. Both cards are "evidence asserted": each is a prompt template with no outcome data. C1559 records that the dotfiles prompt contradicts itself ("Note which approach is preferred" against "Don't recommend"), so even the source has not settled the no-ranking property this family claims. 2) The harness already has most of the mechanism. fixflow-explorer (.claude/agents/fixflow-explorer.md in the main checkout) reports every hit as `path:line` and says "do not pick one", so it already gives the unranked file:line locator. The Sonnet MAP schema (docs/ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md:415-427) returns facts with "path:line — quote" evidence and "neutral, evidenced, no severity" anomalies. MAP briefs already name the implementation to model from: S-04 (design:184) says "`run_weekly_export` as the export template", and S-05 (design:185) maps "fetch/refresh patterns". Finding the nearest analogue is therefore a field you put in a brief, not a missing agent. 3) The test-pattern half does not fit how this harness is routed. Plan §0 (SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md:47-51) has Sonnet implement "from a design's test list", and Opus owns all invariant-sensitive code. The tests are specified upstream, so a "Testing Patterns" block feeds a role that is already handed its tests. 4) The W4 benefit is illusory. Another session is adding 11 fixflow-* agents (worktree wizardly-hertz-02c46a/.claude/agents/), and its 340-line fixflow-repo-conventions skill covers slice boundaries for implementers. "One custom agent" is already being fixed, and one more single-purpose agent does nothing for W4/W5's real gap, which is reuse. 5) The harness review's reason for skipping call-graph tooling ("hot paths small enough for grep") also applies to this lighter version: a Sonnet implementer can grep a sibling slice itself. 6) G3-A's measurement cannot run as written. W3 says the routine has never run, so there is no "median of earlier Sonnet PRs" under the Opus-reviewer regime to compare against, and two phases are noise.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Over the first 3 Sonnet-implemented phase PRs, count Opus-reviewer findings whose root cause is "diverged from an existing sibling slice's shape or test pattern" (with file:line to the sibling). If there are 2 or more, add a required "nearest analogue + its test, path:line" field to the Sonnet implementer brief, following the existing S-04 "as the template" practice. That is a brief-template change, not a new agent. With 0-1 such findings, the skip stands.
refutation.reason: The only evidence is an asserted, self-contradicting prompt template. fixflow-explorer (unranked path:line) and the MAP briefs that already name a template (design:184) cover the mechanism, and Sonnet implementers get their tests from the design's test list. A second agent adds upkeep without addressing W4/W5's reuse gap.

refutation.counter_evidence:
(1) The evidence is weak. C1786 is one BAML bug where one of two PRs was kept, with no numbers. C1587 is a whiteboard talk that links worktree-tool products (multiclaude, vibe-kanban, conductor), so it scores as anecdote plus marketing. C0204 is a skill file that says what to do and reports no outcomes. Under the owner rules, none of these is evidence.

(2) G3-A says "nothing generates divergent alternatives". That is false. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md §2 / Q2 and SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §6.6 record an existing run that generated and judged alternatives:
- Four Opus architects reviewed the design against named alternatives.
- Two Opus judges merged the results.
- Two refuters attacked each of the 45 claims.
- The rulings (HR-A1..A4) are binding from v6. Odoo Community vs Enterprise was weighed, and event-sourcing the money journal was rejected.

(3) Parallel work and duplicate analysts were rejected on purpose, and the reasons still hold:
- ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §6 buys "a second lens at the skeptic rather than a duplicate analyst". The v2 change log (line 814) merged O-01/O-02 for that reason.
- The same §6 says "Owner decisions gate the design agents", because spending Opus before the owner answers is spending it on a guess.
- HARNESS-REVIEW (line ~205) refuted "spare sessions so P9a-1 in parallel costs nothing". P7a→P8a→P8b→P9a-1 are four coupled Opus PRs that each need Docker.

(4) G3-A's trial target does not exist in the plan. Its example was the Odoo export shape. That shape is decided by the owner and accountant at P9-0b (SHIP-PLAN, "the decide-before-build gate"): granularity, basis and custody, recorded as an amendment to w2/O-07-design.md. Every later design-bearing phase already has a fixed design spec:
- P9a-1 implements O-07 parts 1, 2 and 6.
- P10a implements parts 3, 4 and 7, with register ids O07-F11/F14/F17 and ruling R9.

The only open design question left is P5-spike (commercial SDK vs patched Expo). A field measurement on a phone answers it, not divergent interface drafts.
refutation.reason: The evidence is anecdotal or asserted only (n=1, no numbers). The harness already ran a review of named alternatives: four architects, two judges, refuters (HARNESS-REVIEW §2, ship plan §6.6). §6 deliberately chose a second lens at the skeptic over a duplicate analyst and puts owner gates in front of design agents. Every remaining design phase is pinned to w2/O-07-design.md or to the P9-0b owner/accountant gate, so a saved design-it-twice workflow would have nothing to run on in this plan and buys nothing on W5.

refutation.counter_evidence:
1. Both reviewers picked the wrong trial site. In SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md, P12a (line 656) is a fix to how payment idempotency keys are minted and rotated. It is owned by Opus because it touches money, and it involves no screen design. P12 (line 1206) is a set of web defect fixes: the revenue tile, board polling, bare catch blocks that should surface serverReason, and keeping the token on network or 5xx failures. None of that is layout work a mockup could settle. The phases that actually build new screens are P2b-1 (the D7 Drain Report screen, the D6/E4 login banner, the Discard copy, line 421), P5b-1 (banners, the OEM onboarding step, typed-id login, line 834), P9b (the approval and reconciliation pages, line 1166) and P10a (the exports page, line 1177).
2. Both measurements compare against "the previous UI phase without a mockup". No such baseline exists, because the phase routine has never run (W3).
3. C0228's reason for keeping everything in one file is a limit of HumanLayer's own viewer ("sibling files render unstyled"). The Artifact tool here publishes extra files through `files`, so the single-file rule is a convenience, not a requirement.
4. Both cards have evidence graded anecdotal. C0732 says "Example linked as a tweet; no measurement", and the owner rules treat that as a claim, not evidence.
5. A mockup is an alignment step done before the build, not a verifier. It adds no backpressure on outputs (L3). It touches W4 only slightly and does nothing for W2, W3 or W5.
6. This is a one-developer repository. The content of the screens is already fixed by design docs that have been through refuter passes (w2/O-10, O-03), so most of the risk is in behaviour, not in how the screens look. A mockup can only check copy and states.
No existing mechanism covers this: neither docs/ nor .claude/ in this worktree mentions mockups or wireframes, apart from the evidence collected for this review.
refutation.what_would_settle_it:
Run the trial only on the new-screen phases, in plan order: P2b-1, P5b-1, P9b, P10a.
- Before implementation, Sonnet produces one rough HTML mockup showing the screen's states and exact copy (for P2b-1: Drain Report empty, partial and failed; the login banner; Discard "server refused" and "could not reach"). The owner glances at it; this is not a blocking gate.
- In the PR journal, tag every owner correction as either "caught at mockup" or "after the first implementation push". For P2b-1 and P5b-1, also count corrections to copy or states found after the EAS build, during P2c, P4a and P5c.
- Pass: in at least 2 of the 4 phases the mockup catches at least one correction; there are no copy or state corrections after the build in the mobile phases; each mockup takes no more than 30 minutes of session time, and the owner's glance no more than 10 minutes.
- Drop it if the first two phases (P2b-1 and P5b-1) catch nothing at the mockup stage.
refutation.reason: A smaller version survives: a rough mockup of states and copy, written into the brief for the 4 new-screen phases and checked by the owner without blocking the phase. It is worth most on the mobile phases, where a copy mistake costs a new fleet APK build. It is not a skill or a CLAUDE.md rule, and it does not apply to P12a or P12; the single-file reason does not transfer.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The Claude Code skills doc (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md, fetched 2026-11-04) lists disable-model-invocation in its frontmatter table, and the entry says it "Also prevents the skill from being preloaded into subagents". (2) The 13 packages have already landed in commit 1ac6b15 (worktree wizardly-hertz-02c46a). Eleven agent definitions in C:/Users/User/Documents/projects/EMS_workshop1/.claude/worktrees/wizardly-hertz-02c46a/.claude/agents/*.md preload 12 of the 13 skills through `skills:`. The "Agent definitions" section of .claude/skills/README.md makes that preload the wiring rule (design §9). So setting the flag on any of those 12 silently strips the skill from the agent built to carry it. That answers G3-A's open "check preload with the flag set": it breaks. G3-B's "record auto vs manual for each skill" cannot pick manual-only for those 12. (3) The 13th skill, fixflow-orchestration, is the main session's own orchestration contract. Auto-loading it every phase is the point, and making it name-only would add an owner-must-remember step, which is a new W2 failure mode. (4) The flag exists for side-effecting, user-timed workflows (/deploy, /commit). README content rule 4 bars any skill from instructing a deploy, restore, key rotation, customer message or install, so none of the 13 is such a workflow, and the family's target set ("heavy or user-initiated") is empty here. (5) The existing defence is already in place. The README Layout section requires each description to say when NOT to use the skill, and all 13 carry "Use when / Do NOT use" scoping. (6) The evidence is weak. C0639 is an 80% figure with no measurement. C0773 is a fix for Codex in HumanLayer's own product, not Claude Code. C0015, C0208 and C0528 are config values only. (7) The context benefit is small. Thirteen descriptions capped at about 1024 characters each come to roughly 3k tokens, against an HR-C4 threshold of 500k. Nothing touches W1 or W5.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: The flag question is settled by the docs. One residual question remains: would "invoke only by name" wording help in the main session? To check, count Skill-tool loads by the main session (not subagents) of the 12 agent-preloaded skills across the next 3 phase-session transcripts. If there are 0 loads that the phase's brief or PR does not cite, close the question. If there are 2 or more, reword only those descriptions, and never set the flag on them.
refutation.reason: The flag would break the `skills:` preload that 12 of the 13 landed skills depend on (Claude Code docs; .claude/agents/*.md). The 13th is the main session's contract and needs to auto-load. No skill is a side-effecting user-initiated workflow (README rule 4). The README's "Do NOT use" descriptions already narrow triggering, and the evidence is anecdotal and from other harnesses. Both reviewers are overruled (trial and adopt both become skip). The one guard worth writing down: never set disable-model-invocation on a skill named in an agent's `skills:` list.
