refutation.counter_evidence:
1. Most of the "shape" is already decided before coding. The ship plan's phase Scopes pin file layout and data shape, taken from Opus W2 design notes. P8a (SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md line 1054) names `void_payment`, the columns `voided_at`/`voided_by`/`recorded_by`, the FK mode (NOT VALID) and the payload `{payment_id, amount_paisa, method, reason}`, citing w2/O-06 and w2/O-07-design.md. P2b-2 (line 458) names the script, its flags (`--test-window`, `--snapshot-fuel`, `--fuel-baseline`), its output files and the matching rules (w2/O-10-design.md E6). On those phases the review is not where the shape first gets decided, which is the core of the card's "costliest moment" argument.
2. Backend call paths are mostly fixed already. They follow the router → service → repository convention (CLAUDE.md, "Where things live"), and CI's import-linter and ESLint boundaries already flag a cross-slice edge nobody planned.
3. Things I could not check. The w2 design notes are not in the pr182 checkout, so I could not see whether they already include signatures. F035, which both reviewers cite, was not in review-input.
4. The evidence is anecdotal, with no numbers. C0736 even says HumanLayer's own first version was hard to read and had to be reworked.
5. G3-A's measurement cannot tell anything apart. It compares only two invariant phases against unlike phases, with no baseline, and the routine has never run (W3).
6. What still holds up: the plan never asks for signatures or call-stack trees, and control-flow-heavy work is not pinned. That covers the mobile outbox and sync paths, whose known race is a control-flow defect, and the new accounting slice in P9a-1/P9a-2.
refutation.what_would_settle_it:
Run it on the first 4 Opus-owned code phases that change control flow or add a new public surface (candidates: P2a, P7a, P9a-1, P9a-2). Skip phases whose Scope already pins the shape, such as P2b-2 and P8a. In each, before the first code commit, the Opus implementer drafts a "Shape" block in the existing draft PR body: the public signatures it touches, a file-tree diff, and a call-stack tree in diff syntax for any control-flow change. Fable or the owner reviews it before any code is written. Count three things:
(a) Shape-time corrections that changed the plan, logged in the existing "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections" journal.

reviews.measurement: Before P1, restate each §0 routine step as a completion criterion with an observable artefact (PR body line, a reviewer comment naming the head SHA, an OWNER-VIEW commit, evidence manifest entries). At P1 close, a fresh Haiku agent with only gh and git checks each criterion. Count steps it can confirm or refute from outside against those that remain self-report only. Keep the format if 8 or more of about 10 steps become externally checkable.
reviews.reason: This is the cheapest direct attack on W2: compliance becomes visible from artefacts without adding a hook.

refutation.counter_evidence: All three parts of the family already exist in the harness. (1) Ordered steps with checkable completion criteria: SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md has 46 phase "Done when." lines (e.g. P1 at line 373: "curl -i on an unknown path shows the marker; a manual boot with no env fails closed"), and every Scope is a checkbox list. §0 (lines 31-56) already requires each routine step to leave an artefact that someone outside the session can inspect: a draft PR at the first commit, a body whose first line is `Plan @ <sha>`, the "Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections" journal, a reviewer verdict naming the PR head SHA, a fail-on-base/pass-on-head test for each register id, and the OWNER-VIEW.md refresh. P1's cold-resume trial (lines 322-327) commits expected.json. (2) Long templates in sibling reference files: .claude/skills/README.md "Layout" already requires a `references/` folder for upstream and FixFlow references, keeps the SKILL.md body to about 400 lines or less, and caps a package at about 150 KB. (3) One source of truth per rule: CLAUDE.md declares itself authoritative over prose docs. Skills README Content rule 2 says skills must never contradict CLAUDE.md or §0. §0 moves each journal entry "to its owner" at close. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN §7.3 says the store links to the journal instead of restating it, "so the approach has one owner". G3-A's trial measures nothing about the proposed format change. About 8 of the roughly 10 §0 steps can already be checked with gh and git as written, so its pass threshold (8 or more of 10) would pass with no restatement at all. Any benefit comes from running an outside audit, which belongs to a separate verifier family. On W2 the benefit is illusory. A completion criterion written into a SKILL.md is still checked by the same agent that ran the step, so it does not make compliance visible from outside. The W2 example, "the store was never consulted", is not a §0 step. KS §7.2-7.3 already logs it through lookup ids in the PR journal and `missed_check` rows. The only evidence is one HumanLayer author's assertion in two skills (C0924, evidence: asserted), with no numbers.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Cheapest check: read .claude/skills/README.md past line 80 for a per-step done-check rule. If none is there, the only residual is one optional line for the skills session: "a procedure step ends with the command output or artefact that shows it done; restate a CLAUDE.md or §0 rule only by citation". Separately, for W2, run a gh and git audit of P1's §0 artefacts at P1 close. That audit needs no format change.
refutation.reason: Already done. The ship plan's Done-when lines and §0's artefact-producing routine cover the completion criteria, and the skills README already prescribes references/ and the no-contradiction rule. G3-A's trial cannot tell the format change from the status quo, its W2 benefit is illusory, and the only evidence is an uncounted assertion from one author.

Run the agent 3 times with the skill and 3 times without. Count verified facts recovered and false claims each time. refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The harness already has G3-B's rule. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §9 (lines ~715-739, PR #182) lists only domain-knowledge skills (Android background, adb field debugging, recovery, Odoo, offline-sync review, Alembic safety, ASVS, homelab, EAS, Maestro, Pakistan accounting), plus two project-authored ones. Commit 1ac6b15 on claude/wizardly-hertz-02c46a puts these into .claude/skills/README.md. Every one of the 13 has a "Plan phases" column and a register-id column. Content rule 1 there reads "FixFlow facts over generic advice." The sourced parts are single domain extracts pinned to a SHA, not process packs: affaan-m/ECC skills/fastapi-patterns only, unclecatvn skills/odoo-workflow, and bolens backup-restore/homelab-triage. A grep of the PR #182 docs for superpowers, get-shit-done, oh-my-claude or "skill pack" finds nothing, so no public workflow pack is installed or planned. Each agent preloads only its own skill (agents/*.md `skills:` lines), and each skill description states when NOT to use it. (2) The cited evidence shows a null result, not harm. In the June run (C0673), all four packs beat baseline on SWE-bench Pro (54.99/54.45/54.17/53.08 vs 52.80). In July (C0672) the gaps are mixed in sign and all under 2 points on one seed. On SlopCodeBench (n=3), the spreads of up to ±2.3 exceed every gap (at most 1.1). The runs used Codex gpt-5.5 as a single agent with multi-agent packs flattened (C0679), not Claude subagents with a preloaded domain skill. C0690 is a secondhand HN reply. (3) G3-A's trial is contaminated and has too little power to show anything. The skills were written from the W1/W2 register (README index rows cite O-01 F01..F20, O-07 F1..F17 and so on). Asking whether an agent recovers verified register facts with and without the skill therefore hands the with-skill arm the answers. Two questions × 3 runs per arm cannot settle a difference that the source itself could not settle with 36 problems × 3 seeds. The keep-or-unload rule would then drop skills on noise. It would also reopen the low-priority measurement skip (M00–M06) at roughly 11 agents × 12 runs, most of them Opus.
refutation.reason: Rejected as an adopt: "no public workflow packs; domain skills scoped to phases" is already design §9 and the skills README index, and no pack is installed or planned. Rejected as a trial: the source data are null on Codex, not harm on Claude, and the proposed with/without test hands the with-skill arm the register answers and is too small to detect anything.

Its "Layout" convention requires an UPSTREAM.md in every sourced or researched package, giving the repo URL, commit SHA, paths taken, SPDX licence, fetch date, and what was Taken, Changed and Rejected. All 11 sourced/researched packages have one; for example, android-background-execution/UPSTREAM.md pins zakariaf/ReactNative-Skills@41a0e66d… and dont-kill-my-app@3616bc8b…. Upstream can keep moving without touching the repo copy, which changes only through a git commit and PR. So C0680's mechanism (a pack moving past the tested commit) cannot happen here, and G3-B's own success test ("records source URL and commit SHA… an update is a deliberate PR") is met by construction. The README also requires absolute dates and exact versions (rule 6), and upstream "verified against version X on date" notes are kept (rule 1). G3-B's "at-least-two-weeks-old rule" is actually only the graphify trial design (HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md:299), not a general dependency rule. 2) The re-measurement half fails on its own evidence. C0680 reports that pack-update effects (GSD +1.2, OMC +0.5 Strict) were smaller than model drift (about +1.75). A benchmark harness could not separate them, let alone one developer with no benchmark and about 40 phases. It also brings back the skipped measurement pipeline M00–M06 (HARNESS-REVIEW:275, "a month of research established no gain; owner priority low"), and that reason still holds. 3) The other cards do not transfer. C1324 is about regressing *other teams* when shared prompts change; Dex lists it as unsolved and offers no fix, and there is one developer here. C0245 is a second-hand, number-free report from a 300-engineer org mapping skill versions to session sentiment; n=1 has no population to map. reviews.existing_mechanism: P1 cold-resume trial (HARNESS-REVIEW §4) uses the same frozen-facts method for the routine
reviews.reopens_skipped: Measurement pipeline M00–M06: a single-variable replay on frozen tasks is a bounded experiment, not the skipped standing pipeline
reviews.measurement: Use as the method for F066. With the frozen W1/W2 question set and its verified register answers held fixed, change exactly one variable (skill on or off, or effort level). Run 3 times each; count verified facts and false claims. A harness change ships only if it does not lower recall or raise false claims.
reviews.reason: The register gives this repo a ready-made answer key, which makes one-variable replays cheap and decisive.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) No evidence. Both cards (C0547, C0643) are asserted and second-hand: Dex restating Vaibhav's unconference takeaway. C0643's own source says that in SlopCodeBench "harness is confounded with model", so it cannot separate harness effects. The premise that "plan, skills and environment are the only variables" leaves out run-to-run sampling noise. (2) The repo already uses this method for the harness changes it trials. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md §4 (line 268) has P1's cold-resume trial: a fresh Sonnet agent, ten frozen facts, expected.json (SHIP-PLAN line 322). HR §5 has the graphify trial design: ten fixed questions, grep/ast-grep as ground truth, keep-only-if. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN KS-5 is a blind replay of 20 or more positive and 40 or more hard-negative queries against two incumbent arms at the same tier and budget, with thresholds frozen at KS-4 and a kill criterion. KS-9 is the with/without comparison. (3) The "replay a known-good plan" half has nothing to replay. The routine has never run (W3; P1's first act is the routine's first test), and one replay costs a full phase of Opus, Sonnet and Docker gates. (4) Making it a standing gate ("a harness change ships only if…", G3-A) brings back what HR §4 line 275 skipped as "Measurement pipeline M00–M06; evaluation-run schema". That skip's reason still holds: KS design C-01 records the clinic's WF-02 baseline-vs-treatment trial, the same kind of measurement, and the owner's month of it found no gain. (5) At one developer's sample size it would pass almost anything. The deck's measured cards show skill effects under 2 points on 729 SWE-bench Pro instances (C0672), and at n=3 the spread of ±2.3 exceeds the gaps (C0673). G3-A's 3-run, "does not lower recall" threshold therefore passes any skill short of gross harm. Its claim that the result is "decisive" is false. (6) The variable may not even be controllable. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §9 (lines 717-720) says .claude/skills/ holds main-session skills, and workflow subagents get skills only through distillation into agent definitions. A subagent replay with "the skill on or off" may not vary anything. (7) It does nothing for W2: a replay measures capability under test, not whether the routine was followed in live sessions. For W5, it assumes saved workflows exist; it does not create them.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: The open question is whether this repo's noise floor allows one-variable replays at all. It can be checked during P1's existing cold-resume trial for two extra Sonnet dispatches. Dispatch the same fresh agent 3 times on the identical expected.json, with no change, and count the facts recovered (out of 10) and the false claims per run. If recall across identical runs spreads by 2 or more, or false claims vary, a one-variable skill or effort replay at n≤3 cannot detect real effects, and the family stays dead. If the spread is 0–1, a single skill-on/off pair on the same key becomes a credible gross-harm check. Before that, confirm the skill actually loads in the replay agent by checking for a Skill call in its transcript.
refutation.reason: The transferable half (a fixed answer-key trial changing one variable) is already how the repo trials changes (P1 cold-resume trial, KS-5 blind replay, the graphify trial design). The novel half has no known-good phase to replay, would bring back the skipped M00–M06 evaluation regime as a ship gate, and at n≈3 cannot detect the under-2-point skill effects in the measured cards (C0672/C0673). Nothing new should be adopted.

strongest_evidence: anecdotal: Vaibhav '5-7 great skills beat 70'; team-of-10 Docker-environments analogy; observed sprawl from three prompts to a hundred (C1356, C1276, C1013)
sample_quote: "Prune, prune, prune, prune, prune." (C1356)

reviews.lens: cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is reopened, what it costs one developer on Windows to build, run and keep honest
reviews.measurement: After the next five phase sessions, grep their transcripts for each of the 13 skills' invocations. Retire every skill invoked zero times. The trial succeeds if at least one is retired and no later phase has to re-add it.

reviews.lens: benefit-seeker: the best honest case for what each family buys on W4/W5 (and W2 where it applies), with evidence scored strictly
reviews.measurement: After 5 phase sessions with the 13 packages present, count loads per skill (Skill calls plus `skills:` preloads on agents actually dispatched) from the transcripts. Retire, or move out of .claude/skills/, every package with zero loads in phases its description targets.
reviews.reason: Thirteen packages at once is sprawl risk on W1 and W4. A use count turns 'prune' into a decision instead of a taste.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The skill set is already a curated set, not sprawl. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §9 (lines 715-741) is a ranked list in which each skill is tied to the agents it improves. The packages from commit 1ac6b15 (worktree wizardly-hertz-02c46a, .claude/skills/README.md) are indexed by register id and plan phase. Each description has "Do NOT use ... (use <sibling>)" routing, and the content rules cap size and require provenance. 10 of the 13 are preloaded by exactly one agent through `skills:`, so a subagent's context holds one or two skills, never 13. (2) The rationale for pruning is team adoption, and it does not carry over to one developer. C1356 rests on a product-manager analogy (cut features used by about 10% of users). C1276 rests on a team of 10 where shared use raises the median. With one user, "adoption" is undefined. C0317's evidence is two chapter titles. C1013's "three prompts to a hundred" does not describe 13 skills each scoped to phases. (3) "One prescriptive workflow, not variants" is already in place: ship plan §0 is the single routine, and the fixflow-orchestration skill encodes it once. (4) G3-B's measurement would do harm. The next five phases (P0a, P0b, P1, P2a, P2b-1) target none of odoo-accounting-import, pakistan-accounting-context (P9+), android-background-execution (P5*), android-field-debugging or maestro-device-e2e (P2c+), so "retire every skill invoked zero times" deletes packages that later phases need. It also counts only Skill invocations and misses `skills:` preloads on dispatched agents. Its success test, "at least one retired", rewards deleting something whether or not that was right. (5) The cap (Vaibhav's "5-7 beat 70") is opinion, and 13 is nowhere near 70.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run a tally across the first six phase sessions (P0a, P0b, P1, P2a, P2b-1, P2b-2). At each phase close, grep that session's transcript JSONL, main plus subagent files, including Workflow script sources, for (a) Skill calls by skill name and (b) dispatches or agentType mentions of each agent that preloads a skill. Tabulate the results against the "Plan phases" column of the README index, and count only phases that the skill's own description targets. The trial pays off if it finds at least one skill that 2 or more completed phases targeted and none loaded (fix its description or retire it), or at least one phase session with no fixflow-orchestration load (a W2 signal that the routine was skipped). If every targeted skill was loaded in every phase that targeted it, the tally carries no information and is dropped after six sessions. No skill is retired for zero loads in phases that do not target it.
refutation.reason: The cap and the team-adoption pruning are refuted: the set is already curated against design §9, the harness already has one routine, and the team-compounding evidence does not apply to one developer. What survives is a phase-scoped trigger tally: for each skill, count loads (Skill calls plus preloads through dispatched agents) only in the phases its description names. Its value is catching skills whose triggers never fire and giving W2 a signal from outside the session, not pruning.

Sourced skills are "fetched and adapted" and distilled into project agent definitions, never installed raw. reviews.lens: cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is reopened, what it costs one developer on Windows to build, run and keep honest
reviews.measurement: In P1, after the session, list the transcript's raw Skill and Agent/agentType tool calls and compare them with what the closing message claims was used. Pass: every claimed skill or agent use has a matching call, and any missing one is recorded as a defect.

reviews.lens: benefit-seeker: the best honest case for what each family buys on W4/W5 (and W2 where it applies), with evidence scored strictly
reviews.measurement: At P1 close, run a read-only node script over the phase session's transcript JSONL, subagent transcripts included. It lists every Skill, Agent/Task (with agentType and model) and Workflow call. Compare that list with the closing message's claims: reviewer dispatched, skills loaded, store consulted, cold-resume agent run. Count claims confirmed, contradicted and unresolvable. Keep it as a phase-close step if 80% or more of routine claims resolve either way. Drop it if the transcript format makes most of them unresolvable.
reviews.reason: This directly separates 'store never consulted' from 'routine skipped' (W2) without a hook. The risk is the undocumented transcript format, the same kind of risk behind the context-system skip.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The card's mechanism does not transfer, and its evidence is weak. C0054 is a CI test suite for a skill package that runs on more than one host. It runs `codex exec` headless, asserts stderr lacks 'failed to load skill', compares installed with explicit-path loading, and turns a delegation tool on and off. The card scores it "asserted": a script with no results, plus one anecdote about the npx installer layout. The Claude Code desktop app gives the user no stderr to read, and the delegation-tool toggle is a Codex concern. Both reviewers replaced the card with a different idea, a transcript audit at phase close. C0054 gives that idea no evidence. (2) The harness already has part of it. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md §7.8 (lines 480 and 548) and §9 (K24, line 833) already name "the main session's own dispatch records, read at KS-9" as the one cross-check on compliance. That covers only one count, escalations made without a store lookup, and only at KS-9, not every phase. So novelty is partial, not 3. (3) It reopens no skip. HARNESS-REVIEW §6 (lines 310-325) already parsed this session's transcript JSONL to measure compaction, so the undocumented-format worry behind the context-system skip has already been accepted for reading transcripts. The doctor-script skip (line 276) was about tools (P0a item 10). The M00–M06 skip (line 275) was about a measurement pipeline. Neither covers a one-off dispatch tally. (4) The routine has the gap. SHIP-PLAN §0 lines 44-56 make the closing message's "what evidence ran", the Opus reviewer dispatch and "Fable never implements" self-reported. Git and PR artifacts confirm the draft PR, the Plan @ sha line, the journal and OWNER-VIEW, but not who was dispatched with which model, or whether the store was consulted. (5) Feasibility check on this machine. One grep over the current session's transcript (C:/Users/User/.claude/projects/C--Users-User-Documents-projects-EMS-workshop1--claude-worktrees-harness-ideas-horthy-2371b9/9c3f9742-d1e5-4e7b-ad89-bb5bcaada06a.jsonl) listed 180 Bash, 10 Workflow and 2 Skill calls (workflow-authoring), and 0 Agent calls. Agents dispatched by a workflow carry their model and agentType only in the subagents/ and workflows/ journals, so the tally must read those too, and that is the part most likely to go unresolved. Transcripts are local and are subject to cleanup, so the tally's output has to be committed to the phase's evidence folder.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run one read-only tally per session over P1 and the next two phase sessions, 3 in all. It reads the main JSONL plus subagents/ and workflows/ and lists Skill calls by name, Agent and Workflow dispatches with the model and agentType each subagent journal records, Bash `ks lookup`/`ks close` calls, and Edit or Write calls the main session made outside docs/. Commit its output to the phase evidence folder with a sha256. For each claim in the closing message and PR body, record whether the tally confirms it, contradicts it, or cannot resolve it. The claims to check are: an Opus reviewer was dispatched, Fable made no code edits, which skills were used, whether the store was consulted, and whether the cold-resume agent ran. Separately count the claims git or PR artifacts could not already settle. Keep it as a phase-close step if, in all 3 sessions, at least 80% of claims resolve and the run takes under 5 minutes. Adopt it if it finds at least 1 contradiction or an unreported Fable code edit. Drop it if fewer than 80% resolve (for example, workflow-subagent models cannot be read), or if, across all 3 sessions, it resolves nothing that the PR and git artifacts had not already settled.
refutation.reason: The card's version does not transfer: stderr checks, installed versus path-loaded skills, and a delegation-tool toggle make a cross-host CI suite that cites no results. A smaller version survives: a read-only tally of the phase transcript's Skill, Agent and Workflow, `ks lookup` and main-session Edit/Write calls, compared with the closing message. It extends to the whole routine the K24 dispatch-record cross-check the knowledge-store design already plans for KS-9. It is the only outside check on W2 that needs no hook, and a parse of this session's transcript showed it can be done here.

reviews.existing_mechanism: Evidence folders with sha256 manifests (outputs only); ad hoc precedent: docs/program/evidence/harness-ideas/horthy/tools/split-review-input.mjs.txt
reviews.measurement: How we know it worked: every phase's evidence manifest lists the workflow script and the computed briefs (the CONTEXT block plus each role prompt, the reviewer brief with its register ids). A cold reader, such as P1's resume agent, can then say from the folder alone which agents were briefed with what.
reviews.reason: Committing the script and briefs beside the outputs costs almost nothing. It starts the missing workflow library (W5) and makes the reviewer brief inspectable (W2).

refutation.counter_evidence: Both reviewers say evidence folders keep outputs but not scripts. That is false at HEAD 95cc9e6. docs/program/evidence/harness-ideas/horthy/workflows/ holds horthy-sweep-wf_5b59f5db-8bc.js.txt and the round-2 and round-3 scripts, which its README describes as "exactly as run". They are listed in manifest.sha256 (lines 64-66), and tools/*.mjs.txt are listed too. Each saved script builds its prompts inline: the CONTEXT block at line 43, plus a title, file list and note for each reader. So every rendered prompt follows deterministically from the script plus its args (args.S, args.INV, args.today). Only the args are not saved; INV is mostly covered by inventory.md. Dumping every prompt at every step would therefore duplicate the script. The family's own evidence is weak. C0289 is graded 'asserted': an opinion plus an anecdote, and the print-every-prompt method is Aaron's, not Dex's. Nothing measures what reading prompts gains, and the owner rules score that as a claim. Two real gaps remain. First, saving scripts is not yet a rule: the older W1/W2 evidence README (pr182 docs/program/evidence/README.md) records outputs only, and neither ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §7 'Evidence rules' nor ship plan §0 requires the script, its args or the per-PR Opus reviewer brief to be kept. Second, a fresh phase session follows only what is written down.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: How we know it worked: check the next 3 committed evidence folders that come from a Workflow run (P1's cold-resume trial among them). Each manifest must list the script as run and an args JSON. Every phase PR from P1 on must carry its Opus reviewer brief verbatim, in the PR or the folder, with the register ids. Pass if 3 of 3 folders and every PR comply. Spot check: hand a fresh agent one cited output and its folder; it must reproduce the brief that produced that output.
refutation.reason: Only a smaller version survives. Saving the script as run already happens ad hoc (commit 95cc9e6, horthy/workflows/*.js.txt in the manifest). What to adopt is writing that practice into the evidence rules (ORCHESTRATION §7 / ship plan §0), adding the args JSON and keeping the per-PR reviewer brief verbatim. Skip the asserted parts: dumping every prompt at each step, and a reviewer step that reads prompts for filler.

reviews.measurement: Commit the 2-3 workflow shapes that have already recurred (mapper fan-out then citation check, default-refute skeptic panel, judge panel) as parameterised scripts under the repo with a version header. Over the next 3 phases that need a workflow, count those started from a saved script with only args changed against those written from scratch. Keep the library if 2 or more of 3 reuse a saved script with no loss of verification steps.
reviews.reason: This addresses W5 head-on at low cost. The shapes demonstrably recur across W1, W2 and this review; the measurement checks whether reuse actually happens.

refutation.counter_evidence:
(1) The evidence is empty. Of the six members, C0246 is a Warp product pitch and C0968 is HumanLayer launch marketing ("customer names asserted, no data"). C0324 says "no outcomes reported". C0173, C0174 and C0461 are stated beliefs, two of them borrowed from Crawshaw ("no data", "no demo from HumanLayer"). Both reviewers scored evidence 0.

(2) The harness already does what the family describes. CLAUDE.md, docs/program/SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §0, docs/ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md, .claude/agents/fixflow-explorer.md and the .claude/skills/ packages are all plain files held in the repo. Evidence is committed with sha256 manifests and memory holds pointers only (HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md §4 adopted both). Nobody is proposing a black-box factory or a visual integration manager. Claude Code is the one closed component, and the family offers nothing to replace it.

(3) W5's premise, "workflows are not saved", is false. This worktree commits 10 workflow and tool scripts under docs/program/evidence/harness-ideas/horthy/{workflows,tools}/*.js.txt and *.mjs.txt. Branch claude/knowledge-store-research-9c609c commits two more: ks-critique-check-wf_2c872948-51a.js.txt and knowledge-store-refuters-v13-wf_2e148d62-c8f.js.txt. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md lines 970-971 names them. They are kept as .txt "so the frontend lint job does not parse" them, so a runnable .js library held in the repo would need an ESLint exception.

(4) G3-A's trial (save 2-3 parameterised scripts) is really the library idea, which G3-B assigns to F088, and these cards do not support it. Its benefit is also thin. The scripts are short: 34, 73 and 161 lines for the sweeps, 76 for the KS refuters. Two scripts from different tasks share only 5 distinct non-blank lines, so task-specific briefs and schemas make up almost all of each script. The verification steps live in plan §0 and orchestration §5, not in reusable script boilerplate.
refutation.reason: The evidence is all claims and marketing. The harness is already open, repo-held files, and its workflow scripts are already committed as evidence. The residual idea, a parameterised library, belongs to F088 and should be judged there, not under this principle.

label: Hand-write golden example patterns (and capture exemplar diffs or working setups) for a skill to follow before automating, since agents replicate patterns.
strongest_evidence: anecdotal: HumanLayer practice; diff 'verifiably true' and teams keep sample PRs; Storybook copy bootstrapped five components in about five minutes (C1678, C1141)
sources: AI That Works #53 Agentic Coding for Frontend Apps (2026-04-14, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=adpUOpW85ns)
sample_quote: "build out what we call golden patterns by hand before setting the agent loose" (C0751)

reviews.lens: benefit
reviews.existing_mechanism: Partial: CLAUDE.md invariants name exemplar files (completionPrefill.ts, syncClassification.ts, try_claim); no skill carries a reference diff
reviews.measurement: For the 13 skills being added, attach a golden exemplar (commit SHA of a reference diff, e.g. a NOT VALID/VALIDATE migration, an outbox kind with client_id) to the migration and outbox-kind skills only; over the next 2 phases that add a migration or outbox kind, count Opus-reviewer findings that are pattern deviations (FK not NOT VALID, missing client_id, missing alembic pair). Pass = 0 such findings; fail = any, then drop the exemplar lines.
reviews.reason: The best-supported family here, and cheap: one SHA per skill points agents at a pattern this repo already paid for. But it rests on anecdote, so run it on two skills before making it a convention.

reviews.lens: Cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is re-opened, what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build, run and keep it honest, and what could go wrong.
reviews.existing_mechanism: Partly: CLAUDE.md names exemplars in prose (try_claim pattern, test_identity_integration.py, compare_secret, syncClassification.ts); no skill carries a worked exemplar diff
reviews.measurement: For the next 3 phases that each add a recurring shape (an Alembic migration with an FK, an outbox kind, a slice endpoint), put an exemplar pointer (commit SHA plus path, not a copied diff) in the implementer brief. Count the Opus reviewer's convention-deviation findings (missing NOT VALID/VALIDATE, missing client_id, cross-slice import, load-mutate-flush). Pass if there are zero such findings across the 3 phases and no exemplar has gone stale. Otherwise drop it.
reviews.reason: Pointing at a real commit costs little. Copied 'golden' diffs go stale and become one more projection to keep honest, so the trial uses pointers rather than copies.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) The harness already has this mechanism. Commit 1ac6b15 (2026-11-04, worktree wizardly-hertz-02c46a, "add the 13 skill packages") carries reference examples as file:line pointers. In .claude/skills/fastapi-alembic-safety/SKILL.md, lines 64-69 hold a precedent table: 0020 NOT VALID+VALIDATE in the same migration; 0032→0033 VALIDATE in a separate deploy after audit_tech_orphans.py; 0044→0045; and the 0046 seed, each with file:line. Line 172 names the audit-script template (backend/scripts/audit_tech_orphans.py:1-9). Lines 135-139 map each upcoming migration phase to its precedent. fixflow-repo-conventions/SKILL.md lines 52-56 name 0044/0045 as the NOT VALID/VALIDATE precedent, and lines 263-264 give the reviewer a grep for it. offline-sync-review/SKILL.md ties every outbox rule to a line in outboxSync.ts. That is the readers' first landing guess ("skills with golden examples: migration, outbox kind, slice"), already done. Both reviewers' "no skill carries an exemplar" was out of date. 2) Worked examples tied to commits already exist for diagnosis. KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN §2.4 R-02 lists eight commit-SHA worked examples, and KS-4 seeds them. 3) The trial cannot measure anything soon. SHIP-PLAN has no phase that adds an outbox kind (grep found none). The first phase with a migration is P6b-1 (line 955), about 20 sessions out. Migrations are Opus-owned (§0 Routing), not handed to a pattern-copying Sonnet, and §0 lines 85-88 plus each phase's text already spell out NOT VALID/VALIDATE. 4) Most of the deviations the trial would count are already CI-gated: a missing alembic pair (`alembic check`) and a cross-slice import (import-linter). With no baseline, a count of "zero findings over 2-3 phases" cannot be told apart from the result without exemplars. 5) What is left is C1678's "hand over a whole earlier diff". It is supported only by anecdote: the co-host's suggestion, "his team does it all the time", and C1141's 5-components-in-5-minutes Storybook demo in a different domain. Under the owner rules that scores as a claim, not evidence.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Check that 1ac6b15's fastapi-alembic-safety, fixflow-repo-conventions and offline-sync-review skills merge to main with their precedent tables intact. If that skills PR is dropped, re-open this as G3-B's trial: put a SHA+path pointer in the brief at P6b-1 and P6b-2, and count the reviewer's NOT VALID/load-mutate-flush deviation findings. Pass = 0.
refutation.reason: Already done: the 13 skills in commit 1ac6b15 cite file:line precedents for migrations and the outbox. The only new part left is handing over a whole earlier diff, which rests on anecdote and has no phase to measure it until about P6b-1.

label: Crystallise repeated procedures into commands or deterministic scripts: move recurring preferences into commands/agents, write the whole process as one command with stop-for-human steps, and have agents bake discoveries into code.
strongest_evidence: anecdotal: monthly investor updates and sales reports half automated (C1394); Riverside browser automation baked into deterministic code (C1396); live create-plan edit (C1726)
sources: No Vibes Allowed: Live Coding with AI Agents (2025-10-16, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zNZs19fIDHk)
AI That Works #45 AI Content Pipeline Revisited (2026-02-17, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U5Gssat8IUw)
sample_quote: "the thing that the agent learns while it's working ... now let's bake that into a deterministic code" (C1396)
landing_guesses: Skills/command files; keeps task-specific rules out of CLAUDE.md | Phase routine as a slash command with human-stop markers | Saved workflows crystallising recurring procedures

reviews.lens: benefit
reviews.existing_mechanism: Partial: ship plan §0 is the routine as prose; ORCHESTRATION §9 plans a FixFlow orchestration skill (CONTEXT block, schemas, routing table); workflow scripts are per-task and unsaved
reviews.measurement: Package the phase routine (§0) as one command/skill with explicit STOP-FOR-OWNER markers and use it for P1 plus the next two phases; from the PR artifacts alone, score each phase on 6 checks (draft PR body starts 'Plan @ <sha>', journal present, reviewer verdict bound to head SHA, fail-before/pass-after per register id, six-question close, OWNER-VIEW refreshed). Pass = 6/6 on all 3 phases with no step re-derived by hand.
reviews.reason: Bears directly on W5 and makes W2's skipped steps visible as missing artifacts. The phase routine is the one procedure certain to repeat 40 times, so it is the right first thing to crystallise.

reviews.lens: Cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is re-opened, what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build, run and keep it honest, and what could go wrong.
reviews.existing_mechanism: ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §9 already plans a project 'FixFlow orchestration skill' (CONTEXT block, schemas, routing table); P1 adds deterministic CI checks (Alembic head, CLAUDE.md paths); the phase routine itself is prose in ship plan §0
reviews.measurement: Run the §0 routine by hand for P1 and P2. If the same open/close steps recur, encode them as one skill or command with explicit stop-for-owner markers and use it for P3 to P5. Count PR bodies or closing messages that miss a §0 element (Plan @ sha, decisions journal, head-SHA-bound verdict, six-question close, OWNER-VIEW refresh). Pass if the skill phases miss none and the hand-run phases missed at least one.
reviews.reason: Writing the routine down as a command before it has ever run (W3) would freeze an untested procedure. Crystallise it only after two hand runs, where it also gives some visible evidence of compliance (W2).

refutation.counter_evidence:
Both reviewers wrote that this was only planned (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §9). It has in fact already been built. Commit 1ac6b15 on branch claude/wizardly-hertz-02c46a, "add the 13 skill packages and 11 agent definitions", contains it:
(1) .claude/skills/fixflow-orchestration/SKILL.md (371 lines). Its description says to use it "at the start of every ship-plan phase session (P0a..P14-fleet)". It encodes §0 as numbered steps: resume via gh pr view and the first unticked box, the Plan @ <sha> line, git diff --stat and the decisions journal. It has explicit stop markers: "An agent running under a brief from this skill stops at every [owner] step and returns" (line 186). That is C1394's "stop and get the human" mechanism, and .claude/skills/README.md convention 4 makes it a rule for every package.
(2) fixflow-repo-conventions/SKILL.md, lines 129-135, and references/pr-body-and-review.md. Together they are a PR-body skeleton carrying all six §0 elements: Plan @ sha, Scope checkboxes, the journal, a reviewer verdict bound to the head SHA with fail-before/pass-after per id, the six-question close, and the OWNER-VIEW refresh.
(3) C1726's "move it into commands/agents" is the 11 .claude/agents/fixflow-*.md definitions, including fixflow-pr-reviewer.
(4) C1396's "bake discoveries into deterministic code" is already the harness's habit. The fixflow-orchestration skill fixes the reusable W1/W2 script contract (stable labels, slices of five, circuit breaker, tail retries). P1 adds deterministic CI checks (the Alembic head, CLAUDE.md paths). Run tools are kept in evidence folders (tools/split-review-input.mjs.txt).
Evidence is weak on every card: all three are anecdotal with no numbers. C1394 is investor updates and sales reports, and C1396 is Riverside browser automation, where the saving comes from not rediscovering a UI. Neither is the same work as code phases that differ each time.
The W2 benefit is illusory. Invoking a skill or command is just as self-reported as following prose, so only the PR artifacts are visible, and §0 already requires those artifacts.
The real cost of what already landed: §0 now exists in two copies, the plan and the skill (cited plan:28-56). Any fix P1's cold-resume trial makes to the plan must also be made in the skill, or the two drift.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: The family is settled as already-done. One check would show whether the existing skills work. Merge 1ac6b15. Then score P1, P2a and P2b-1 from their PR artifacts alone on six §0 checks: body starts Plan @ <sha>; journal present; reviewer verdict names the head SHA; fail-before/pass-after per register id; six-question close; OWNER-VIEW.md refreshed. Pass = 6/6 on all three phases. Separately, after P1's cold-resume trial, diff SHIP-PLAN §0 against fixflow-orchestration's §0 steps; pass = no drift. Any miss is fixed in those two skills, not by building a new command.
refutation.reason: The proposal is already built: the uncommitted-to-main skill commit 1ac6b15 encodes the §0 phase routine with [owner] stop markers, a PR-body skeleton and 11 agent definitions. The cards are anecdotal and carry no numbers, and the W2 gain is illusory, so nothing new remains to adopt or trial.

reviews.reason: Agents already get explicit context. The skill authors adding the 13 packages need only one line: take the phase id as an argument and never infer it.

refutation.counter_evidence: C1441 is a single asserted remark about HumanLayer's own tool, not Claude Code. A Claude Code skill loads into the session that already holds the owner's opening message, so the phase is visible to it without any hidden injection. Of the 13 packages in worktrees/wizardly-hertz-02c46a/.claude/skills/, 12 are domain-knowledge skills (android-background-execution, odoo-accounting-import and the like). None of them depends on the phase, and none uses $ARGUMENTS (grep returned no hits). That makes "every skill takes the phase id" a ceremony for 12 of the 13. Subagents and agents already get explicit context: ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §5.1 prepends the CONTEXT block, and .claude/agents/fixflow-pr-reviewer.md:3 is given the PR number and register ids. G3-A's premise is partly wrong: the §5.1 block carries today, settled and apkCommit but has no phase field. Echoing an id in a skill's first output line is self-report, so it adds nothing on W2. One real gap remains: fixflow-orchestration/SKILL.md:190 says "Find the phase in the checklist (168-215)" without saying where the phase id comes from. Ship plan §0 (plan:26-29) allows a mobile, web or ops phase to run alongside a backend phase, and desktop worktree branch names (claude/<adjective>-<name>) do not name the phase. So "first unticked phase" is ambiguous, and repo state cannot recover the id.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Settled as a one-line edit. To show it worked: over the next 5 phase sessions (P0a onward), count the sessions whose first gate statement and draft-PR or W0-results "Plan @" header name a phase different from the one in the owner's opening message. Pass: 0. Also count the sessions opened without a named phase that picked one themselves instead of asking. Pass: 0.
refutation.reason: A smaller version survives, adopted as one line in fixflow-orchestration SKILL.md session-start step 1 and nowhere else: the phase id comes from the owner's opening message or the skill args, it is never inferred from the checklist, and if it is missing the session asks. Plan §0 allows concurrent phases and branch names do not name phases. The rest of the idea is dropped: no convention across all 13 skills, no echoed id, and no claim on W2.

reviews.lens: benefit

reviews.lens: Cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is re-opened, what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build, run and keep it honest, and what could go wrong.
reviews.existing_mechanism: Partly: the harness review's skip-by-default posture; §9 ties each wanted skill to named agents. No written rule governs when a workflow or skill gets saved, and 13 skills are being added up front
reviews.measurement: Each saved workflow or skill names in its header the recurrence (two dated uses) or the recorded agent failure it answers. At P10, count saved items with no recorded use since saving and prune them. It worked if the library holds only items with at least one use.
reviews.reason: A rule that costs nothing and answers W5 directly: save a script only on its second recurrence or after a logged failure. It also gives the 13 incoming skills a pruning test.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The evidence is thin. All three cards are anecdote or assertion with no numbers: C0908 is a "general product-development argument", C1256 is "author's retrospective; no numbers", and C1771 has "no data". (2) The W4 premise in both reviews is wrong. They treat the 13 incoming skills as the "dozens just in case" failure. In fact they are exactly the 13 rows of ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §9 (lines 722-736), and each row names the agents or sessions it lifts (S-01a/b, O-01, R-02, O-07, the APK and verification sessions). .claude/skills/README.md also requires FixFlow claims cited path:line plus an UPSTREAM.md provenance file for each package. They were aimed at known needs, not installed speculatively. (3) The harness already works this way for rules and hooks. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md §4 (lines 254-289) skips the pre-commit hook, the context system, the doctor script and M00-M06 because none was proven. It also carries lessons from recorded failures (RT-02..RT-06, state loss 093b793, G2's lost skeptic budget) into the plan. (4) Workflows are partly covered already. The parts that recur (the CONTEXT block, the schemas, the tier/routing table, §3-§5) are already written down, and the §9 'FixFlow orchestration skill (written here)' row (line 735) turns them into a skill. Only the per-task script itself is not saved. (5) Both reviewers' pruning tests are defective. A count at P5 (G3-A) or P10 (G3-B) would prune skills for phases that have not run yet: Odoo (R-02/O-07), Pakistan accounting (O-07), Maestro (verification sessions), EAS (APK sessions). (6) The harness has no hooks (W2), so the only objective way to count skill use is to grep the transcripts. A self-reported count does not settle anything.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: For the narrowed adopt, it worked if all of the following hold at P10. (a) Every saved workflow file under the chosen folder has a header that names at least 2 dated prior phase uses, or a recorded failure id. (b) Each saved workflow has been reused at least once since it was saved, counted by grepping its name in the PR bodies and in the session transcripts (~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl). (c) Over P1-P10, the number of times a saved shape was re-authored from scratch is 0. (d) Take each skill whose §9-named phases have all closed. A transcript grep for a Skill tool_use with its name, or for subagent_type/agentType set to its distilled agent, shows at least 1 load, or the skill has been flagged for pruning in that phase's closing message. It fails if any saved workflow is never reused, or any closed-phase skill has 0 loads and was not flagged.
refutation.reason: Survives only in a smaller form. First, a written save rule: a Workflow script is kept only after its shape has run in a second phase or answers a recorded failure, and its header names those uses. Second, a retire check for each skill, run at the close of the phases §9 names for it and based on a transcript grep. The 13 skills are not reopened, and neither reviewer's calendar-based P5/P10 prune is adopted, because the harness already has the failure-driven posture and the anecdotal evidence cannot carry more than this.

label: Question/Research split: one context generates questions from the ticket, then a fresh context that never sees the goal answers them, done deterministically.
strongest_evidence: asserted: described as a trivial query-planning analogue, no results (C1325)
sources: Everything We Got Wrong About RPI (2026-03-03, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YwZR6tc7qYg)
sample_quote: "we just hide the ticket from the context window that's doing research" (C1325)
landing_guesses: Workflow script (questions agent then blind researcher); fixflow-explorer usage

reviews.lens: benefit
reviews.existing_mechanism: Partial: fresh-context refuters and the P1 cold-resume trial use blinding, but discovery/research agents (fixflow-explorer, Sonnet mappers) see the goal
reviews.measurement: In one phase's discovery step, run two arms on the same generated question list: arm A answers with the ticket/goal visible, arm B with it hidden. An Opus refuter (blind to arm) checks every claim. Pass = arm B has fewer REFUTED or uncited claims and misses no fact that arm A found (judged against the phase's eventual diff).
reviews.reason: Hiding the goal from researchers is new here and targets confirmation-biased discovery, which the refuters only catch afterwards. It is one bounded A/B in a single phase.

reviews.lens: Cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is re-opened, what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build, run and keep it honest, and what could go wrong.
reviews.existing_mechanism: Partly: fresh-context refuters with default-refuted verdicts and the Haiku locator; but mapper briefs (S-0x) include the goal, so researchers can steer toward it
reviews.measurement: On one upcoming mapping question, run the normal Sonnet mapper beside a questions-agent then blind-researcher pair (the researcher never sees the goal) over the same scope. Count facts that pass the citation check, and facts Fable marks as goal-steered or unsupported. Adopt as a saved workflow if the blind pair yields at least as many verified facts, with fewer unsupported ones, at no more than 1.5x the tokens.
reviews.reason: This is a debiasing step the harness lacks, and it costs one extra agent per question. The evidence is asserted, so test it once before saving it.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) The harness already has two of the idea's three parts. The question step exists: S-01b in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md §4.2 is a Sonnet mapper that answers "a fixed question list" written by the orchestrator. The facts-only research step exists: the §5.1 CONTEXT block says "Return constants, lines and declared names; never a severity or a verdict". §5.3 says "Mappers return constants, lines and names; the hypotheses tag routes, it does not judge". §6 calls discovery "judgement-free and schema-bounded". Blinding is applied where the harness judged it pays: §4.6 skeptics get "the claim, its evidence and its failing condition only". (2) The only missing part is hiding the goal, and it has nowhere to land. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md Q3 (line 47), a ruling the owner accepted, says "discovery is the phase this program has finished". The phase routine in SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md §0 (lines 24-116) has no mapping or research step: brief, implement, Opus reviewer, gates, close. So both reviewers' trials ("one upcoming mapping question", "one phase's discovery step") assume a step the 40-phase plan does not contain. (3) Blinding can make things worse here: §4.3 caps mappers at 40 facts. A researcher that cannot see the goal still has to pick which facts to report under that cap, and the goal is the only thing that tells it what is relevant. (4) The only evidence is C1325: asserted, "no results given". Under the owner's rules that is a claim, not evidence. (5) Both proposed measurements fail as a test. Each is one A/B with no repeats, and LLM run-to-run variance alone can decide the result. G3-B's metric depends on Fable labelling facts "goal-steered", which is subjective. G3-A judges against the phase's eventual diff, which the arm outputs themselves influence.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Take the W1 citation-check outputs and the G1 adjudications under docs/program/evidence/. Count mapper facts that a later analyst, skeptic or gate showed were omitted, slanted toward a hypothesis, or uncited. If fewer than 3 of the roughly 16 W1 tasks show one, the bias this idea targets did not occur in this harness, so the skip stands. If 3 or more do, and a new discovery round is actually scheduled, run the blind and non-blind arms on the same question list, 3 repeats each. Pass if the blind arm's REFUTED or uncited rate is at least 30% lower and its recall of the facts the analysts later used is no lower.
refutation.reason: The harness already writes question lists in the orchestrator and limits researchers to facts with no verdicts (ORCHESTRATION §4.2 S-01b, §5.1, §5.3, §6). The only new part is hiding the goal, and it has no step to attach to, because discovery is finished (HARNESS-REVIEW Q3) and the ship plan §0 phases have no research step. The evidence is asserted only.

sample_quote: "Read the spec markdown file" (C1346)
landing_guesses: Bundle templates/scripts with a skill (e.g. owner one-page view generator)

reviews.lens: benefit
reviews.existing_mechanism: Skill packages natively support bundled files; OWNER-VIEW.md is refreshed by hand at each phase close
reviews.measurement: Bundle a template + fill script with the phase-close skill so OWNER-VIEW.md is generated from the PR state; over 3 phase closes, count fields the owner or reviewer has to correct by hand. Pass = 0 corrections and the refresh is never skipped.
reviews.reason: OWNER-VIEW is refreshed 40 times in a fixed format, which makes it the one artifact that justifies a bundled template. Its benefit is small but cheap to test alongside F104.

reviews.lens: Cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is re-opened, what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build, run and keep it honest, and what could go wrong.
reviews.existing_mechanism: Claude Code skills natively bundle files beside SKILL.md; OWNER-VIEW.md is refreshed by hand at phase close
reviews.reason: No artifact is produced often enough yet to justify a generator script that would need its own upkeep. If OWNER-VIEW refreshes recur, the F117 rule decides.

refutation.counter_evidence:
The evidence is thin. The only source is C1346 (G3-cards.md:1523-1529): a slides skill's file layout, graded "asserted" with "no data". It reports no measured gain, and the artifact it makes is HTML slides, which FixFlow never produces.

The template half is already done. The skill packages being added (.claude/worktrees/wizardly-hertz-02c46a/.claude/skills/) already keep templates and example skeletons in references/ beside SKILL.md. Examples: fixflow-repo-conventions/references/pr-body-and-review.md ("Body skeleton (first commit, draft PR)"), fixflow-orchestration/references/{w1-script-skeleton,output-schemas,context-block}.md, eas-expo-release/references/fixflow-build-receipt.md and android-field-debugging/references/fixflow-capture-sheet.md. Phase close (refreshing OWNER-VIEW) is already a written step in fixflow-repo-conventions/SKILL.md:234 and fixflow-orchestration/SKILL.md:302. So the family adds nothing for W4 except the build script.

No artifact needs that script. The trial's target, OWNER-VIEW.md (92 lines on PR #182), is mostly judgment prose: "Where we are", a "What only you can do next" list that is specific to each phase, "The rules that never bend (plain words)" and a hand-drawn mermaid order of work. Its own header says "This page explains; the plan decides." Only the 3-row status table could be filled mechanically. Even that table has no machine-readable source today: phase state lives in draft-PR checkboxes, W0-results step tables and git (ship plan §0 Resume, lines 31-46).

A generator would therefore add another projection that has to track the plan's roughly 40 phases. That is the drift risk the overhead-skeptic raised against OWNER-VIEW itself (HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md:267). The page was accepted only because the refresh is tied to the phase-close routine, which already exists.

G3-A's measurement ("count hand corrections over 3 closes") has no baseline either. The routine has never run (W3), so no refresh has yet been missed or mis-filled.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: The skip stands for now. Reopen it only on this trigger: after the first 3 phase closes, compare the OWNER-VIEW status table with `gh pr list --state merged` for the phase branches. If any close skipped the refresh, or any row disagrees with the merged PRs, a status-table-only fill script is worth a trial. The prose sections stay hand-written either way.
refutation.reason: Putting templates beside SKILL.md is already standard in the new skill packages (references/ skeletons). The only new part is a deterministic build script, and no harness artifact needs one: OWNER-VIEW is mostly judgment prose with no machine-readable state source, so a script would add drift and upkeep to fix a problem nobody has seen yet.

label: Wrap every verification command (tests, lint, typecheck) in a silent runner that prints one success line and the full output only on failure, with a VERBOSE=1 opt-out.
strongest_evidence: anecdotal/asserted: ~48-line run-silent.ts and ~150-line run_silent.sh in the repo; quality, test and typecheck scripts all route through it (C0235, C0101); 'thousands of warnings' avoided is asserted, not counted (C0184).
sample_quote: "Run command silently, show output only on failure" (C0070)
landing_guesses: scripts/ wrapper around pytest, ruff, mypy, npm test named in CLAUDE.md | one wrapper plus one success string per verifier command in the phase routine

reviews.lens: benefit
reviews.measurement: Wrap backend/web/mobile gate commands in one Git Bash script (full output only on failure, VERBOSE=1 opt-out); over the next 2 code phases count gate-output tokens in the phase transcript vs the P1 baseline and count failures the agent misread; pass = at least 70% fewer gate-output tokens and zero missed or misread failures.
reviews.reason: Gate output is the biggest self-inflicted context cost on a one-phase-per-session plan; a 50-line wrapper is cheap, and CI keeps the full logs.

reviews.lens: cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is reopened, and what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build, run and keep it honest
reviews.existing_mechanism: ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §3 tier guide: Sonnet runs the gates and reports in a JSON schema, so raw gate output never reaches the Fable context
reviews.reason: Gate output already lands in a schema-bound Sonnet subagent. A bash plus PowerShell wrapper would only save subagent tokens, and it risks hiding warnings.

refutation.counter_evidence:
1. The mechanism already exists for the noisiest gates. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN Appendix A (lines 630-666) is the backend gate recipe, and SHIP-PLAN §0 "Gates" (lines 57-60) makes every backend phase use it. Its g() function already does what run_silent does: it sends each gate's output to its own log file (`"$@" > /work/logs/gate-$i.log 2>&1`) and prints one `GATE[i cmd] EXIT=rc` line per gate. The agent reports only those lines plus the tail of each failing gate's log, and the full logs stay on disk, which serves the same purpose as VERBOSE=1. That covers ruff, mypy, lint-imports, alembic, pytest and pip-audit.
2. There is already a general output rule. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §4.3 (line 217) says command agents redirect npm, pytest and docker output to scratchpad logs and return tails plus exit codes. The COMMANDS schema in §5.2 (lines 456-457) has exit_code, summary and tail fields.
3. The main session never sees gate output. SHIP-PLAN §0 (line 55) and ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §3 (line 98) say Fable never implements, and §3 (line 96) gives running and reporting gates to Sonnet. So the L2 benefit would land only in short-lived subagents.
4. G4-A's claim that gate output is the biggest context cost has no support. HARNESS-REVIEW §6 (line 316) measured 68% tool results in a Fable session, and Fable runs no gates. G4-A's 70% target is also measured against a P1 baseline that does not exist yet (W3), and P1's backend gates already run through Appendix A, so that baseline is already quiet.
5. A wrapper that is silent on success clashes with two existing rules. The §0 closing message must report "what evidence ran (incl. skipped counts)", and P1's skip-aware gate (SHIP-PLAN lines 361-364) uses `pytest -rs` output. Appendix A keeps both by holding the logs on disk.
6. The upstream evidence is anecdotal. C0184 only asserts "thousands of warnings", and that problem comes from oxlint's no-explicit-any warnings.
7. Native web and mobile gates are the only gap. §0 says they "run natively" but gives no output rule. Their commands are `eslint .`, `prettier --check .`, `vitest run`, `vite build`, `tsc --noEmit` and `jest` (package.json lines 12-19; technician-app/package.json lines 10-11). tsc and eslint print nothing on success when there are no warnings, prettier prints about one line, and vitest and jest print about one line per test file. Covering that gap means copying the §4.3 rule into §0, not adopting a new wrapper.
8. One correction to G4-B: its "bash plus PowerShell" cost is overstated, because a Node .mjs runner would work on all three shells. This does not change the verdict.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: The one open question is native web and mobile gate output. Check it before the first web or mobile phase (P2a). Run once with output to a file: `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `npm run build` at the repo root, then `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in technician-app. Count the characters of each successful run (`wc -c`). If any single gate prints more than about 8,000 characters on success, add one line to SHIP-PLAN §0: native gates follow ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN §4.3's output rule (log to scratchpad, report exit code plus failing tail). Otherwise do nothing. Neither outcome needs a run_silent script.
refutation.reason: The harness already does this. Backend gates run through Appendix A's per-gate logs and GATE EXIT lines, §4.3 sets an output rule for command agents, and Fable never runs gates. A wrapper silent on success would also hide skip counts that the §0 closing message and P1's skip-aware gate need. The only gap is native web and mobile output, which a one-line §0 rule would cover if measurement shows it is large.

label: The quiet wrapper should still print the test count so that a pass with zero tests run is visible to the agent.

refutation.counter_evidence: In this repo a run with zero tests already fails, and the skip case is already printed and gated. (1) backend/pyproject.toml:59 sets addopts "-ra --strict-markers", so every pytest run already prints the skip summary with reasons. pytest exits with code 5 when it collects nothing. (2) vitest.config.js sets no passWithNoTests, so `vitest run` (package.json:16) exits 1 when it finds no test files. (3) technician-app/package.json:11 runs plain `jest`, which exits 1 when it finds no tests. Only ci.yml:71 adds `--passWithNoTests`, and P1 removes it (SHIP-PLAN lines 361-365). (4) The case this repo actually has is that conftest.py:65-72 skips every @integration test when FIXFLOW_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset. P1's skip-aware gate already makes that fatal (pytest -rs --junitxml, failing on any skipped @integration test, mirrored in ci.yml). Reviewer A's proposed measurement ("an empty run with FIXFLOW_TEST_DATABASE_URL unset shows a non-green line") tests exactly what P1 already delivers. (5) Plan §0 (line 45) already requires the closing message to report "evidence incl. skipped counts". Any wrapper that hid the counts would break an existing rule, so the constraint is already in the routine. (6) The family only matters if F001 is adopted, and the harness has no quiet wrapper today. The source is anecdotal: a shell function that greps the output, with no measurement, and the reader saw only about 60 of 150 lines. The one gap left is ad-hoc name-filtered runs (jest -t, vitest -t), which can exit 0 with every test skipped. Those are not the gate commands a wrapper would wrap.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: I took the exit codes from each runner's documented defaults; I did not run them here. To confirm, run three commands and check each exit status: `cd backend && pytest -k __nomatch__; echo $?` should give 5; `npx vitest run __nomatch__; echo $?` at the repo root should give 1; `cd technician-app && npx jest __nomatch__; echo $?` should give 1. If any of them exits 0, a count line in a wrapper would earn its place for that runner only.
refutation.reason: This repo already turns a zero-test run into a failure (pytest exits 5; vitest and plain jest exit 1; P1 removes --passWithNoTests). Skips are already printed (-ra) and fatal (P1's skip gate), and plan §0 already requires skipped counts at phase close, so a count-printing wrapper adds nothing.

label: Tell the agent to run the full test command once and filter the spooled output afterwards, never piping test commands to head/tail/grep and never re-running long tests just to change a grep.
strongest_evidence: asserted: rule in humanlayer AGENTS.md, relies on Bash tool output spooling (C0077).
sample_quote: "you must NEVER pipe the output of test commands to head/tail/grep/etc" (C0077)
landing_guesses: CLAUDE.md commands section | phase-routine verification step

reviews.lens: benefit

reviews.lens: cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is reopened, and what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build, run and keep it honest
reviews.measurement: Gate-runner subagent transcripts show no test command piped to head/tail/grep, and no rerun only to change a filter, across one phase
reviews.reason: Costs one line in the gate-runner brief or the §5.1 CONTEXT block, not in CLAUDE.md. It stops truncated failures and repeated long Docker test runs.

refutation.counter_evidence: The harness already has this rule for the long test runs, which is where the claimed benefit lives. ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md:217-218 ("Output discipline: command agents redirect npm/pytest/docker output to scratchpad logs and return tails + exit codes"). Lines 619-622 ("redirect output to scratchpad logs ... never re-issue a mutating command", plus fixed container names, so a second gate start fails on a name conflict and a second pytest cannot run). Appendix A, lines 630-664: each gate writes its full output to gate-$i.log, the agent greps only the spooled gates.log, and a timeout means "run docker wait again, NEVER a second docker run". Ship plan §0 line 57 makes Appendix A the backend gate for every phase. That covers both of reviewer B's targets: rerunning the long Docker tests is mechanically blocked, and failures are not truncated because full logs stay on disk with each failing gate's tail reported. B's proposed measurement ("gate-runner transcripts show no piped test command") is therefore already guaranteed by the fixed script. Transfer: card C0077 is evidence class 'asserted', a rule in an agent file with no numbers, so it is anecdotal under the owner rules. It also depends on the Bash tool spooling long output to a file, which this environment does not promise; the PowerShell tool says output over 30000 chars "will be truncated". The explicit redirect to a log file that the harness already uses is the version that carries over. Reviewer A's suggested home, CLAUDE.md's commands section, contains no pipes today, and a new rule there would make W1 worse.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Only the native web and mobile test runs (vitest/jest) are outside Appendix A, and those are short. At the first code phase, grep the phase's subagent transcripts for a test command (npm test | npx vitest | jest | pytest) piped to head, tail or grep, and for the same test command run twice where only the filter changed. If either happens even once and hides a failure or costs more than 60s, add one sentence to the implementer brief template, never to CLAUDE.md. If it never happens, close the question.
refutation.reason: Narrowed. The useful part, running long tests once into a log and filtering the log, is already in Appendix A and the command-agent rules (design :217, :619-622). The only gap left is the short native web/mobile test runs. At most that is one sentence in a brief, added only if the transcript check shows the problem; it does not belong in CLAUDE.md.

sources: HN thread: Why Software Factories Fail (2026-07-23, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49023019)
sample_quote: "they don't update their agent's memory, they don't update their prompts or their skills, they actually just go build another linter" (C0542)
landing_guesses: bare-catch and load-mutate-flush as ruff/ESLint custom rules | CLAUDE.md invariants become import-linter contracts

reviews.lens: benefit

reviews.reason: This is the strongest lever on W1 and W2 together: every invariant made mechanical is prose that can leave CLAUDE.md and a check nobody self-reports.

reviews.lens: cost, risk and novelty: what the harness already does, whether a deliberate skip is reopened, and what a one-developer Windows setup pays to build, run and keep it honest
reviews.existing_mechanism: import-linter contracts, ESLint no-restricted-imports, dependency-cruiser planned P5b-2 (HARNESS-REVIEW §5)
reviews.measurement: Write one ast-grep (or ESLint) rule for the bare-catch / catch{return;} shape that CLAUDE.md names in completionPrefill, and run it once on main over technician-app/src. Adopt into CI only if the owner judges at least 1 hit a real defect-shape instance and false positives are no more than 20% of hits. ast-grep is a new dependency, so that step needs an owner decision.
reviews.reason: Boundary rules exist, but no rules exist for defect shapes. One bounded rule tests whether rules beat invariant prose, which bears on W1.

refutation.counter_evidence: (1) None of the evidence is measured. C0128 lists only the names of HumanLayer's rule test files (the rule code was not read). C0312 is a Commands section. C0542 is relayed from an unnamed attendee. C0774 is one HN commenter. C0321 is a chapter title with no answer. The same episode (C0543) argues that a cheap model reading a rule list is "nearly as good" as a linter. The HumanLayer rules are generic TypeScript style rules (max-ternary-depth, no-object-parameters), not domain invariants. (2) The premise that FixFlow's recurring defect shapes can be caught by syntax does not hold. All seven shapes in docs/HANDOFF-2026-07-28-open-work.md §6 are process or semantic problems: tests that pin broken behaviour, mocks that hide FKs, fixture defaults, docstrings that overclaim, scope exclusions, unvisited callers, guards never generalised. Most CLAUDE.md invariants are the same kind (bill freeze, monotonic wizard state, "unknown is not none", the dispatcher cursor, the lock that is deliberately kept), and they are already pinned by pytest and Jest pure-function tests. (3) G4-B's bare-catch trial fails its own gate today. A grep finds 3 empty catches in technician-app/src (ArrivalJobStep2.tsx:142, :163; CreateJobStep2.tsx:158). All are best-effort audio-player swallows, so 100% would be false positives. The one real instance (completionPrefill.ts) is already fixed, and its defect ("offline" read as "no completion") cannot be seen in the syntax. (4) Parts of this already exist. The web eslint.config.js uses js.configs.recommended, which includes no-empty, and the web tree has 0 empty catches. Slice boundaries are enforced by import-linter and ESLint, model/migration drift by alembic check, and the head number by the P1 CI check. "Never fetch a write from a screen" is already adopted as the dependency-cruiser rule in P5b-2 (HARNESS-REVIEW §5 Q3). (5) Mobile has no ESLint, so any mobile ESLint or ast-grep rule means new dependencies. (6) W2 is about whether the phase routine is followed, not about code invariants, so lint rules do nothing for it. The W1 gain is a few lines out of 390.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run two checks. (a) The compare_digest rule: add ruff's built-in flake8-tidy-imports banned-api (TID251) for hmac.compare_digest, with a per-file ignore for backend/app/core/security.py. This needs no new dependency, because ruff already runs in CI. It passes if three things hold. First, a seeded hmac.compare_digest call in a feature module fails `ruff check` in the CI backend job. Second, the one current hit, backend/app/features/identity/security.py:44, is resolved: either switched to compare_secret, or given a noqa whose reason the owner accepts. Third, main has 0 remaining hits, and the compare_secret paragraph in CLAUDE.md shrinks to one line that points at pyproject. (b) Whether a rule per defect shape is worth it: across the next 10 phase PRs, have the per-PR Opus reviewer tag each confirmed defect as either expressible with an existing linter's built-in config (ruff banned-api or select, ESLint no-restricted-syntax or no-restricted-imports, import-linter, dependency-cruiser, with no custom plugin and no new dependency) or not. Adopt a standing "one rule per recurring shape" convention only if at least 2 confirmed defects are expressible, and each resulting rule fails its seeded violation with 0 false positives on main. Otherwise drop it.
refutation.reason: Narrowed. The broad family fails: its evidence is unmeasured, FixFlow's recorded recurring defect shapes (HANDOFF §6) and most CLAUDE.md invariants are semantic and already covered by tests, the proposed bare-catch rule would flag only 3 false positives today, the web already has no-empty, and the outbox import rule is already planned for P5b-2. What survives is one zero-dependency rule (ruff TID251 banning hmac.compare_digest outside core/security.py) plus a 10-PR count of how many confirmed defects an existing linter could express. The W1 gain is a few lines and the W2 gain is none.

reviews.existing_mechanism: Per-PR Opus review only; no scheduled slow-loop audit
reviews.measurement: After about 10 merged phases, run one Opus architecture-drift audit over the diff since the plan start. Count actionable findings (a new cross-slice edge, a duplicated helper or source of truth, a file grown past 1.5k lines) that no per-PR reviewer flagged. Schedule it every 10 phases only if it produces 2 or more.
reviews.reason: Per-PR review cannot see cumulative drift. One bounded audit costs a single session and decides whether a slow loop earns its place.

refutation.counter_evidence: 1) Evidence is 0. All four cards (C0353, C0597, C0770, C0841) are asserted conceptual argument, and C0597 borrows the phrase from Osmani. The same source (C0843) says models are unreliable judges of code quality, so an Opus design audit is itself not an oracle. It is only another proxy. 2) Part of the mechanism already exists. Cross-slice edges already have a fast oracle: import-linter contracts in backend/pyproject.toml and ESLint no-restricted-imports (CLAUDE.md, "Respect slice boundaries"), plus dependency-cruiser on mobile (SHIP-PLAN P5b-2, around line 860). That makes G4-B's "new cross-slice edge" count double-count CI. HARNESS-REVIEW §1 Q2 and §2 record a one-time four-lens architecture panel, which was a slow-loop design review already held at plan start. 3) G4-B's "file grown past 1.5k lines" fires at baseline: backend/app/features/jobs/service.py is 1958 lines and attendance/service.py is 1932 lines today. 4) G4-A's pass bar (>=1 issue no PR reviewer raised) does not discriminate. The per-PR Opus brief (SHIP-PLAN §0 Routing) is scoped to register ids, not design, so "not raised" is close to automatic. An Opus sweep of about 10 PRs on a 56k-line repo will almost always find one duplicated helper. 5) The W2 link is illusory. A code-design audit says nothing about whether the phase routine ran. 6) No skip is reopened. The graphify/call-graph skip is about tooling; this audit needs only git diff and grep.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Run one fresh-context Opus audit after the 10th merged code PR or immediately before P9a-1 (the new accounting slice), whichever comes first. Scope it to git diff <P1 merge sha>..main. Count only cumulative-drift findings that meet all of these: (a) not visible inside any single PR diff, for example the same helper or rule reimplemented across two or more PRs, a second source of truth for a value, or one file grown by more than 300 lines across two or more PRs (the delta, not the absolute size); (b) not caught by import-linter, ESLint or dependency-cruiser; (c) not present at the P1 sha. Each finding must survive a fresh default-refuted refuter. Pass = 2 or more refuter-confirmed findings that the owner accepts as plan fix items. Then run it once more before program close; do not schedule it every 10 phases. 0 or 1 = drop the slow loop. Record the session's token and wall-clock cost beside the count.
refutation.reason: Per-PR review is scoped to register ids and cannot see drift that builds up across PRs, so one audit as a trial survives. But it must exclude boundary edges (CI already catches them) and the two pre-existing ~1.95k-line service files. It also needs a refuter-gated pass bar of 2 or more owner-accepted findings, because both reviewers' bars pass trivially.
